TRANSACTION PROPOSED—YOUR VOTE IS VERY IMPORTANT

 

Dear Stockholders of Iridium Communications Inc.:

 

On June 28, 2026, Iridium Communications Inc., a Delaware corporation (“Iridium”), entered into an Agreement and Plan of Merger (the “Merger Agreement”) with Rocket Lab Corporation, a Delaware corporation (“Rocket Lab”), Ion Merger Sub I, Inc., a Delaware corporation and an indirect wholly owned subsidiary of Rocket Lab (“Merger Sub I”), and Ion Merger Sub II, LLC, a Delaware limited liability company and an indirect wholly owned subsidiary of Rocket Lab (“Merger Sub II”). Pursuant to the Merger Agreement, and subject to the satisfaction or waiver of the conditions set forth therein, Merger Sub I will merge with and into Iridium, with Iridium continuing as the surviving corporation and an indirect wholly owned subsidiary of Rocket Lab (the “First Merger,” and the time at which the First Merger becomes effective, the “First Effective Time”), and (a) if the Second Merger Condition (as defined below) is satisfied, immediately following the First Effective Time, or (b) if the Equity Threshold Condition (as defined below) (but not the Second Merger Condition) is satisfied, on the second trading day following the First Effective Time, the surviving corporation in the First Merger will merge with and into Merger Sub II, with Merger Sub II continuing as the surviving entity (the “Second Merger” and, together with the First Merger, the “Mergers”). The Mergers are generally intended to qualify as a tax-free reorganization for U.S. federal income tax purposes so long as the value of the Stock Consideration relative to the Cash Consideration (each as defined below) received by the holders of Iridium Common Stock, par value $0.001 per share (“Iridium Common Stock”) (which could vary depending on the price per share of Rocket Lab Common Stock, par value $0.0001 per share, of Rocket Lab (“Rocket Lab Common Stock”) at the First Effective Time) meets the conditions for tax-free treatment. Should those conditions not be met, the Mergers will not be treated as a tax-free reorganization for U.S. federal income tax purposes. The Iridium board of directors (the “Iridium Board”) has unanimously approved the Merger Agreement and recommends that Iridium stockholders vote in favor of adopting the Merger Agreement.

 

As a result of the Mergers, at the First Effective Time, each outstanding share of Iridium Common Stock, other than as specified in the Merger Agreement, will be converted into the right to receive (i) $27.00 in cash (the “Cash Consideration”) and (ii) a number of shares (the “Stock Consideration” and, together with the Cash Consideration, the “Merger Consideration”) of Rocket Lab Common Stock equal to the Exchange Ratio, in each case without interest. The “Exchange Ratio” will be the following: (i) if the Rocket Lab Stock Price (as defined below) is equal to or less than $67.50, then the Exchange Ratio will be 0.4000; (ii) if the Rocket Lab Stock Price is greater than $67.50 but less than $112.50, then the Exchange Ratio will be the quotient obtained by dividing $27.00 by the Rocket Lab Stock Price, rounded to four decimal places; and (iii) if the Rocket Lab Stock Price is equal to or greater than $112.50, then the Exchange Ratio will be 0.2400. “Rocket Lab Stock Price” means the volume weighted average price per share of Rocket Lab Common Stock on the Nasdaq Global Select Market (“Nasdaq”) for the period of the ten consecutive trading days ending on and including the second full trading day prior to the First Effective Time. If the First Merger is consummated, Iridium Common Stock will be delisted from Nasdaq and deregistered under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, as amended, as promptly as practicable after the consummation of the First Merger.

 

 

 

 

The value of the Merger Consideration will fluctuate with the market value of Rocket Lab Common Stock until the transaction is complete. The Iridium Common Stock is listed on Nasdaq under the symbol “IRDM,” and the Rocket Lab Common Stock is listed on Nasdaq under the symbol “RKLB.”

 

The Mergers cannot be completed without approval of the proposal to adopt the Merger Agreement by the affirmative vote of holders of a majority of the outstanding shares of Iridium Common Stock entitled to vote thereon. Because of this, Iridium is holding a special meeting of its stockholders on September 24, 2026, to vote on the proposal necessary to complete the Mergers. Information about the meeting, the Mergers, the Merger Agreement and the other business to be considered by stockholders at the special meeting is contained in this proxy statement/prospectus. The Iridium Board has fixed the close of business on August 21, 2026, as the record date for the determination of Iridium stockholders entitled to notice of, and to vote at, the special meeting. Any stockholder entitled to attend and vote at the special meeting is entitled to appoint a proxy to attend and vote on such stockholder’s behalf. Such proxy need not be a holder of Iridium Common Stock. We urge you to read this proxy statement/prospectus and the annexes and documents incorporated by reference carefully. You should also carefully consider the risks that are described in the “Risk Factors” section beginning on page 23.

 

The Iridium Board has unanimously determined that the Merger Agreement and the transactions contemplated thereby, including the Mergers, are fair to and in the best interests of Iridium and its stockholders, approved and declared advisable the Merger Agreement and the transactions contemplated thereby, including the Mergers, and directed that the Merger Agreement be submitted to the Iridium stockholders for adoption at a meeting of such stockholders, and unanimously recommends that Iridium stockholders vote “FOR” the proposal to approve and adopt the Merger Agreement and the transactions contemplated thereby, including the Mergers.

 

Your vote is very important regardless of the number of shares of Iridium Common Stock that you own.

 

Whether or not you plan to attend the special meeting, please submit your proxy as soon as possible by following the instructions on the accompanying proxy card to make sure that your shares are represented at the meeting. If your shares are held in the name of a broker, bank or other nominee, please follow the instructions on the voting instruction form furnished by the broker, bank or other nominee. You must provide voting instructions by filling out the voting instruction form in order for your shares to be voted.

 

The special meeting will be held in a virtual meeting format only. You will not be able to attend the special meeting physically in person.

 

Thank you for your continued support, interest and investment in Iridium.

 

Very truly yours,

 

 

 

Matthew J. Desch
Chief Executive Officer 

Neither the Securities and Exchange Commission nor any state securities commission has approved or disapproved of the Mergers or the other transactions described in this proxy statement/prospectus or the securities to be issued in connection with the Mergers or determined if this proxy statement/prospectus is accurate or complete. Any representation to the contrary is a criminal offense.

 

This proxy statement/prospectus is dated August 26, 2026, and is first being mailed to stockholders of Iridium on or about August 26, 2026.

NOTICE OF SPECIAL MEETING OF IRIDIUM STOCKHOLDERS

 

To be held on September 24, 2026

  

To the Stockholders of Iridium Communications Inc.:

 

We are pleased to invite you to attend the special meeting of stockholders of Iridium Communications Inc., a Delaware corporation (“Iridium”), which will be held at 8:30 a.m. Eastern Time on September 24, 2026, virtually at http://www.virtualshareholdermeeting.com/IRDM2026SM, for the following purposes:

 

·to vote on a proposal to adopt the Agreement and Plan of Merger, dated as of June 28, 2026, among Rocket Lab Corporation, a Delaware corporation (“Rocket Lab”), Ion Merger Sub I, Inc., a Delaware corporation and an indirect wholly owned subsidiary of Rocket Lab, Ion Merger Sub II, LLC, a Delaware limited liability company and an indirect wholly owned subsidiary of Rocket Lab, and Iridium (as it may be amended from time to time, the “Merger Agreement”), which is further described in the sections titled “The Mergers” and “The Merger Agreement” beginning on pages 64 and 108, respectively, and a copy of which is attached as Annex A to the proxy statement/prospectus of which this notice is a part (the “Merger Agreement Proposal”);

 

·to approve, on an advisory (non-binding) basis, the golden parachute compensation payments that may be paid or become payable by Iridium to its named executive officers in connection with the Mergers (the “Merger-Related Compensation Proposal”); and

 

·to approve the adjournment of the special meeting, if necessary or appropriate, to solicit additional proxies if there are not sufficient votes to adopt the Merger Agreement (the “Adjournment Proposal”).

 

Iridium will transact no other business at the special meeting except such business as may properly be brought before the special meeting or any adjournment or postponement thereof by or at the direction of the Iridium board of directors (the “Iridium Board”). Please refer to the proxy statement/prospectus of which this notice is a part for further information with respect to the business to be transacted at the special meeting.

 

The special meeting will be held in a virtual meeting format only. You will not be able to attend the special meeting physically in person.

 

Iridium fixed the close of business on August 21, 2026, as the record date for the special meeting. Only Iridium stockholders of record at the record date are entitled to receive notice of, and to vote at, the special meeting or any adjournment or postponement thereof. A complete list of stockholders entitled to vote at the special meeting will be available for inspection for a period of 10 days ending the day prior to the special meeting and during the special meeting at http://www.virtualshareholdermeeting.com/IRDM2026SM by entering the control number provided on your proxy card, voting instruction form or notice.

  

Completion of the Mergers is conditioned on adoption of the Merger Agreement by the Iridium stockholders, which requires the affirmative vote of holders of a majority of the outstanding shares of Iridium Common Stock entitled to vote thereon.

 

The Iridium Board has unanimously determined that (i) the Merger Agreement and the Mergers, on the terms and subject to the conditions set forth in the Merger Agreement, are fair to and in the best interests of Iridium and its stockholders; (ii) the Merger Agreement and the Mergers are advisable; (iii) the Merger Agreement, the execution and delivery by Iridium of the Merger Agreement and the performance by Iridium of the agreements contained in the Merger Agreement and the consummation of the Mergers, on the terms and subject to the conditions contained in the Merger Agreement, are approved; (iv) the adoption of the Merger Agreement should be submitted to a vote at a meeting of Iridium’s stockholders and (v) the adoption of the Merger Agreement and the Mergers, in accordance with the terms of the Merger Agreement, be recommended to the Iridium stockholders.

 

Your vote is very important regardless of the number of shares of Iridium Common Stock that you own. If you plan to attend the special meeting virtually, please follow the instructions as outlined in this proxy statement/prospectus. Whether or not you expect to attend the special meeting virtually, we urge you to submit your vote in advance of the meeting. If your shares are held in the name of a broker, bank or other nominee,

DEFINED TERMS

 

Unless stated otherwise, when the following bolded terms and abbreviations appear in this proxy statement/prospectus, they have the meanings indicated below:

 

·Aireon Credit Agreement refers to the Credit and Guaranty Agreement, dated as of October 10, 2023, as amended by the First Amendment to the Credit and Guaranty Agreement, dated as of July 2, 2026, by and among Aireon LLC, as borrower, Aireon Holdings LLC, other subsidiaries of Aireon Holdings LLC from time to time party thereto as guarantors, GLAS USA LLC, a New Jersey limited liability company, as administrative agent, GLAS AMERICAS LLC, a New York limited liability company, as collateral agent and the lenders from time to time party thereto.

 

  · Aireon Seller Loan Agreement refers to the Credit and Guaranty Agreement, dated as of July 2, 2026, by and among Iridium Monitor Holdings LLC, as borrower, the guarantors from time to time party thereto, GLAS USA LLC, a New Jersey limited liability company, as administrative agent and collateral agent, and the lenders from time to time party thereto.

 

·Aireon Transaction refers to Iridium’s acquisition, completed on July 2, 2026, of the remaining 61% of the equity interests in Aireon Holdings LLC that Iridium did not already own.

 

·Assumed Iridium RSU Award refers to an Iridium RSU Award or Iridium PSU Award that is outstanding immediately prior to the First Effective Time that is assumed by Rocket Lab and converted into a restricted stock unit award covering Rocket Lab Common Stock.

 

·Bridge Facility refers to the committed 364-day senior secured bridge term loan facility in an aggregate principal amount of $3.6 billion pursuant to the Commitment Letter.

 

·Cash Consideration refers to $27.00 in cash, without interest, payable in respect of each share of Iridium Common Stock converted in the First Merger, subject to the terms of the Merger Agreement.

 

·Closing refers to the closing of the Mergers.

 

·Closing Date refers to the date on which the Closing occurs.

 

·COBRA refers to the Consolidated Omnibus Budget Reconciliation Act of 1985, as amended.

 

·Code refers to the Internal Revenue Code of 1986, as amended.

 

·Combined Company refers to Rocket Lab and its subsidiaries, including Iridium and its subsidiaries, taken as a whole, immediately after giving effect to the Mergers.

 

·Commitment Letter refers to the commitment letter, dated as of June 28, 2026, among Rocket Lab, Deutsche Bank AG New York Branch, Deutsche Bank Securities Inc., Wells Fargo Bank, National Association, and Wells Fargo Securities, LLC, pursuant to which Deutsche Bank AG New York Branch and Wells Fargo Bank, National Association have committed, subject to the terms and conditions thereof, to provide the Bridge Facility.

 

·Continuity of Interest Requirement refers to the continuity-of-interest requirement applicable to the treatment of the Mergers as a “reorganization” within the meaning of Section 368(a) of the Code.

 

·Debt Financing refers to the debt financing to be obtained by Rocket Lab or its subsidiaries in connection with the transactions contemplated by the Merger Agreement, including the Bridge Facility, any issuance and sale of senior secured or unsecured notes, borrowing under a senior secured term loan “B” facility (including the consummation of an amendment to the Iridium Credit Agreement to permit the Mergers), or any combination thereof.

 

·DGCL refers to the General Corporation Law of the State of Delaware.

 

·Dissenting Shares refers to shares of Iridium Common Stock held by an Iridium stockholder who has neither voted in favor of the adoption of the Merger Agreement nor consented thereto in writing and who has properly and validly demanded appraisal of such shares in accordance with Section 262 of the DGCL, until such stockholder fails to perfect, effectively withdraws or otherwise loses such appraisal rights.

·End Date refers to June 28, 2027, as such date may be automatically extended, in the circumstances specified in the Merger Agreement relating to the receipt of required regulatory approvals or the absence of certain legal restraints, first to September 28, 2027, and subsequently to December 28, 2027.

 

·Equity Award Exchange Ratio refers to the sum of (a) the quotient obtained by dividing the Cash Consideration by the Rocket Lab Stock Price, rounded to four decimal places, plus (b) the Exchange Ratio.

 

·Equity Financing refers to any equity financing undertaken by Rocket Lab or its subsidiaries following the date of the Merger Agreement, including any private or public offering of equity or equity-linked securities, for the purpose of funding the acquisition of Iridium or replacing the Bridge Facility.

 

·Equity Threshold Condition refers to the condition that the value of the shares of Rocket Lab Common Stock received by holders of Iridium Common Stock as part of the Merger Consideration constitutes at least 40% of the total value of all Merger Consideration received by such holders (as determined under the Merger Agreement).

-0.4000, if the Rocket Lab Stock Price is equal to or less than $67.50;

 

-the quotient obtained by dividing $27.00 by the Rocket Lab Stock Price, rounded to four decimal places, if the Rocket Lab Stock Price is greater than $67.50 but less than $112.50; or

 

-0.2400, if the Rocket Lab Stock Price is equal to or greater than $112.50.

·Supporting Stockholders refers to the directors and officers of Iridium who entered into the Support Agreement.

Rocket Lab has supplied all information contained in, and incorporated by reference into, this proxy statement/prospectus relating to Rocket Lab, Merger Sub I and Merger Sub II, and Iridium has supplied all such information relating to Iridium.

QUESTIONS AND ANSWERS ABOUT THE MERGERS AND THE SPECIAL MEETING

 

The following questions and answers are intended to address briefly some commonly asked questions regarding the Merger Agreement and the Mergers and the Iridium Special Meeting. Rocket Lab and Iridium urge you to read carefully this entire proxy statement/prospectus, including the annexes and the other documents referred to or incorporated by reference into this proxy statement/prospectus, because the information in this section does not provide all of the information that might be important to you.

 

About the Merger Agreement and the Mergers

 

Q:Do any of Iridium’s directors or officers have interests in the Mergers that may differ from or be in addition to my interests as a stockholder?

 

A:Yes. In considering the recommendation of the Iridium Board with respect to the Merger Agreement Proposal, you should be aware that Iridium’s directors and executive officers have certain interests in the Mergers that may be different from, or in addition to, the interests of Iridium stockholders generally. The Iridium Board was aware of and considered these interests, among other matters, in evaluating and negotiating the Merger Agreement and the Mergers, and in recommending that the Merger Agreement be approved by Iridium stockholders. See the sections titled “The Mergers—Interests of Iridium Directors and Executive Officers in the Mergers” and “Iridium Proposals—Proposal 2: The Merger-Related Compensation Proposal.”

 

Q:Are there any risks that I should consider in deciding whether to vote in favor of the Merger Agreement Proposal?

 

A:Yes. You also should read and carefully consider the risk factors relating to the Mergers and of Rocket Lab and Iridium contained in the documents that are incorporated by reference into this proxy statement/prospectus and in the section titled “Risk Factors” beginning on page 23.

 

Q:What is the Merger Agreement and what are the Mergers?

 

A:Rocket Lab, Merger Sub I, Merger Sub II and Iridium have entered into the Merger Agreement. Merger Sub I and Merger Sub II are both indirect, wholly owned subsidiaries of Rocket Lab. A copy of the Merger Agreement is attached as Annex A to this proxy statement/prospectus. The Merger Agreement contains the terms and conditions of the proposed acquisition of Iridium by Rocket Lab. Under the Merger Agreement, subject to the satisfaction (or, to the extent permitted by law and in accordance with the Merger Agreement, waiver) of the conditions to the Mergers set forth in the Merger Agreement and described in this proxy statement/prospectus, (i) Merger Sub I will merge with and into Iridium in accordance with the DGCL, with Iridium continuing as the Surviving Corporation in the First Merger, and (ii) (a) if the Second Merger Condition is satisfied, immediately following the First Effective Time, or (b) if the Equity Threshold Condition (but not the Second Merger Condition) is satisfied, on the second trading day following the First Effective Time, the Surviving Corporation will merge with and into Merger Sub II in accordance with the DGCL and the DLLCA, with Merger Sub II continuing as the Surviving Entity. Following the Second Merger, the Surviving Entity will be an indirect, wholly owned subsidiary of Rocket Lab.

 

As a result of the Mergers, Iridium will become an indirect, wholly owned subsidiary of Rocket Lab and will no longer be a publicly held company. Following the Mergers, Iridium Common Stock will be delisted from Nasdaq and will be deregistered under the Exchange Act, after which Iridium will no longer be required under SEC rules and regulations to file periodic reports with the SEC in respect of Iridium Common Stock.

 

Q:Why am I receiving this proxy statement/prospectus?

 

A:Rocket Lab and Iridium are sending these materials to Iridium stockholders to help them decide how to vote their shares of Iridium Common Stock with respect to the Mergers and other matters to be considered at the special meeting.

 

The Mergers cannot be completed unless Iridium stockholders adopt the Merger Agreement with the affirmative vote of the holders of a majority of the outstanding shares of Iridium Common Stock entitled to vote thereon. Iridium is holding a special meeting of its stockholders to vote on the proposal to adopt the Merger Agreement and other related proposals. Information about this special meeting, the Mergers and the other business to be considered by stockholders at the special meeting is contained in this proxy statement/prospectus.

 

1

 

 

This proxy statement/prospectus constitutes both a proxy statement of Iridium and a prospectus of Rocket Lab. It is a proxy statement because the Iridium Board is soliciting proxies from its stockholders. It is a prospectus because Rocket Lab will issue shares of its common stock in exchange for outstanding shares of Iridium Common Stock in the Mergers.

 

Q:What will Iridium stockholders receive in the Mergers?

 

A:In the Mergers, Iridium stockholders will receive the Merger Consideration, consisting of (i) the Cash Consideration, (ii) a number of validly issued, fully paid and nonassessable shares of Rocket Lab Common Stock equal to the Exchange Ratio and (iii) cash in lieu of any fractional shares of Rocket Lab Common Stock to which such holder would otherwise be entitled. The Exchange Ratio is as follows (in each case rounded to four decimal places): (A) 0.4000 if the Rocket Lab Stock Price is equal to or less than $67.50; (B) the quotient obtained by dividing $27.00 by the Rocket Lab Stock Price if the Rocket Lab Stock Price is greater than $67.50 but less than $112.50; and (C) 0.2400 if the Rocket Lab Stock Price is greater than or equal to $112.50. The Rocket Lab Stock Price is the volume-weighted average price per share of Rocket Lab Common Stock on Nasdaq, as reported by Bloomberg L.P. or another authoritative source mutually selected by Rocket Lab and Iridium, for the ten consecutive trading days ending on and including the second full trading day prior to the First Effective Time.

 

No fractional shares of Rocket Lab Common Stock will be issued in connection with the Mergers. Each holder of Iridium Common Stock that otherwise would have been entitled to receive a fractional share of Rocket Lab Common Stock will instead have the right to receive an amount in cash without interest determined by multiplying the Rocket Lab Stock Price by the fraction of a share of Rocket Lab Common Stock to which such holder would otherwise have been entitled.

 

For more details on the Merger Consideration, see “The Merger Agreement—Merger Consideration Received by Iridium Stockholders; Withholding Rights” beginning on page 109.

 

Q:What equity stake will Iridium stockholders hold in Rocket Lab immediately following the Mergers?

 

A: If the Rocket Lab Stock Price were equal to the closing price of Rocket Lab Common Stock on Nasdaq on August 18, 2026, the most recent practicable date prior to the date of this proxy statement/prospectus, the Exchange Ratio would be 0.3411. At this Exchange Ratio, it is estimated that, immediately after completion of the Mergers, Rocket Lab stockholders as of immediately prior to the Mergers would hold approximately 95% of the voting power of Rocket Lab stockholders and Iridium stockholders as of immediately prior to the Mergers (disregarding any shares of Rocket Lab Common Stock held by Iridium stockholders immediately prior to the Mergers) would hold approximately 5% of the voting power of Rocket Lab stockholders, calculated based on the number of shares of Iridium Common Stock, Rocket Lab Common Stock and Rocket Lab preferred stock outstanding as of August 18, 2026, the most recent practicable date prior to the date of this proxy statement/prospectus. The exact equity stake of former Iridium stockholders in Rocket Lab immediately following the completion of the Mergers will depend on (i) the number of outstanding shares of capital stock and outstanding stock-based awards of Rocket Lab and Iridium immediately prior to the First Effective Time and (ii) the final Exchange Ratio.

 

For more details on the Merger Consideration and the treatment of Iridium stock-based awards, see “The Merger Agreement—Merger Consideration Received by Iridium Stockholders; Withholding Rights” beginning on page 109 and “The Merger Agreement—Treatment of Iridium Equity Awards” beginning on page 113, respectively.

 

Q:Are the Mergers subject to conditions?

 

A:The respective obligations of Rocket Lab and Iridium to complete the Mergers are subject to the satisfaction (or written waiver by Rocket Lab or Iridium, as applicable) of a number of conditions, including (i) the Merger Agreement having been adopted by Iridium stockholders, (ii) any waiting period applicable to the Mergers under the HSR Act, as well as foreign regulatory approvals, having expired or having been terminated, (iii) the absence of any applicable law or regulation enacted or deemed applicable to the Mergers by a governmental authority in certain jurisdictions that has the effect of preventing, impairing, prohibiting, rendering illegal or enjoining the consummation of the Mergers, (iv) the approval for listing on Nasdaq of the Rocket Lab Common Stock to be issued in connection with the Mergers and (v) the registration statement on Form S-4,

 

2

 

 

of which this proxy statement/prospectus forms a part, becoming effective under the Securities Act and not being the subject of any stop order or any proceedings by the SEC seeking a stop order. The completion of the Mergers is not subject to the approval of Rocket Lab stockholders or the receipt of financing by Rocket Lab.

 

See “The Merger Agreement—Conditions to the Mergers” beginning on page 127.

 

Q:When do Iridium and Rocket Lab expect to complete the Mergers?

 

A:Rocket Lab and Iridium currently expect the Mergers to be completed in mid-2027, subject to certain regulatory approvals and the satisfaction or waiver of the other closing conditions contained in the Merger Agreement. However, neither Rocket Lab nor Iridium can predict the actual date on which the Mergers will be completed because it is subject to conditions beyond each company’s control, and it is possible that such conditions could result in the Mergers being completed earlier or later than expected or not being completed at all. The Merger Agreement may be terminated by either party if the Mergers have not been completed by the End Date, subject to two automatic 3-month extensions if the sole unsatisfied closing conditions at such time relate to regulatory approvals. For additional details regarding when the Mergers are expected to be completed, see “The Merger Agreement—Conditions to the Mergers” beginning on page 127 and “The Merger Agreement—Termination” beginning on page 128.

 

Q:What happens if the Mergers are not completed?

 

A:If the Merger Agreement is not adopted by Iridium stockholders or if the Mergers are not completed for any other reason, Iridium stockholders will not receive any consideration for their shares of Iridium Common Stock. Instead, Iridium will remain an independent public company, Iridium Common Stock will continue to be listed and traded on Nasdaq and registered under the Exchange Act and Iridium will continue to file periodic reports with the SEC. Under specific circumstances, Iridium may be required to pay Rocket Lab the Termination Fee. See “The Merger Agreement—Termination” beginning on page 128 and “The Merger Agreement—Termination Fees and Other Fees” beginning on page 130.

 

Q:Will the Rocket Lab Common Stock I acquire in the Mergers receive a dividend?

 

A:After the Closing, as a holder of Rocket Lab Common Stock, you will receive the same dividends on shares of Rocket Lab Common Stock that all other holders of shares of Rocket Lab Common Stock will receive with any dividend record date that occurs after the Closing. However, Rocket Lab has never declared or paid any cash dividends on its capital stock, and it is the present intention of the Rocket Lab Board to retain all earnings, if any, for use in Rocket Lab’s business operations and, accordingly, the Rocket Lab Board does not anticipate declaring any dividends in the foreseeable future. The payment of cash dividends in the future will be dependent upon Rocket Lab’s revenues and earnings, if any, capital requirements and general financial condition. The payment of any cash dividends is within the discretion of the Rocket Lab Board. Further, Rocket Lab’s ability to declare dividends may be limited by the terms of financing or other agreements entered into by it or its subsidiaries from time to time, including those contemplated by the Commitment Letter. For example, in connection with the Direct Funding Agreement with the United States Department of Commerce, Rocket Lab is currently restricted from buying back outstanding shares of its capital stock without obtaining prior approval and from paying dividends.

 

Q:What are the material U.S. federal income tax consequences of the Mergers?

 

A:The U.S. federal income tax consequences of the Mergers will depend, among other factors, on whether the Continuity of Interest Requirement is met, which requires that the value of Rocket Lab Common Stock paid to Iridium stockholders represents at least a certain minimum percentage of the total consideration paid to Iridium stockholders.

 

For this purpose, Rocket Lab and Iridium intend to treat the Mergers, taken together, as meeting the Continuity of Interest Requirement and qualifying as a “reorganization” within the meaning of Section 368(a) of the Code, if the “Equity Threshold Condition” (as defined in the Merger Agreement) is satisfied. However, the U.S. Treasury Department has not issued definitive guidance about how to determine the value of Rocket Lab Common Stock for a transaction like ours in which the amount of stock paid is subject to a collar. Accordingly, the Internal Revenue Service (the “IRS”) may challenge our determination that the Continuity of Interest Requirement is met if the Equity Threshold Condition is satisfied.

 

3

 

 

Assuming the Mergers qualify as a reorganization, a U.S. Holder (as defined in “The Mergers—Material U.S. Federal Income Tax Consequences of the Mergers”) will generally recognize a capital gain (but not loss) upon the exchange of Iridium Common Stock for Rocket Lab Common Stock equal to the lesser of gain recognized in the Mergers or the amount of Cash Consideration received pursuant to the Mergers (excluding any cash received in lieu of a fractional share of Rocket Lab Common Stock, which shall be treated as discussed below under the section titled “Material U.S. Federal Income Tax Consequences of the Mergers—Tax Consequences if the Mergers Qualify for the Intended Tax Treatment—Cash in Lieu of Fractional Shares” beginning on page 106 of this proxy statement/prospectus).

  

If the Continuity of Interest Requirement is not satisfied or the Second Merger is never consummated, then the exchange of Iridium Common Stock for Rocket Lab Common Stock and cash in the Mergers will be a fully taxable transaction in which a U.S. Holder generally would recognize gain or loss in an amount equal to the difference, if any, between the sum of the fair market value of the Rocket Lab Common Stock and the amount of Cash Consideration received in the Mergers, and such U.S. Holder’s aggregate tax basis in the corresponding Iridium Common Stock surrendered in the Mergers.

 

Iridium’s obligation and Rocket Lab’s obligation to complete the Mergers are not conditioned on the Mergers being treated as a “reorganization” within the meaning of Section 368(a) of the Code or upon the receipt by Rocket Lab or Iridium of an opinion from counsel to that effect. Rocket Lab and Iridium have not sought, and will not seek, any ruling from the IRS regarding any matters related to the Mergers, and as a result, there can be no assurance that the IRS would not assert that the Mergers do not qualify as a “reorganization” within the meaning of Section 368(a) of the Code (even if the Equity Threshold Condition is met), or that a court would not sustain such a position. Whether or not the Mergers will qualify to be treated as a reorganization may not be known until after the Closing Date.

 

Neither Iridium nor Rocket Lab or any of their respective advisors or affiliates provides any assurances regarding the tax consequences of the Mergers, including whether the Equity Threshold Condition will be satisfied or the Mergers will qualify as a “reorganization” under Section 368(a) of the Code. As a result, in deciding whether to approve the Mergers, you should consider the possibility that the Mergers may be taxable to you because the Equity Threshold Condition is not satisfied or the Mergers otherwise do not qualify as a “reorganization” described under Section 368(a) of the Code. All holders of Iridium Common Stock should consult with their own tax advisor to determine the particular U.S. federal, state or local or non-U.S. income or other tax consequences of the Mergers to them. See “The Mergers—Material U.S. Federal Income Tax Consequences of the Mergers” beginning on page 103 for additional information.

 

Q:Am I entitled to exercise appraisal rights in connection with the Mergers instead of receiving the Merger Consideration for my shares of Iridium Common Stock?

 

A:Yes. Iridium stockholders are entitled to appraisal rights in connection with the First Merger. To exercise such appraisal right, you must make a proper demand for appraisal of your shares of Iridium Common Stock in accordance with Section 262 of the DGCL and otherwise comply with all applicable provisions of Section 262 of the DGCL. If this appraisal right is properly exercised, and assuming you do not fail to perfect, validly withdraw or otherwise lose your appraisal rights under Section 262 of the DGCL with respect to your shares of Iridium Common Stock, your shares of Iridium Common Stock will not be converted into or represent the right to receive the Merger Consideration, and you shall be entitled only to such rights as are granted by Section 262 of the DGCL to a holder of shares of Iridium Common Stock that are outstanding immediately prior to the First Effective Time (other than Canceled Shares) and that are held by any person who is entitled to demand and properly demands appraisal of those shares pursuant to, and who complies in all respects with, Section 262 of the DGCL (“Appraisal Shares”). If any Appraisal Shares lose their status as such (through failure to perfect or otherwise), then such shares will thereupon be deemed, as of the First Effective Time, to have been converted into, and shall represent only, the right to receive the Merger Consideration in accordance with the Merger Agreement, without interest thereon. The term “Canceled Shares” means shares of Iridium Common Stock owned by Rocket Lab, Merger Sub I, Merger Sub II, Iridium or any of their respective wholly owned subsidiaries immediately prior to the First Effective Time which are canceled at the First Effective Time without any consideration being delivered in exchange therefor. For more information, see the section titled “The Mergers—Appraisal Rights in the Mergers” beginning on page 98 of this proxy statement/prospectus.

 

4

 

 

Q:What is the source of the Cash Consideration for the Mergers?

 

A:Rocket Lab expects to fund the aggregate Cash Consideration from a combination of cash on hand, and cash obtained in connection with any Debt Financing and Equity Financing. The proceeds from the Bridge Facility, which will be available in a single drawing on the Closing Date, will be used to fund the Cash Consideration. Commitments under the Bridge Facility, or any loans funded thereunder, will be reduced or prepaid, as applicable, with proceeds from any Debt Financing or Equity Financing. For more information, see the section titled “Financing the Mergers” beginning on page 98 of this proxy statement/prospectus.

 

Q:What will happen to Iridium equity awards?

 

A:The Merger Agreement provides that, at the First Effective Time, the outstanding equity awards of Iridium will be treated as follows:

 

Iridium RSU Awards and Iridium PSU Awards. Each Iridium RSU Award and Iridium PSU Award that is outstanding immediately prior to the First Effective Time will be assumed by Rocket Lab and converted into an Assumed Iridium RSU Award subject to the same terms and conditions as applied to the applicable Iridium RSU Award or Iridium PSU Award immediately prior to the First Effective Time (including the same vesting and leaver provisions), except that each such Assumed Iridium RSU Award will cover a whole number of shares of Rocket Lab Common Stock equal to the number of shares of Iridium Common Stock covered by such Iridium RSU Award or Iridium PSU Award immediately prior to the First Effective Time (which, in the case of Iridium PSU Awards, will assume satisfaction of applicable performance-based vesting conditions at target levels) multiplied by the Equity Award Exchange Ratio (with the result rounded down to the nearest whole share), and each Assumed Iridium RSU Award will vest in full in the event of a termination of employment without cause within 12 months following the First Effective Time (in addition to any other termination vesting provisions that apply to the corresponding Iridium RSU Award or Iridium PSU Award).

 

Iridium Option Awards and Iridium CSAR Awards. Each Iridium Option or Iridium CSAR that is outstanding and unexercised immediately prior to the First Effective Time will be fully vested and exercisable and canceled and converted into the right to receive the Merger Consideration in respect of each share of Iridium Common Stock covered by such Iridium Option or Iridium CSAR, calculated net of the exercise price or strike price, as applicable, less applicable withholdings; provided that the Merger Consideration payable with respect to any Iridium CSAR will be paid solely in cash, with the stock portion converted into cash based on the Rocket Lab Stock Price.

 

For additional information on the treatment of Iridium equity awards in connection with the Mergers, see the section titled “The Merger Agreement—Treatment of Iridium Equity Awards.”

 

Q:What happens if I sell my shares of Iridium Common Stock after the record date but before the special meeting?

 

A: The record date for the special meeting (the close of business on August 21, 2026) is earlier than the date of the special meeting and earlier than the date that the Mergers are expected to be completed. If you sell or otherwise transfer your shares of Iridium Common Stock after the record date but before the date of the special meeting, you will retain your right to vote at the special meeting. However, you will not have the right to receive the Merger Consideration to be received by Iridium stockholders in the Mergers. In order to receive the Merger Consideration, you must hold your shares through completion of the Mergers.

 

About the Iridium Special Meeting

 

Q:What are Iridium stockholders being asked to vote on, and why is this approval necessary?

 

A:Iridium stockholders are being asked to vote on the following proposals:

 

·a proposal to adopt the Merger Agreement, a copy of which is attached as Annex A to this proxy statement/prospectus, which is further described in the sections titled “The Mergers” and “The Merger Agreement,” beginning on pages 64 and 108, respectively (the “Merger Agreement Proposal”);

 

5

 

 

·a proposal to approve, on an advisory (non-binding basis), the golden parachute compensation payments that may be paid or become payable by Iridium to its named executive officers in connection with the Mergers (the “Merger-Related Compensation Proposal”); and

 

·a proposal to approve the adjournment of the Iridium special meeting, if necessary or appropriate, to solicit additional proxies if there are not sufficient votes to adopt the Merger Agreement (the “Adjournment Proposal”).

 

Approval of the Merger Agreement Proposal by the affirmative vote of holders of a majority of the outstanding shares of Iridium Common Stock entitled to vote thereon is required for completion of the Mergers. The completion of the Mergers is not conditioned on the Adjournment Proposal.

 

Q:Why am I being asked to consider and act upon a proposal to approve, on an advisory, non-binding basis, certain compensation that will or may be paid by Iridium to its named executive officers that is based on or otherwise relates to the Mergers?

 

A:Section 14A of the Exchange Act requires Iridium to seek an advisory, non-binding vote to approve any agreements or understandings and compensation that will or may be paid by Iridium to its named executive officers that is based on or otherwise relates to the Mergers. Approval of this proposal by Iridium stockholders is not required to complete the Mergers. Even if such executive compensation proposal is not approved by Iridium stockholders, if the Mergers are completed, then the Mergers-related executive compensation may be paid to Iridium’s named executive officers to the extent payable in accordance with the terms of their compensation agreements and arrangements.

 

Q:What constitutes a quorum?

 

A:The presence at the special meeting, in person or by proxy, of the holders of a majority in voting power of the issued and outstanding shares of Iridium Common Stock entitled to vote at the special meeting will constitute a quorum for the transaction of business at the special meeting. Virtual attendance at the special meeting will constitute presence in person for the purpose of determining the presence of a quorum for the transaction of business at the special meeting. Abstentions will count as votes present and entitled to vote for the purpose of determining the presence of a quorum for the transaction of business at the special meeting. Brokers, banks or other nominees that hold shares for beneficial owners do not have discretionary authority to vote the shares as to any matter at the meeting without receiving voting instructions from the beneficial owners. Such shares will not be counted as present for quorum purposes.

 

A quorum is necessary to transact business at the special meeting. The Iridium Bylaws provide that if a quorum fails to attend any meeting, the chair of the meeting or a majority in interest of the stockholders who are present in person or by proxy and entitled to vote at the special meeting may adjourn the meeting from time to time, without notice other than by announcement at the meeting, to another date, place, if any, and time until a quorum is present. If the adjournment is for more than 30 days or if after the adjournment, a new record date is fixed for the adjourned meeting, Iridium will provide a notice of the adjourned meeting to each stockholder of record entitled to vote at the meeting.

 

Q:How does the Iridium Board recommend that I vote?

 

A:The Iridium Board unanimously recommends that Iridium stockholders vote “FOR” the Merger Agreement Proposal, “FOR” the Merger-Related Compensation Proposal and “FOR” the Adjournment Proposal.

 

Q:What do I need to do now?

 

A:After carefully reading and considering the information contained in, and incorporated by reference into, this proxy statement/prospectus, please vote your shares as soon as possible so that your shares will be represented at the special meeting. Please follow the instructions set forth on the accompanying proxy card or on the voting instruction form provided by the record holder if your shares are held in the name of your broker, bank or other nominee.

 

Please do not submit your Iridium Common Stock certificates at this time. If the Mergers are completed, you will receive instructions for surrendering your Iridium Common Stock certificates in exchange for shares of Rocket Lab Common Stock from the Exchange Agent.

 

6

 

 

Please carefully consider the information contained in, and incorporated by reference into, this proxy statement/prospectus. Whether or not you plan to attend the special meeting, Iridium encourages you to submit your proxy to vote via the internet, by telephone or by mail so that your shares will be voted in accordance with your wishes even if you later decide not to attend the special meeting.

 

Q:How can I attend the special meeting?

  

A: Stockholders as of the close of business on August 21, 2026 (the “record date”), may attend, vote and submit questions virtually at the special meeting by logging in at http://www.virtualshareholdermeeting.com/IRDM2026SM. To log in, stockholders (or their authorized representatives) will need the control number provided on their proxy card or voting instruction form.

  

Q:How do I vote?

 

A:If you are a stockholder of record of Iridium as of the close of business on the record date, you may submit your proxy before the special meeting in one of the following ways:

 

·Telephone-use the toll-free number shown on your proxy card;

 

·Internet-visit the website shown on your proxy card to vote via the internet; or

 

·Mail-complete, sign, date and return the enclosed proxy card in the enclosed postage-paid envelope.

 

If you are a stockholder of record, you may also cast your vote virtually at the special meeting by following the instructions at http://www.virtualshareholdermeeting.com/IRDM2026SM. If you decide to attend the special meeting virtually and vote at the meeting, your vote will revoke any proxy previously submitted.

  

If your shares are held in “street name” through a broker, bank or other nominee, that institution will send you separate instructions describing the procedure for voting your shares. If your shares are held in “street name” and you intend to vote at the special meeting, you may cast your vote virtually at the special meeting by following the instructions at http://www.virtualshareholdermeeting.com/IRDM2026SM. If your shares are held in “street name” then you must ask your broker for a legal proxy to vote virtually at the special meeting. Your vote at the special meeting will revoke any proxy previously submitted on your behalf by your broker, bank or other nominee.

 

The meeting will begin promptly at 8:30 a.m. Eastern Time, on September 24, 2026. Iridium encourages its stockholders to access the meeting prior to the start time leaving ample time for check-in. Please follow the instructions as outlined in this proxy statement/prospectus.

 

Even if you plan to attend the special meeting, Iridium recommends that you vote your shares in advance as described below so that your vote will be counted even if you later decide not to or become unable to attend the special meeting.

 

Q:When and where is the special meeting of stockholders? What must I bring to attend the special meeting?

 

A: The special meeting of Iridium stockholders will be held virtually at http://www.virtualshareholdermeeting.com/IRDM2026SM, at 8:30 a.m. Eastern Time on September 24, 2026. Online access will begin at 8:15 a.m. Eastern Time and Iridium encourages its stockholders to access the meeting prior to the start time. Even if you plan to attend the special meeting, Iridium recommends that you vote your shares in advance as described above so that your vote will be counted if you later decide not to or become unable to attend the special meeting.

  

Q:What is the difference between holding shares as a stockholder of record and as a beneficial owner?

 

A:If your shares of Iridium Common Stock are registered directly in your name with the transfer agent of Iridium, Equiniti Trust Company, LLC (“Equiniti”), you are considered the stockholder of record with respect to those shares. As the stockholder of record, you have the right to vote or to grant a proxy for your vote directly to Iridium or to a third party to vote at the special meeting.

 

If your shares are held by a broker, bank or other nominee, you are considered the beneficial owner of shares held in “street name,” and your broker, bank or other nominee is considered the stockholder of record with respect to those shares. Your broker, bank or other nominee will send you, as the beneficial owner, voting

 

7

 

 

instruction forms for you to use in directing the broker, bank or other nominee in how to vote your shares. You should follow the instructions provided by them to vote your shares. You are invited to attend the special meeting and you may cast your vote virtually at the special meeting by following the instructions at http://www.virtualshareholdermeeting.com/IRDM2026SM.

 

Q:If my shares are held in “street name” by a broker, bank or other nominee, will my broker, bank or other nominee vote my shares for me?

 

A:If your shares are held in “street name” in a stock brokerage account or by a broker, bank or other nominee, you must provide the record holder of your shares with instructions on how to vote your shares. Please follow the voting instructions provided by your broker, bank or other nominee. Please note that you may not vote shares held in street name by returning a proxy card or voting instruction form directly to Iridium. Your broker, bank or other nominee is obligated to provide you with a voting instruction form for you to use. You may also cast your vote virtually at the special meeting by following the instructions at http://www.virtualshareholdermeeting.com/IRDM2026SM.

 

Applicable stock exchange rules permit brokers to vote their customers’ stock held in street name on routine matters when the brokers have not received voting instructions from their customers. Those rules do not, however, allow brokers to vote their customers’ stock held in street name on non-routine matters unless they have received voting instructions from their customers. “Broker non-votes” occur when shares held in street name are present at a stockholder meeting at which at least one item of business is a routine proposal, but the broker is not instructed by the beneficial owner of those shares to vote on a particular proposal for which the broker does not have discretionary voting power. The Merger Agreement Proposal, the Merger-Related Compensation Proposal and the Adjournment Proposal are non-routine matters on which brokers are not allowed to vote unless they have received voting instructions from their customers. Therefore, it is expected that there will be no broker non-votes at the special meeting.

 

If you are an Iridium “street name” stockholder and you do not instruct your broker, bank or other nominee on how to vote your shares:

 

·your broker, bank or other nominee may not vote your shares on the Merger Agreement Proposal, which will have the same effect as votes cast “AGAINST” this proposal;

 

·your broker, bank or other nominee may not vote your shares on the Merger-Related Compensation Proposal, which will have no effect on the vote for this proposal (assuming a quorum is present); and

 

·your broker, bank or other nominee may not vote your shares on the Adjournment Proposal, which will have no effect on the vote for this proposal (assuming a quorum is present).

 

Q:What if I fail to vote or abstain?

 

A:For purposes of the special meeting, an abstention occurs when a stockholder attends the special meeting virtually and does not vote or returns a proxy with an “abstain” instruction.

 

Merger Agreement Proposal: An abstention or failure to vote will have the same effect as a vote cast “AGAINST” the Merger Agreement Proposal.

 

Merger-Related Compensation Proposal: An abstention will have the same effect as a vote cast “AGAINST” the Merger-Related Compensation Proposal. If an Iridium stockholder is not present virtually at the special meeting and does not respond by proxy, it will have no effect on the vote for the Merger-Related Compensation Proposal (assuming a quorum is present).

 

Adjournment Proposal: An abstention will have the same effect as a vote cast “AGAINST” the Adjournment Proposal. If an Iridium stockholder is not present virtually at the special meeting and does not respond by proxy, it will have no effect on the vote for the Adjournment Proposal (assuming a quorum is present).

 

Q:What will happen if I return my proxy card or voting instruction form without indicating how to vote?

 

A:If you sign and return your proxy card or voting instruction form without indicating how to vote on any particular proposal, the Iridium Common Stock represented by your proxy will be voted as recommended by the Iridium Board with respect to that proposal.

Information about the Parties to the Mergers

 

Rocket Lab

 

Rocket Lab is an end-to-end space company with an established track record of mission success. Rocket Lab delivers launch services, spacecraft design services, spacecraft components, spacecraft manufacturing and other spacecraft and on-orbit management solutions intended to make it faster, easier and more affordable to access space. Rocket Lab’s business is organized primarily into two operating segments: launch services and space systems.

 

Rocket Lab is incorporated in Delaware. Its principal executive offices are located at 3881 McGowen Street, Long Beach, California 90808, and its telephone number is (714) 465-5737. Rocket Lab’s website address is www.rocketlabcorp.com. Information contained on Rocket Lab’s website does not constitute part of this proxy statement/prospectus. Rocket Lab Common Stock is publicly traded on Nasdaq under the ticker symbol “RKLB.”

 

Additional information about Rocket Lab is included in documents incorporated by reference in this proxy statement/prospectus. See the section titled “Where You Can Find More Information” beginning on page 149.

 

Iridium

 

Iridium operates the world’s only truly global mobile satellite network, delivering reliable voice, data, and positioning, navigation, and timing (PNT) services anywhere on Earth. Iridium supports safety- and mission-critical operations for diverse markets such as aviation, maritime, government, emergency services, critical infrastructure, autonomous systems, and remote monitoring applications, where connectivity is essential. Headquartered in McLean, Virginia, Iridium provides its products and services through an ecosystem of 500-plus partner companies around the world.

 

Iridium is incorporated in Delaware. Its principal executive offices are located at 1676 International Drive, Suite 1100, McLean, Virginia 22102, and its telephone number is (703) 287-7400. Iridium’s website address is www.iridium.com. Information contained on Iridium’s website does not constitute part of this proxy statement/prospectus. The Iridium Special Meeting

 

Date, Time, Place and Purpose of the Iridium Special Meeting

 

The special meeting of Iridium stockholders will be held virtually at http://www.virtualshareholdermeeting.com/IRDM2026SM, on September 24, 2026, at 8:30 a.m. Eastern Time. The special meeting can be accessed by visiting http://www.virtualshareholdermeeting.com/IRDM2026SM, where Iridium stockholders will be able to participate and vote online. The purpose of the Iridium special meeting is to consider and vote on the Merger Agreement Proposal and other related proposals. Completion of the Mergers is conditioned on the approval of the Merger Agreement Proposal.

  

Record Date and Outstanding Shares

 

Only holders of record of Iridium Common Stock at the close of business on August 21, 2026, the record date, will be entitled to notice of, and be able to vote at, the special meeting or any adjournment or postponement thereof.

 

On the record date, there were 105,981,552 shares of Iridium Common Stock outstanding and entitled to vote at the special meeting. Each share of Iridium Common Stock outstanding on the record date entitles the holder thereof to one vote on each proposal to be considered at the special meeting.

 

A complete list of Iridium stockholders of record who are entitled to vote at the special meeting will be available for inspection for a period of 10 days ending the day prior to the special meeting and during the special meeting at http://www.virtualshareholdermeeting.com/IRDM2026SM by entering the control number provided on your proxy card, voting instruction form or notice.

 

Quorum; Abstentions and Broker Non-Votes

 

The presence at the special meeting, in person or by proxy, of the holders of a majority in voting power of the issued and outstanding shares of Iridium Common Stock entitled to vote at the special meeting will constitute a quorum for the transaction of business at the special meeting.

 

Abstentions will count as votes present and entitled to vote for the purpose of determining the presence of a quorum for the transaction of business at the special meeting. Broker non-votes, if any, will not be counted as present for the purpose of determining the presence of a quorum.

 

Required Vote

·The Merger-Related Compensation Proposal requires the affirmative vote of holders of a majority of the outstanding shares of Iridium Common Stock present in person or represented by proxy at the special meeting and entitled to vote thereon. Failures to be present virtually or by proxy, including broker non-votes, if any, will have no effect on the vote for this proposal (assuming a quorum is present). Abstentions will have the same effect as votes cast “AGAINST” this proposal.

 

·The Adjournment Proposal requires the affirmative vote of holders of a majority of the outstanding shares of Iridium Common Stock present in person or represented by proxy at the special meeting and entitled to vote thereon. Failures to be present virtually or by proxy, including broker non-votes, if any, will have no effect on the vote for this proposal (assuming a quorum is present). Abstentions will have the same effect as votes cast “AGAINST” this proposal.

The Mergers; Merger Consideration; Treatment of Stock-Based Awards

 

The Mergers

 

The terms and conditions of the Mergers are contained in the Merger Agreement, a copy of which is attached as Annex A to this proxy statement/prospectus. You are encouraged to read the Merger Agreement carefully and in its entirety, as it is the legal document that governs the Mergers.

 

On June 28, 2026, Iridium, Rocket Lab, Merger Sub I and Merger Sub II entered into the Merger Agreement, which provides that, upon the terms and subject to the conditions set forth therein and in accordance with the DGCL, Merger Sub I will merge with and into Iridium in the First Merger, with Iridium continuing as the Surviving Corporation and an indirect wholly owned subsidiary of Rocket Lab.

 

Subject to the satisfaction of the conditions described below, immediately following the First Effective Time, or on the second trading day thereafter, the Surviving Corporation will merge with and into Merger Sub II in the Second Merger, with Merger Sub II continuing as the Surviving Entity and an indirect wholly owned subsidiary of Rocket Lab, in accordance with the DGCL and the DLLCA. The Second Merger will occur immediately following the First Effective Time if the Second Merger Condition is satisfied, or on the second trading day following the First Effective Time if the Equity Threshold Condition, but not the Second Merger Condition, is satisfied.

 

Whether the Second Merger occurs depends on whether the value of the shares of Rocket Lab Common Stock to be received by Iridium stockholders in the Mergers represents at least 40% of the total value of the consideration to be received by Iridium stockholders in the Mergers. If neither the Second Merger Condition nor the Equity Threshold Condition is satisfied, the Second Merger will not occur, Iridium will continue as the Surviving Entity, and all references in this proxy statement/prospectus to the “Mergers” will refer solely to the First Merger. For a more detailed description of the structure of the Mergers and the conditions to the Second Merger, see the section

 

13

 

 

titled “The Merger Agreement—Structure of the Mergers” beginning on page 108, and for a description of the Intended Tax Treatment of the Mergers, see the section titled “Material U.S. Federal Income Tax Consequences of the Mergers” beginning on page 103.

 

Merger Consideration

 

At the First Effective Time, each share of Iridium Common Stock outstanding immediately prior to the First Effective Time (other than shares of Iridium Common Stock (x) held by Iridium as treasury stock or owned by Rocket Lab, Merger Sub I, Merger Sub II or any other subsidiary of Rocket Lab, (y) held by any subsidiary of Iridium or (z) as to which the holder has properly demanded and not withdrawn or lost appraisal rights pursuant to Section 262 of the DGCL) will be automatically converted into the right to receive (i) $27.00 in cash, without interest, and (ii) a number of validly issued, fully paid and nonassessable shares of Rocket Lab Common Stock, equal to the Exchange Ratio, together with cash in lieu of any fractional shares of Rocket Lab Common Stock.

 

Because the Exchange Ratio is subject to a collar, the number of shares of Rocket Lab Common Stock issuable in respect of each share of Iridium Common Stock, and the value of the stock portion of the Merger Consideration, will depend on the Rocket Lab Stock Price. For a description of the Exchange Ratio, the collar and the manner in which the Merger Consideration is calculated, see “The Merger Agreement—Merger Consideration Received by Iridium Stockholders; Withholding Rights” beginning on page 109.

 

Rocket Lab stockholders will continue to own their existing shares of Rocket Lab Common Stock, which will not be affected by the Mergers.

 

Restrictions on Sales of Rocket Lab Common Stock Received in the Mergers

 

All shares of Rocket Lab Common Stock received by Iridium stockholders in the Mergers will be freely tradable for purposes of the Securities Act and the Exchange Act, except for shares of Rocket Lab Common Stock received by any Iridium stockholder who becomes an “affiliate” of Rocket Lab after completion of the Mergers. This proxy statement/prospectus does not cover resales of shares of Rocket Lab Common Stock received by any person upon completion of the Mergers, and no person is authorized to make any use of this proxy statement/prospectus in connection with any resale.

 

Treatment of Iridium Equity Awards

 

The Merger Agreement provides that, at the First Effective Time, the outstanding equity awards of Iridium will be treated as follows:

 

Iridium RSU Awards and Iridium PSU Awards. Each Iridium RSU Award and Iridium PSU Award that is outstanding immediately prior to the First Effective Time will be assumed by Rocket Lab and converted into an Assumed Iridium RSU Award subject to the same terms and conditions as applied to the applicable Iridium RSU Award or Iridium PSU Award immediately prior to the First Effective Time (including the same vesting and leaver provisions), except that each such Assumed Iridium RSU Award will cover a whole number of shares of Rocket Lab Common Stock equal to the number of shares of Iridium Common Stock covered by such Iridium RSU Award or Iridium PSU Award immediately prior to the First Effective Time (which, in the case of Iridium PSU Awards, will assume satisfaction of applicable performance-based vesting conditions at target levels) multiplied by the Equity Award Exchange Ratio (with the result rounded down to the nearest whole share), and each Assumed Iridium RSU Award will vest in full in the event of a termination of employment without cause within 12 months following the First Effective Time (in addition to any other provisions that apply to the corresponding Iridium RSU Award or Iridium PSU Award, including under the Severance Plan).

 

Iridium Option Awards and Iridium CSAR Awards. Each Iridium Option Award or Iridium CSAR Award that is outstanding and unexercised immediately prior to the First Effective Time will be fully vested and exercisable and canceled and converted into the right to receive the Merger Consideration in respect of each share of Iridium Common Stock covered by such Iridium Option Award or Iridium CSAR Award, calculated net of the exercise price or strike price, as applicable, less applicable withholdings; provided that the Merger Consideration payable with respect to any Iridium CSAR Award will be paid solely in cash, with the stock portion converted into cash based on the Rocket Lab Stock Price.

The full text of the written opinion of Evercore, dated June 28, 2026, which sets forth, among other things, the procedures followed, assumptions made, matters considered and qualifications and limitations on the scope of review undertaken in rendering its opinion, is attached as Annex C and is incorporated herein by reference into this proxy statement/prospectus in its entirety. You are urged to read Evercore’s opinion carefully and in its entirety. Evercore’s opinion was addressed to, and provided for the information and benefit of, the Iridium Board (in its capacity as such) in connection with its evaluation of the proposed Mergers.
