Accounting Treatment of the Mergers

 

Rocket Lab and Iridium prepare their respective financial statements in accordance with GAAP. The Mergers will be accounted for as a business combination, with Rocket Lab as the accounting acquirer and Iridium as the accounting acquiree, using the acquisition method of accounting in accordance with Accounting Standards Codification 805, Business Combinations. Rocket Lab has been determined to be the accounting acquirer based on the Merger Consideration and composition of the Rocket Lab Board following the Mergers. The acquisition method of accounting will generally result in the recognition of the assets acquired and liabilities assumed of Iridium at their estimated fair values as of the date of the completion of the Mergers. The excess of the consideration transferred over the identifiable net assets acquired will be allocated to goodwill.

 

Regulatory Approvals Required for the Mergers

 

The completion of the Mergers is subject to the satisfaction or waiver of certain regulatory conditions, including the receipt of the required approval of the FCC for the transfer of control of Iridium’s FCC licenses and

 

15

 

 

authorizations. In addition, the Mergers require compliance with, and filings, registrations or notifications under, other applicable Satellite and Communications Laws and certain competition laws and foreign investment laws of non-U.S. jurisdictions, as well as compliance with the requirements of the National Industrial Security Program Operating Manual rule (the “NISPOM”) administered by the DCSA. In connection with its review, the FCC may refer the transaction to Team Telecom. The waiting period under the HSR Act applicable to the Mergers expired at 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time on August 12, 2026.

 

Iridium and Rocket Lab have agreed to use their respective reasonable best efforts to obtain the Required Regulatory Approvals as promptly as practicable, subject to specified limitations on Rocket Lab’s obligation to take divestiture and similar actions. Neither Iridium nor Rocket Lab can provide any assurance that the Required Regulatory Approvals will be obtained, or as to the timing of, or any conditions that may be imposed in connection with, such approvals.

 

For more information, see “The Mergers—Regulatory Approvals Required for the Mergers” beginning on page 96.

 

Financing the Mergers

 

Rocket Lab intends to fund the cash component of the Merger Consideration through a combination of cash from its balance sheet and other debt and equity financing sources. Iridium’s obligations to complete the Mergers are not conditioned on Rocket Lab obtaining any financing. For additional information, see “Financing the Mergers” beginning on page 98.

 

Bridge Facility

 

The Bridge Facility will be available in a single drawing on the Closing Date (as defined in the Commitment Letter) and the proceeds will be used to finance the Cash Consideration to holders of Iridium Common Stock in the Mergers, to refinance the Iridium Credit Agreement and for other purposes not prohibited by the Commitment Letter.

 

The terms of the Bridge Facility will be set forth in definitive loan documentation that will be consistent with the Commitment Letter. The Bridge Facility will also be subject to affirmative and negative covenants, events of default and other customary terms consistent with the specified documentation standards.

 

The Commitment Letter provides that, on or prior to the Closing Date, the commitments under the Bridge Facility, or, to the extent funded after the Closing Date, the loans under the Bridge Facility, will be reduced or prepaid, as applicable, with proceeds from the Debt Financing or Equity Financing.

 

Termination of Iridium’s Existing Debt

 

In connection with the Mergers, the parties intend to terminate and payoff the commitments and outstanding indebtedness under each of the Aireon Credit Agreement and the Aireon Seller Loan Agreement.

 

In connection with the Commitment Letter, Rocket Lab may elect to amend the Iridium Credit Agreement to, among other things, permit the existing loans thereunder to remain outstanding after the consummation of the Mergers. To the extent that such amendment is not elected by Rocket Lab or the lenders under the Iridium Credit Agreement do not consent to such amendments, Rocket Lab expects to repay the loans under the Iridium Credit Agreement at Closing with proceeds from the Bridge Facility, Debt Financing or Equity Financing or a combination thereof. The terms and timing of any such transactions have not been determined as of August 26, 2026, the date of this proxy statement/prospectus.

 

Appraisal Rights in the Mergers

 

Record holders and beneficial owners of Iridium Common Stock who comply with the procedures set forth in Section 262 of the DGCL will be entitled to appraisal rights if the First Merger is completed. Under Section 262 of the DGCL, record holders and beneficial owners of shares of Iridium Common Stock with respect to which appraisal rights are properly demanded and perfected and not withdrawn or lost are entitled to have such shares of Iridium Common Stock appraised by the Delaware Court of Chancery. Shares of Iridium Common Stock held by record holders and beneficial owners who properly exercise appraisal rights in accordance with Section 262 of the DGCL will not be converted into the right to receive the Merger Consideration, but instead will be canceled and represent the right to receive, in lieu of the Merger Consideration, a cash payment that is equal to the fair value of

 

16

 

 

their shares of Iridium Common Stock at the First Effective Time (exclusive of any element of value arising from the accomplishment or expectation of the First Merger), as determined by the Delaware Court of Chancery, together with interest, if any as determined in accordance with Section 262 of the DGCL. The fair value of such shares of Iridium Common Stock could be more than, less than or equal to the Merger Consideration. Iridium is required to send a notice to that effect to each record holder, as of the record date for giving notice of the special meeting, of Iridium Common Stock not less than 20 days prior to the special meeting and include in the notice a copy of Section 262 of the DGCL or information directing the stockholders to a publicly available electronic resource at which Section 262 of the DGCL may be accessed without subscription or cost. This proxy statement/prospectus constitutes Iridium’s notice to the record holders of Iridium Common Stock that appraisal rights are available in connection with the First Merger, and the full text of Section 262 of the DGCL may be accessed without subscription or cost at the following publicly available website: https://delcode.delaware.gov/title8/c001/sc09/index.html#262. YOU ARE STRONGLY ENCOURAGED TO CONSULT A LEGAL ADVISOR BEFORE ATTEMPTING TO EXERCISE YOUR APPRAISAL RIGHTS. For more information regarding Iridium stockholders’ appraisal rights, see the section titled “The Mergers—Appraisal Rights in the Mergers” beginning on page 98.

 

Nasdaq Listing of Rocket Lab Common Stock; Delisting and Deregistration of Iridium Common Stock

 

Prior to completion of the Mergers, Rocket Lab has agreed to use its reasonable best efforts to cause the shares of Rocket Lab Common Stock to be issued in connection with the Mergers to be approved for listing on Nasdaq. Approval of those shares for listing on Nasdaq is a condition to completion of the Mergers.

 

If the First Merger is completed, Iridium Common Stock will be delisted from Nasdaq and deregistered under the Exchange Act as promptly as practicable after completion of the First Merger. Following such deregistration, Iridium will no longer be required under SEC rules and regulations to file periodic reports with the SEC with respect to Iridium Common Stock.

 

Expected Timing of the Mergers

 

Rocket Lab and Iridium currently expect the Mergers to be completed in mid-2027, subject to the receipt of certain required approvals under applicable Competition Laws, Foreign Investment Laws and Satellite and Communications Laws (including any required FCC approvals and, if applicable, Team Telecom review), the receipt of the Iridium Stockholder Approval and the satisfaction or waiver of the other conditions to Closing contained in the Merger Agreement. However, neither Rocket Lab nor Iridium can predict the actual date on which the Mergers will be completed because completion is subject to conditions beyond each company’s control, and it is possible that such conditions could result in the Mergers being completed earlier or later than expected, or not being completed at all. For additional details regarding when the Mergers are expected to be completed, see “The Merger Agreement—Conditions to the Mergers” beginning on page 127.

 

Material U.S. Federal Income Tax Consequences of the Mergers

 

The U.S. federal income tax consequences of the Mergers will depend, among other factors, on whether the Continuity of Interest Requirement is met, which requires that the value of Rocket Lab Common Stock paid to Iridium stockholders represents at least a certain minimum percentage of the total consideration paid to Iridium stockholders. For this purpose, Rocket Lab and Iridium intend to treat the Mergers as meeting the Continuity of Interest Requirement and qualifying as a “reorganization” within the meaning of Section 368(a) of the Code if the Equity Threshold Condition is satisfied. However, the U.S. Treasury Department has not issued definitive guidance about how to determine the value of Rocket Lab Common Stock for a transaction like this one with a collar. Accordingly, the IRS may challenge a determination that the Continuity of Interest Requirement is met or may otherwise challenge the treatment of the Mergers as a “reorganization” described under Section 368(a) of the Code. Assuming the Mergers so qualify, a U.S. Holder (as defined in the section titled “The Mergers—Material U.S. Federal Income Tax Consequences of the Mergers”) will generally recognize a capital gain (but not loss) upon the exchange of Iridium Common Stock for Rocket Lab Common Stock equal to the lesser of gain recognized in the Mergers or the amount of Cash Consideration received pursuant to the Mergers (excluding any cash received in lieu of a fractional share of Rocket Lab Common Stock, which shall be treated as discussed below under the section titled “The Mergers—Material U.S. Federal Income Tax Consequences of the Mergers—Tax Consequences if the Mergers Qualify for the Intended Tax Treatment—Cash in Lieu of Fractional Shares” beginning on page 106 of this proxy statement/prospectus). However, Iridium’s obligation and Rocket Lab’s obligation to complete the Mergers

 

17

 

 

are not conditioned on the Mergers being treated as a “reorganization” within the meaning of Section 368(a) of the Code or that Rocket Lab or Iridium receive an opinion from counsel to that effect. Rocket Lab and Iridium have not sought, and will not seek, any ruling from the IRS regarding any matters related to the Mergers, and as a result, there can be no assurance that the IRS would not challenge the treatment of the Mergers as a “reorganization” within the meaning of Section 368(a) of the Code, or that a court would not sustain such a position. Whether the Equity Threshold Condition has been satisfied and the Mergers will be intended to be treated as a “reorganization” may not be known until after the Closing Date.

 

If the Continuity of Interest Requirement is not satisfied or the Mergers otherwise fail to qualify as a “reorganization” described under Section 368(a) of the Code, then the exchange of Iridium Common Stock for Rocket Lab Common Stock and cash in the Mergers will be a fully taxable transaction in which a U.S. Holder generally would recognize gain or loss in an amount equal to the difference, if any, between the sum of the fair market value of the Rocket Lab Common Stock and Cash Consideration received in the Mergers, and such U.S. Holder’s aggregate tax basis in the corresponding Iridium Common Stock surrendered in the Mergers.

 

All holders of Iridium Common Stock should consult their own tax advisors as to the specific tax consequences to them of the Mergers, including the applicability and effect of the alternative minimum tax and any U.S. state, local, non-U.S. and other tax laws. For a more detailed discussion, see “The Mergers—Material U.S. Federal Income Tax Consequences of the Mergers” beginning on page 103.

 

Litigation Related to the Mergers

 

Stockholders may file lawsuits challenging the merger, which may name Rocket Lab, Iridium, members of the boards of directors of Rocket Lab or Iridium, or others as defendants.

 

The Merger Agreement

 

Conditions to the Mergers

 

The parties expect to complete the Mergers after all of the conditions to the Mergers in the Merger Agreement are satisfied or waived, including after the Merger Agreement has been adopted by the stockholders of Iridium. The parties currently expect the transactions contemplated by the Merger Agreement to be completed in mid-2027. However, it is possible that factors outside of each party’s control could require them to complete the transactions contemplated by the Merger Agreement at a later time or not to complete them at all.

 

In addition to the approval of the Merger Agreement Proposal by Iridium stockholders, each party’s obligation to complete the Mergers is also subject to the satisfaction (or, to the extent permitted by law and in accordance with the Merger Agreement, waiver) of other conditions, including: the receipt of certain required regulatory approvals (such as the approval of the FCC), effectiveness of the registration statement on Form S-4 of which this proxy statement/prospectus forms a part (and the absence of any stop order by the SEC), approval for the listing on Nasdaq of Rocket Lab Common Stock to be issued in the Mergers (subject to official notice of issuance), the absence of any provision of any applicable law or regulation, and of any judgment, injunction, order or decree, that prohibits or enjoins the completion of the Mergers, the accuracy of the representations and warranties of the other party under the Merger Agreement (subject to the materiality standards set forth in the Merger Agreement), the performance by the other party of its respective obligations under the Merger Agreement in all material respects and delivery of an officer’s certificate by the other party certifying satisfaction of the two preceding conditions, and the absence, since the date of the Merger Agreement, of a material adverse effect with respect to Rocket Lab (in the case of Iridium) or Iridium (in the case of Rocket Lab, Merger Sub I and Merger Sub II).

 

Neither Rocket Lab nor Iridium can be certain when, or if, the conditions to the Mergers will be satisfied or waived, or that the Mergers will be completed. For a more complete summary of the conditions that must be satisfied or waived prior to completion of the Mergers, see “The Merger Agreement—Conditions to the Mergers” beginning on page 127.

 

No Shop

 

In the Merger Agreement, Iridium agreed to cease, and to cause its subsidiaries, directors, officers and financial advisors to cease, and to use reasonable best efforts to cause its and its subsidiaries’ other representatives

 

18

 

 

to cease, any existing solicitation of, or discussions or negotiations with, any third party relating to any Acquisition Proposal or potential Acquisition Proposal. Iridium also will not, and will cause its subsidiaries, directors, officers and financial advisors not to, and will use reasonable best efforts to cause its and its subsidiaries’ other representatives not to, directly or indirectly:

 

·solicit, initiate or take any action to knowingly facilitate or encourage the submission of any inquiry or proposal that constitutes, or would reasonably be expected to lead to, any Acquisition Proposal;

 

·solicit, initiate or participate in any discussions or negotiations with, furnish any material nonpublic information relating to Iridium or any of its subsidiaries to, or afford access to the business, properties, assets, books, records or representatives of Iridium or any of its subsidiaries to, or otherwise knowingly cooperate with, any third party, in each case relating to any inquiry or proposal that constitutes, or would reasonably be expected to lead to, any Acquisition Proposal;

 

·effect an Adverse Recommendation Change (as described below); or

 

·approve, authorize, recommend or enter into any letter of intent, agreement in principle, merger agreement, acquisition agreement or other similar arrangement relating to an Acquisition Proposal, other than an acceptable confidentiality agreement.

 

Notwithstanding these restrictions, at any time prior to receipt of the Iridium Stockholder Approval, if Iridium receives a bona fide written Acquisition Proposal that did not arise from a material breach of the non-solicitation provisions of the Merger Agreement, and the Iridium Board determines in good faith, after consultation with its outside legal counsel and financial advisor, that the Acquisition Proposal constitutes or would reasonably be expected to lead to a Superior Proposal and that the failure to take such action would reasonably be expected to violate the directors’ fiduciary duties under applicable law, then Iridium may, subject to entry into an acceptable confidentiality agreement and prior written notice to Rocket Lab, engage in discussions or negotiations with, and furnish nonpublic information to, that third party, subject to the requirement that any nonpublic information not previously provided to Rocket Lab be provided to Rocket Lab within 24 hours. In addition, prior to receipt of the Iridium Stockholder Approval and subject to the procedures specified in the Merger Agreement (including a prior notice period and Rocket Lab’s right to propose revisions to the terms of the Mergers), the Iridium Board may, in response to such a Superior Proposal, or in response to an Intervening Event, effect an Adverse Recommendation Change, and may terminate the Merger Agreement to enter into a definitive agreement providing for a Superior Proposal upon payment of the termination fee described under “The Merger Agreement—Termination—Termination Fees and Other Fees” beginning on page 130.

 

For a discussion of what constitutes an Acquisition Proposal or a Superior Proposal and the limitations on solicitation of Acquisition Proposals, see “The Merger Agreement—Covenants and Agreements—No Shop” beginning on page 119.

 

Termination

 

The Merger Agreement may be terminated and the Mergers may be abandoned at any time prior to the First Effective Time (notwithstanding any approval of the Merger Agreement by Iridium’s stockholders):

 

·by mutual written agreement of Iridium and Rocket Lab;

 

·by either Iridium or Rocket Lab, if:

 

-the Mergers have not been consummated on or before the End Date (June 28, 2027, unless extended, as described in this paragraph); provided that if as of the End Date, specified regulatory conditions (relating to certain Legal Restraints arising under, or the receipt of Required Regulatory Approvals within the scope of, the Competition Laws, Foreign Investment Laws, Satellite and Communications Laws or the NISPOM) have not been satisfied or waived, but all other conditions to Closing have been (or would be capable of being) satisfied or waived, the End Date will be automatically extended to September 28, 2027, and, in the same circumstances, will be further automatically extended to December 28, 2027; provided, further, that this termination right is not available to any party whose breach of the Merger Agreement has caused or resulted in the failure of the Closing to occur on or before the End Date;

 

19

 

 

-any Legal Restraint permanently preventing, prohibiting, rendering illegal or enjoining the consummation of the Mergers has become final and non-appealable; or

 

-the Iridium Stockholder Approval has not been obtained at the special meeting (including any adjournment or postponement thereof) duly convened and at which a vote on the adoption of the Merger Agreement has been taken;

 

·by Rocket Lab, if:

 

-prior to receipt of the Iridium Stockholder Approval, (A) an Adverse Recommendation Change has occurred or (B) Iridium has committed an Intentional Breach of its no-shop and related obligations under Section 6.05 of the Merger Agreement in any material respect; or

 

-Iridium has breached or failed to perform any of its representations, warranties, covenants or agreements in the Merger Agreement, such that the related closing condition would not be satisfied, and such breach or failure is incapable of being cured or, if curable, has not been cured by the date that is 30 business days after Iridium’s receipt of written notice thereof from Rocket Lab (or, if earlier, one business day prior to the End Date); provided that this termination right is not available if Rocket Lab, Merger Sub I or Merger Sub II is then in breach of the Merger Agreement in a manner that would cause the corresponding Rocket Lab-side closing condition to fail; and

 

·by Iridium, if:

 

-prior to receipt of the Iridium Stockholder Approval, the Iridium Board authorizes Iridium to enter into a definitive written agreement providing for a Superior Proposal in accordance with, and subject to the conditions set forth in, Section 6.05 of the Merger Agreement (with such agreement being entered into substantially concurrently with the termination of the Merger Agreement), provided that concurrently with such termination Iridium pays the Termination Fee; or

 

-Rocket Lab, Merger Sub I or Merger Sub II has breached or failed to perform any of its representations, warranties, covenants or agreements in the Merger Agreement, such that the related closing condition would not be satisfied, and such breach or failure is incapable of being cured or, if curable, has not been cured by the date that is 30 business days after Rocket Lab’s receipt of written notice thereof from Iridium (or, if earlier, one business day prior to the End Date); provided that this termination right is not available if Iridium is then in breach of the Merger Agreement in a manner that would cause the corresponding Iridium-side closing condition to fail.

 

The party desiring to terminate the Merger Agreement (other than by mutual written agreement) must give notice of such termination to the other parties, specifying the provision pursuant to which the Merger Agreement is being terminated. In specified circumstances, a terminating party may be required to pay the Termination Fee, as described under “The Merger Agreement—Termination Fees and Other Fees” beginning on page 130.

 

Termination Fees and Other Fees

 

The Merger Agreement requires Iridium to pay Rocket Lab the Termination Fee if the Merger Agreement is terminated in specified circumstances. The Termination Fee is payable if:

 

·Iridium terminates the Merger Agreement to enter into a definitive agreement providing for a Superior Proposal in accordance with the terms of the Merger Agreement (in which case the Termination Fee is payable immediately before, and as a condition to, such termination); or

 

·Rocket Lab terminates the Merger Agreement because, prior to receipt of the Iridium Stockholder Approval, an Adverse Recommendation Change has occurred or Iridium has committed an Intentional Breach of its non-solicitation (no-shop) and related obligations under the Merger Agreement in any material respect (in which case the Termination Fee is payable within two business days after termination).

 

20

 

 

In addition, Iridium must pay Rocket Lab the Termination Fee if all of the following occur (such circumstances, an “Acquisition Proposal Termination Scenario”):

 

·the Merger Agreement is terminated: (i) by either party pursuant to Section 10.01(b)(i) of the Merger Agreement because the Mergers have not been completed by the End Date, (ii) by either party pursuant to Section 10.01(b)(iii) of the Merger Agreement because the Iridium Stockholder Approval was not obtained at the special meeting, or (iii) by Rocket Lab pursuant to Section 10.01(c)(i) of the Merger Agreement as a result of an Intentional Breach by Iridium giving rise to a failure of the related closing condition;

 

·after the date of the Merger Agreement and prior to the applicable termination (or, in the case of a termination for failure to obtain the Iridium Stockholder Approval, prior to the special meeting), a bona fide Acquisition Proposal was made to Iridium or publicly disclosed; and

 

·within 12 months after such termination, Iridium consummates, or enters into a definitive agreement providing for, any Acquisition Proposal.

 

In an Acquisition Proposal Termination Scenario, the Termination Fee is payable concurrently with the consummation of such Acquisition Proposal or the earlier execution of such definitive agreement. For purposes of this “tail” provision, each reference to “25%” in the definition of Acquisition Proposal is instead treated as a reference to “50%.”

 

The Termination Fee of $223,620,000 represents approximately 3.75% of the equity value of Iridium implied by the transaction (based on the value of the Merger Consideration and the fully diluted number of shares of Iridium Common Stock outstanding, each calculated by the parties as of June 26, 2026, the last full trading day prior to the execution of the Merger Agreement). In no event will Iridium be required to pay the Termination Fee on more than one occasion.

 

The Merger Agreement characterizes the Termination Fee as liquidated damages, and not a penalty, representing a reasonable estimate of the losses that would be suffered by reason of the applicable termination. Except in the case of fraud or an Intentional Breach of the Merger Agreement by Iridium, if the Termination Fee becomes payable and is paid in full, the receipt of the Termination Fee will be Rocket Lab’s, Merger Sub I’s and Merger Sub II’s sole and exclusive remedy against Iridium, its subsidiaries and their respective directors, officers, employees, stockholders, affiliates and representatives in connection with the Merger Agreement and the transactions contemplated by it. However, nothing in the foregoing will limit a party’s rights as described below in the section titled “The Merger Agreement—Specific Performance” beginning on page 131.

 

The Merger Agreement does not provide for any reverse termination fee payable by Rocket Lab to Iridium under any circumstances, and does not provide for the reimbursement of either party’s expenses upon termination. For a description of the allocation of fees and expenses generally, see the section titled “The Merger Agreement—Expenses” beginning on page 130.

Risks Relating to the Mergers

 

Because the market price of Rocket Lab Common Stock will fluctuate and the Exchange Ratio may be fixed under certain circumstances, and in such circumstances will not be adjusted for stock price changes, Iridium stockholders cannot be sure of the value of the consideration they will receive.

 

At the First Effective Time, each share of Iridium Common Stock issued and outstanding immediately prior to the First Effective Time (other than any Canceled Shares or Appraisal Shares) will be automatically converted into the right to receive (i) an amount of cash equal to $27.00, without interest, (ii) such number of shares of Rocket Lab Common Stock equal to the Exchange Ratio, and (iii) cash in lieu of any fractional shares to which such share of Iridium Common Stock would otherwise be entitled. The “Exchange Ratio” means the following (in each case rounded to four decimals): (A) if the Rocket Lab Stock Price is equal to or less than $67.50, then the Exchange Ratio is 0.4000; (B) if the Rocket Lab Stock Price is greater than $67.50 but less than $112.50, then the Exchange Ratio is the quotient obtained by dividing $27.00 by the Rocket Lab Stock Price; and (C) if the Rocket Lab Stock Price is greater than or equal to $112.50, then the Exchange Ratio is 0.2400. The “Rocket Lab Stock Price” is the volume-weighted average price per share of Rocket Lab Common Stock on Nasdaq (as reported by Bloomberg L.P. or, if not reported therein, in another authoritative source mutually selected by Rocket Lab and Iridium) for the period of the ten consecutive trading days ending on and including the second full trading day prior to the First Effective Time.

 

The market price of Rocket Lab Common Stock at the time of completion of the Mergers may vary significantly from the market price of Rocket Lab Common Stock on the date the Merger Agreement was executed and the date of this proxy statement/prospectus. Because the stock portion of the Merger Consideration is payable based on an exchange ratio that is dependent on the Rocket Lab Stock Price, which will not be known until the second full trading day prior to the First Effective Time, Iridium stockholders will not know the actual Exchange Ratio, or be able to calculate the market value of the stock consideration they will receive upon completion of the Mergers, when they are asked to approve the proposals at the Iridium special meeting.

 

Stock price changes may result from a variety of factors, including general market and economic conditions, changes in Rocket Lab’s and Iridium’s respective businesses, operations and prospects, market assessments of the likelihood that the Mergers will be completed, the timing of the Mergers, regulatory considerations and other risk factors set forth or incorporated by reference in this proxy statement/prospectus. Many of these factors are beyond Rocket Lab’s and Iridium’s control.

 

See “The Merger Agreement—Merger Consideration Received by Iridium Stockholders; Withholding Rights” beginning on page 109 for a description of how the Exchange Ratio is calculated.

 

The Mergers are subject to conditions, some or all of which may not be satisfied or completed on a timely basis, if at all, and the Merger Agreement may be terminated in accordance with its terms if such conditions are not satisfied.

 

The completion of the Mergers is subject to a number of conditions, including, among others, (i) the receipt of the Iridium Stockholder Approval, (ii) the receipt of any regulatory approvals required to consummate the Mergers, (iii) the absence of any orders, judgements, law or regulation deemed applicable to the Mergers

 

23

 

 

that has the effect of preventing, impairing, prohibiting, rendering illegal or enjoining the consummation of the Mergers, (iv) the absence of any material adverse effect (as defined in the section titled “The Merger Agreement—Representations and Warranties” beginning on page 113) with respect to Rocket Lab or Iridium since the date of the Merger Agreement, (v) the effectiveness of the registration statement of which this proxy statement/prospectus forms a part and (vi) the authorization for listing on Nasdaq of the Rocket Lab Common Stock to be issued in connection with the Mergers. These conditions make the completion and timing of the Mergers uncertain. For a more detailed discussion regarding the conditions to the Mergers, see “The Merger Agreement—Conditions to the Mergers” beginning on page 127.

 

Although Rocket Lab and Iridium have agreed in the Merger Agreement to use their reasonable best efforts to complete the Mergers as promptly as practicable, many of the closing conditions are not within Rocket Lab’s or Iridium’s control, and neither company can predict when or if these conditions will be satisfied. In addition, if the Mergers are not completed by the End Date (which is June 28, 2027), subject to up to two automatic extensions (to September 28, 2027, and then to December 28, 2027), if on each applicable date all of the closing conditions, except those relating to regulatory approvals and governmental orders, have been satisfied or waived (or would be satisfied or capable of being satisfied if the Closing were to occur), either Rocket Lab or Iridium may choose not to proceed with the Mergers by terminating the Merger Agreement, and the parties may mutually agree to terminate the Merger Agreement at any time. The failure to satisfy all of the required closing conditions could delay the completion of the Mergers for a significant period of time or prevent it from occurring. Any delay in completing the Mergers could cause Rocket Lab not to realize some or all of the benefits that it expects to achieve if the Mergers are successfully completed within the expected time frame. There can be no assurance that the closing conditions will be satisfied or waived or that the Mergers will be completed. Further, either Rocket Lab or Iridium may elect to terminate the Merger Agreement in certain other circumstances, as further described in the section titled “The Merger Agreement—Termination” beginning on page 128.

 

Rocket Lab intends to finance the cash portion of the Merger Consideration with financing. Although obtaining financing is not a condition to the completion of the Mergers, the failure of that financing to be available when required could delay or prevent completion of the Mergers.

 

Rocket Lab expects to fund the aggregate Cash Consideration payable in the Mergers from a combination of cash on hand, and cash obtained in connection with any Debt Financing and Equity Financing. The completion of the Mergers is not conditioned on Rocket Lab obtaining any financing. As a result, if the anticipated Debt Financing or Equity Financing (or any alternative financing) is not available at the time required, Rocket Lab will nonetheless remain obligated to complete the Mergers and pay the Cash Consideration, subject to the terms of the Merger Agreement, and Iridium may seek to enforce that obligation, including, in specified circumstances, through an action for specific performance. However, if Rocket Lab is unable to obtain sufficient funds when required, the completion of the Mergers could be delayed or might not occur, and the remedies available to Iridium may not fully compensate Iridium for the resulting harm. In addition, the obligation to complete the Mergers regardless of the availability of financing could require Rocket Lab to obtain financing on terms that are less favorable than anticipated. For additional information regarding the financing of the Mergers, see “Financing the Mergers” beginning on page 98.

 

Rocket Lab expects to incur or assume substantial additional indebtedness in connection with the Mergers, which could adversely affect the Combined Company’s financial condition and limit its operational and financial flexibility.

 

To finance the Cash Consideration and related fees and expenses, Rocket Lab has obtained financing commitments for a $3.6 billion senior secured Bridge Facility and expects to incur or assume a significant amount of new indebtedness. Rocket Lab expects to replace all or a portion of the Bridge Facility with the Permanent Financing, which may consist of debt, equity or a combination of the two. The amount, composition and terms of the Permanent Financing have not yet been determined and will depend on market conditions and other factors at the relevant time. This increased level of indebtedness and the related debt service obligations and collateral arrangements could have important consequences for the Combined Company, including requiring it to dedicate a substantial portion of its cash flow from operations to the payment of principal and interest on its indebtedness, thereby reducing the funds available for operations, capital expenditures and other purposes, including Rocket Lab’s development and growth programs (including Neutron) and Iridium’s constellation replacement; increasing its vulnerability to rising interest rates and adverse general economic and industry conditions; limiting its ability

 

24

 

 

to obtain additional financing, incur additional indebtedness, make investments, pursue strategic acquisitions or other strategic opportunities or fund future capital requirements; placing it at a competitive disadvantage compared with less leveraged competitors; and resulting in a downgrade of, or other adverse action with respect to, its credit ratings. If Rocket Lab is unable to complete the Permanent Financing on favorable terms or at all, it may be required to retain or draw on the Bridge Facility, which is short-term and secured, or to accept less favorable terms. The Combined Company’s ability to service its indebtedness will depend on its future operating performance, which is subject to economic, financial, competitive and other factors, many of which are beyond its control. If the Combined Company is unable to generate sufficient cash flow to service its indebtedness, or to refinance its indebtedness on commercially reasonable terms or at all, its business, financial condition and results of operations could be materially and adversely affected. The agreements governing the new indebtedness are also expected to contain covenants that impose operating and financial restrictions on the Combined Company.

 

If the Mergers do not qualify as a “reorganization” within the meaning of Section 368(a) of the Code, the stockholders of Iridium may be required to pay substantial U.S. federal income taxes.

 

The U.S. federal income tax consequences of the Mergers will depend, among other factors, on whether the value of Rocket Lab Common Stock paid to Iridium stockholders represents at least a certain minimum percentage of the total consideration paid to Iridium stockholders. The Mergers are intended to qualify as a “reorganization” within the meaning of Section 368(a) of the Code if the Equity Threshold Condition is satisfied. However, the U.S. Treasury Department has not issued definitive guidance about how to determine the value of Rocket Lab Common Stock for a transaction like ours in which the amount of stock paid is subject to a collar. Accordingly, the IRS may challenge a determination that the Continuity of Interest Requirement is met even if the Equity Threshold Condition is satisfied or may otherwise challenge the treatment of the Mergers as a “reorganization” within the meaning of Section 368(a) of the Code. Whether or not the Mergers will qualify as a “reorganization” within the meaning of Section 368(a) of the Code depends on facts, including the value of the Rocket Lab Common Stock issued in the Mergers, that may not be known until after the Closing Date. The receipt by Rocket Lab or Iridium of an opinion from counsel as to whether the Mergers will be treated as a “reorganization” within the meaning of Section 368(a) of the Code is not a condition to Rocket Lab’s obligation or Iridium’s obligation to complete the Mergers. Rocket Lab and Iridium have not sought, and will not seek, any ruling from the IRS regarding any matters relating to the Mergers, and as a result, there can be no assurance that the IRS would not assert, or that a court would not sustain, a position contrary to the treatment of the Mergers as a “reorganization” within the meaning of Section 368(a) of the Code. If the Mergers do not qualify as a “reorganization” within the meaning of Section 368(a) of the Code because the Equity Threshold Condition is not satisfied, or if the IRS or a court determines that the Mergers do not so qualify, a U.S. Holder would generally recognize taxable gain or loss upon the exchange of Iridium Common Stock for Rocket Lab Common Stock and the Cash Consideration pursuant to the Mergers. See “The Mergers—Material U.S. Federal Income Tax Consequences of the Mergers” beginning on page 103.

 

The Merger Agreement contains provisions that limit Iridium’s ability to pursue alternatives to the Mergers, which could discourage a potential competing acquirer from making a favorable alternative transaction proposal and, in specified circumstances, could require Iridium to pay a Termination Fee to Rocket Lab.

 

The Merger Agreement contains provisions that restrict Iridium’s ability to solicit, initiate, or take any action to knowingly facilitate or encourage, subject to certain exceptions, the submission of any proposal for an alternative transaction, or to participate in any discussions or negotiations with, furnish any material nonpublic information relating to Iridium or any of its subsidiaries to, or afford access to Iridium’s business, properties, assets, books or records with respect to, or approve or recommend, any third-party proposal for an alternative transaction. Additionally, the Iridium Board must publicly recommend against a publicly disclosed proposal for an alternative transaction, subject to certain exceptions. Further, even if the Iridium Board effects an Adverse Recommendation Change, unless the Merger Agreement has been terminated in accordance with its terms, Iridium will still be required to convene the special meeting and submit the adoption of the Merger Agreement to a vote of its stockholders. In addition, Rocket Lab generally has an opportunity to offer to modify the terms of the Mergers in response to any third-party alternative transaction proposal that constitutes a Superior Proposal before the Iridium Board may effect an Adverse Recommendation Change or terminate the Merger Agreement to accept such a proposal.

 

In specified circumstances, Iridium will be required to pay Rocket Lab the Termination Fee of $223,620,000. The Termination Fee is payable if (i) Iridium terminates the Merger Agreement to enter into a definitive agreement

 

25

 

 

providing for a Superior Proposal in accordance with the terms of the Merger Agreement, or (ii) Rocket Lab terminates the Merger Agreement because, prior to receipt of the Iridium Stockholder Approval, an Adverse Recommendation Change has occurred or Iridium has committed an intentional and material breach of its non-solicitation obligations. In addition, Iridium will be required to pay the Termination Fee if (a) the Merger Agreement is terminated because the Mergers were not completed by the End Date, because the Iridium Stockholder Approval was not obtained, or by Rocket Lab as a result of an intentional and material breach by Iridium giving rise to a failure of the related closing condition; (b) after the date of the Merger Agreement and before the applicable termination (or, in the case of a termination for failure to obtain the Iridium Stockholder Approval, before the special meeting), a bona fide Acquisition Proposal was made to Iridium or publicly disclosed; and (c) within 12 months after the termination, Iridium enters into a definitive agreement providing for, or consummates, an alternative transaction. The Merger Agreement does not require Iridium to pay any termination fee solely as a result of a failure to obtain the required regulatory approvals, and it does not provide for any reverse termination fee payable by Rocket Lab or for the reimbursement of either party’s expenses. See the sections titled “The Merger Agreement—No Shop” and “The Merger Agreement—Termination” beginning on pages 119 and 128, respectively.

 

These provisions could discourage a potential third-party acquirer or merger partner that might have an interest in acquiring all or a significant portion of Iridium, or in pursuing an alternative transaction, from considering or proposing such a transaction, even if it were prepared to pay consideration with a higher per share cash or market value than the per share cash or market value proposed to be received or realized in the Mergers. In particular, the Termination Fee, if applicable, could result in a potential third-party acquirer or merger partner proposing to pay a lower price to the Iridium stockholders than it might otherwise have proposed to pay absent such a fee. If the Merger Agreement is terminated and Iridium determines to seek another business combination, Iridium may not be able to negotiate a transaction with another party on terms comparable to, or better than, the terms of the Mergers.

 

Completion of the Mergers is subject to regulatory approvals, and regulatory authorities may impose conditions that could have an adverse effect on Iridium and/or Rocket Lab following the Mergers or that could delay, prevent or increase the costs associated with completion of the Mergers.

 

Completion of the Mergers is subject to the receipt of certain regulatory approvals under applicable Competition Laws, Foreign Investment Laws and Satellite and Communications Laws. In deciding whether to grant the required approvals, consents, registrations, permits, expirations or terminations of waiting periods, authorizations or other confirmations, the relevant governmental entities may impose requirements, limitations or restrictions on the conduct of the business of Rocket Lab following the Mergers. Under the Merger Agreement, Rocket Lab and Iridium have agreed to use their respective reasonable best efforts to obtain, as promptly as practicable, all permits, approvals, clearances, expirations, consents, notices, waivers or terminations of applicable waiting periods, authorizations, qualifications and orders from any governmental authority required to be obtained to consummate the Mergers.

 

However, notwithstanding the foregoing, Rocket Lab is not required to take, agree to or propose any divestiture or behavioral remedy that (i) would reasonably be expected to be material to Iridium and its subsidiaries, taken as a whole, to Rocket Lab and its subsidiaries, taken as a whole, or to the Combined Company following the Mergers, taken as a whole, and (ii) is not conditioned on the completion of the Mergers. Iridium may not take, agree to or propose to take any divestiture or behavioral remedy without Rocket Lab’s prior written consent, and at Rocket Lab’s request Iridium is required to agree to such a divestiture or behavioral remedy so long as it is conditioned on the completion of the Mergers.

 

Governmental authorities may also impose conditions, terms, obligations or restrictions in connection with their approval of or consent to the Mergers, and such conditions, terms, obligations or restrictions may delay completion of the Mergers or impose additional material costs on, or materially limit the revenues of, Rocket Lab following the completion of the Mergers. There can be no assurance that governmental authorities will not impose any such conditions, terms, obligations or restrictions, and, if imposed, such conditions, terms, obligations or restrictions may delay or lead to the abandonment of the Mergers. At any time before or after consummation of the Mergers, notwithstanding the expiration of the applicable waiting period under the HSR Act, the FTC, the DOJ or any state attorney general could take such action under the U.S. antitrust laws as it deems necessary or desirable in the public interest, including seeking (i) to enjoin the completion of the Mergers, (ii) to require the divestiture of substantial assets of Rocket Lab or Iridium or their respective subsidiaries, (iii) to require the parties to license rights, hold separate assets, terminate existing relationships and contractual rights, grant certain rights or commercial

 

26

 

 

accommodations to third parties, or agree to other restrictions limiting the freedom of action of the parties and their respective affiliates, or (iv) to require any other changes or restructuring of the parties and their respective affiliates. Private parties also may bring legal actions under the U.S. antitrust laws under certain circumstances, notwithstanding the expiration of the applicable waiting periods under the HSR Act, seeking similar relief or seeking conditions to the completion of the Mergers. Neither Rocket Lab nor Iridium can be certain that a challenge to the Mergers on antitrust grounds will not be made or, if such a challenge is made, what the result will be. Rocket Lab will not be obligated to complete the Mergers if a non-appealable order prohibiting the Mergers is in effect, or if the Mergers have not been completed by the End Date (as it may be extended).

 

For a more detailed description of the regulatory review process, see the section titled “The Mergers—Regulatory Approvals Required for the Mergers” beginning on page 96.

 

The Mergers are subject to the receipt of certain regulatory approvals and consents, including from the FCC, foreign telecommunications and investment authorities, and national security facility clearances, and the timing for receipt of such approvals and consents could delay, prevent or increase the costs associated with completion of the Mergers.

 

Because Iridium and its subsidiaries hold licenses and authorizations issued by the FCC, the completion of the Mergers requires the prior consent of the FCC to the transfer of control of those licenses and authorizations, including Iridium’s space station authorization, gateway earth station authorizations, blanket earth station authorizations, experimental authorizations and international Section 214 authorization. Before the Mergers may be completed, such approval from the FCC for the transfer of the licenses and authorizations must be obtained. Additionally, the Mergers require compliance with, and filings, registrations or notifications under, other applicable Satellite and Communications Laws, including with the International Telecommunication Union.

 

The completion of the Mergers is also conditioned on the receipt of specified regulatory approvals, to the extent required by applicable law, in Chile, France, Spain, Switzerland and the United Arab Emirates, and, solely to the extent the relevant governmental authority affirmatively confirms that its approval is required prior to the completion of the Mergers, in Australia, New Zealand and the United Kingdom, relating to the transfer or continued effectiveness of certain of Iridium’s non-U.S. telecommunications licenses and authorizations, and on specified foreign investment approvals, in each case as set forth in the Merger Agreement. In addition, the Mergers are subject to the receipt of approvals under the foreign investment laws of Australia, New Zealand and the United Kingdom, and, to the extent required as a result of changes in applicable law after the date of the Merger Agreement, Canada.

 

Because Iridium, Rocket Lab and/or certain of their respective subsidiaries hold facility security clearances subject to the NISPOM, which is administered by the DCSA, to the extent requested by the DCSA, Rocket Lab, Iridium, or any of Iridium’s subsidiaries may be required to enter into a written commitment to mitigate or negate any foreign ownership, control or influence arising as a result of the Mergers. The completion of the Mergers may be conditioned on either the DCSA’s written acknowledgment that it has accepted a foreign ownership, control or influence mitigation plan proposed by Rocket Lab, or the execution and delivery to the DCSA of the requested commitment notice or commitment letter.

 

For a more detailed description of the regulatory review process and approvals required, see the section titled “The Mergers—Regulatory Approvals Required for the Mergers” beginning on page 96.

 

Failure to complete the Mergers could negatively affect the stock price and the future business and financial results of Iridium.

 

If the Mergers are not completed for any reason, the ongoing business of Iridium may be adversely affected and, without realizing any of the benefits of having completed the Mergers, Iridium could be subject to a number of negative consequences, including the following:

 

·Iridium may experience negative reactions from the financial markets, including negative impacts on its stock price;

 

·Iridium may experience negative reactions from its customers and suppliers;

 

·Iridium may experience negative reactions from its employees and may not be able to retain key management personnel and other key employees;

 

27

 

 

·Iridium will have incurred, and will continue to incur, significant non-recurring costs in connection with the Mergers that it may be unable to recover;

 

·the Merger Agreement places certain restrictions on the conduct of Iridium’s business prior to completion of the Mergers, the waiver of which is subject to the consent of Rocket Lab (not to be unreasonably withheld, conditioned or delayed), which may prevent Iridium from making certain acquisitions, taking certain other specified actions or otherwise pursuing business opportunities during the pendency of the Mergers that may be beneficial to Iridium (for additional information regarding the restrictive covenants applicable to Iridium, please see the section titled “The Merger Agreement—Covenants and Agreements—Conduct of Business” beginning on page 116); and

 

·matters relating to the Mergers (including integration planning) will require substantial commitments of time and resources by Iridium management, which could otherwise be devoted to day-to-day operations and other opportunities that may be beneficial to Iridium as an independent company.

 

In addition, Iridium could be subject to litigation related to any failure to complete the Mergers or related to any enforcement proceeding commenced against Iridium to perform its obligations under the Merger Agreement. If the Mergers are not completed, any of these risks may materialize and may adversely affect Iridium’s business, financial condition, financial results and stock price.

 

Rocket Lab may fail to realize the anticipated benefits and synergies of the Mergers, and the integration of Iridium may be more difficult, costly or time-consuming than expected.

 

The success of the Mergers, if completed, will depend, in part, on Rocket Lab’s ability to realize the anticipated strategic and financial benefits from combining the businesses of Rocket Lab and Iridium, including anticipated synergies. Rocket Lab and Iridium have different business models, management styles, risk tolerances, compensation structures and operating cadences, including Rocket Lab’s project-based launch and space-systems business and Iridium’s subscription-based global satellite-services business. The integration of two companies that have previously operated independently is a complex, costly and time-consuming process and may disrupt Rocket Lab’s current plans or operations and divert significant management attention and resources from ongoing business concerns. The difficulties Rocket Lab may encounter include the integration of operations, systems, technologies (including satellite operations and ground infrastructure), controls, personnel and cultures; the retention of key management and other employees, customers and suppliers; the retention or attraction of business and operational relationships; the consolidation of corporate and administrative functions; the coordination of geographically separate organizations and the different regulatory regimes applicable to Iridium’s satellite and communications business; the possibility of faulty assumptions underlying expectations regarding the integration process and associated expenses; and potential unknown liabilities, unforeseen integration expenses or delays associated with the Mergers. Even if Rocket Lab successfully integrates Iridium, it may not realize the expected benefits or synergies within the anticipated time frame, or at all, and the costs of achieving them may exceed expectations. Any of the foregoing could adversely affect the Combined Company’s business, financial condition and results of operations, as well as the market price of Rocket Lab Common Stock. The market price of Rocket Lab Common Stock may also decline if the Mergers are not completed within the anticipated time frame, if transaction costs related to the Mergers are greater than expected, if Rocket Lab does not achieve the perceived benefits of the Mergers as rapidly or to the extent anticipated by financial or industry analysts or if the effect of the Mergers on Rocket Lab’s financial position, results of operations or cash flows is not consistent with the expectations of financial or industry analysts.

 

Members of the Iridium Board and management have interests in the Mergers that are different from, or in addition to, those of other stockholders.

 

In considering whether to adopt the Merger Agreement and approve the Mergers, Iridium stockholders should recognize that members of management and the Iridium Board have interests in the Mergers that differ from, or are in addition to, their interests as stockholders of Iridium. The executive officers and directors of Iridium have arrangements with Iridium that provide for certain severance payments or benefits, accelerated vesting of certain equity-based awards or other rights and payments or benefits upon completion of the Mergers and/or if their employment or service is terminated under certain circumstances following the completion of the Mergers. In addition, the executive officers and directors of Iridium have rights to indemnification, advancement of expenses and directors’ and officers’ liability insurance that will survive the completion of the Mergers. The Iridium Board was aware of these interests and considered them, among other matters, in evaluating, negotiating and approving the

 

28

 

 

Merger Agreement and making its recommendation that the Iridium stockholders vote “FOR” the Merger Agreement Proposal. These interests are further described in “The Mergers—Interests of Iridium Directors and Executive Officers in the Mergers” beginning on page 90.

 

The opinion of Iridium’s financial advisor will not reflect changes in circumstances between the signing of the Merger Agreement and the completion of the Mergers.

 

Iridium has received an opinion from its financial advisor in connection with the signing of the Merger Agreement, but has not obtained any updated opinion from its financial advisor as of the date of this proxy statement/prospectus. Changes in the operations and prospects of Rocket Lab or Iridium, general market and economic conditions and other factors that may be beyond the control of Rocket Lab or Iridium, and on which Iridium’s financial advisor’s opinion was based, may significantly alter the value of Rocket Lab or Iridium, or the prices of the shares of Rocket Lab Common Stock or Iridium Common Stock, by the time the Mergers are completed. The opinion does not speak as of the time the Mergers will be completed or as of any date other than the date of such opinion. Because Iridium does not currently anticipate asking its financial advisor to update its opinion, the opinion will not address the fairness of the Merger Consideration, from a financial point of view, at the time the Mergers are completed. The Iridium Board’s recommendation that Iridium stockholders vote “FOR” approval of the Merger Agreement Proposal and “FOR” the Adjournment Proposal, however, is made as of the date of this proxy statement/prospectus. For a description of the opinion that Iridium received from its financial advisor, see the section titled “The Mergers—Opinion of Iridium’s Financial Advisor” beginning on page 81. A copy of the opinion of Evercore, Iridium’s financial advisor, is attached as Annex C to this proxy statement/prospectus.

 

Iridium may be unable to retain key employees during the pendency of the Mergers.

 

In connection with the pending Mergers, Iridium’s current and prospective employees may experience uncertainty about their future roles with Rocket Lab following the Mergers, which may materially adversely affect Iridium’s ability to attract and retain key personnel during the pendency of the Mergers. Key employees may depart because of issues relating to the uncertainty and difficulty of integration or a desire not to remain with Rocket Lab following the Mergers. Accordingly, no assurance can be given that Iridium will be able to retain key employees to the same extent that Iridium has been able to in the past.

 

Potential litigation against Rocket Lab and Iridium could result in substantial costs, an injunction preventing the completion of the Mergers and/or a judgment resulting in the payment of damages.

 

Securities class action lawsuits and derivative lawsuits are often brought against public companies that have entered into merger agreements. Even if such a lawsuit is unsuccessful, defending against these claims can result in substantial costs. An adverse judgment could result in monetary damages, which could have a negative impact on Rocket Lab’s and Iridium’s respective liquidity and financial condition. Stockholders of Iridium may file lawsuits against Rocket Lab, Iridium and/or the directors and officers of either company in connection with the Mergers. These lawsuits could prevent or delay the completion of the Mergers and result in significant costs to Iridium and/or Rocket Lab, including any costs associated with the indemnification of directors and officers. There can be no assurance that any of the defendants will be successful in the outcome of any potential lawsuits.

 

Completion of the Mergers may trigger change in control or other provisions in certain agreements to which Iridium is a party, which may have an adverse impact on Rocket Lab’s business and results of operations after the Mergers.

 

The completion of the Mergers may trigger change in control and other provisions in certain agreements to which Iridium or its subsidiaries are a party. If Rocket Lab and Iridium are unable to negotiate waivers of those provisions, the counterparties may exercise their rights and remedies under the agreements, potentially terminating the agreements or seeking monetary damages. Even if Rocket Lab and Iridium are able to negotiate waivers, the counterparties may require a fee for such waivers or seek to renegotiate the agreements on terms less favorable to Iridium or Rocket Lab following the Mergers.

 

29

 

 

The market price of Rocket Lab Common Stock may decline as a result of the Mergers, including as a result of the issuance of a substantial number of shares of Rocket Lab Common Stock and potential future sales of those shares.

 

In connection with the Mergers, Rocket Lab will issue a substantial number of shares of Rocket Lab Common Stock to Iridium stockholders. The increase in the number of outstanding shares of Rocket Lab Common Stock may lead to sales of such shares, or the perception that such sales may occur, either of which could adversely affect the market price of Rocket Lab Common Stock. In addition, the market price of Rocket Lab Common Stock could decline following the Mergers if, among other things, the Combined Company does not achieve the perceived benefits of the Mergers as rapidly, or to the extent, anticipated, or if the effect of the Mergers on the Combined Company’s business and financial results is not consistent with the expectations of financial analysts or investors. Substantially all of the shares of Rocket Lab Common Stock issued in the Mergers will be freely tradable, which could contribute to selling pressure, although shares received by any Iridium stockholder who becomes an affiliate of Rocket Lab will be subject to resale restrictions under the Securities Act.

 

The shares of Rocket Lab Common Stock to be received by Iridium stockholders upon completion of the Mergers will have different rights from shares of Iridium Common Stock.

 

Upon completion of the Mergers, Iridium stockholders will no longer be stockholders of Iridium but will instead become stockholders of Rocket Lab, and their rights as Rocket Lab stockholders will be governed by the terms of the Rocket Lab Certificate of Incorporation and the Rocket Lab Bylaws. The terms of the Rocket Lab Certificate of Incorporation and Rocket Lab Bylaws are in some respects materially different from the terms of the Iridium Certificate of Incorporation and the Iridium Bylaws, which currently govern the rights of Iridium stockholders. See the section titled “Comparison of Rights of Stockholders of Rocket Lab and Iridium” beginning on page 142 for a discussion of the different rights associated with shares of Iridium Common Stock and shares of Rocket Lab Common Stock.

 

Iridium stockholders will have a significantly reduced ownership and voting interest after the Mergers and will exercise less influence over the policies of Rocket Lab following the Mergers than they now have over the policies of Iridium.

 

Rocket Lab stockholders currently have the right to vote in the election of the Rocket Lab board of directors (the “Rocket Lab Board”) and on other matters affecting Rocket Lab. Iridium stockholders currently have the right to vote in the election of the Iridium Board and on other matters affecting Iridium. Immediately after the Mergers are completed, it is expected that current Rocket Lab stockholders will own between approximately 94% and 96% of the voting power of Rocket Lab stockholders following the Mergers, and current Iridium stockholders will own between approximately 4% and 6% of the voting power of Rocket Lab stockholders following the Mergers (disregarding any shares of Rocket Lab Common Stock held by Iridium stockholders immediately prior to the Mergers), calculated based on the number of shares of Iridium Common Stock, Rocket Lab Common Stock and Rocket Lab preferred stock outstanding as of August 18, 2026, the most recent practicable date prior to the date of this proxy statement/prospectus. As a result, current Iridium stockholders will have significantly less influence over the policies of Rocket Lab than they now have over the policies of Iridium.

 

Rocket Lab has and will continue to incur substantial direct and indirect costs as a result of the Mergers.

 

Rocket Lab expects to incur significant non-recurring costs associated with combining the operations of Iridium with Rocket Lab’s operations. These costs include legal, financial advisory, accounting, consulting and other advisory fees, employment-related costs, filing fees and other regulatory fees and other related costs. Rocket Lab will also incur substantial transaction and financing fees and costs related to the Mergers and financing of the Cash Consideration. Whether or not the Mergers are consummated, Rocket Lab has already incurred and will continue to incur substantial expenses in pursuing the Mergers, which may adversely impact its results of operations.

 

Risks Relating to Rocket Lab after Consummation of the Mergers

 

The market price of Rocket Lab Common Stock after the Mergers may be affected by factors different from those affecting the price of Rocket Lab Common Stock or Iridium Common Stock before the Mergers.

 

Upon completion of the Mergers, holders of Rocket Lab Common Stock and Iridium Common Stock will be holders of Rocket Lab Common Stock, with Iridium stockholders receiving shares of Rocket Lab Common Stock in addition to the Cash Consideration. As the businesses of Rocket Lab and Iridium are different, including Rocket Lab’s launch services and space systems operations and Iridium’s satellite communications business, the results of

 

30

 

 

operations as well as the price of Rocket Lab Common Stock may in the future be affected by factors different from those factors affecting Rocket Lab and Iridium as independent standalone companies. The Combined Company will face additional risks and uncertainties that Rocket Lab or Iridium may currently not be exposed to as independent companies. Following the Mergers, the value of the Rocket Lab Common Stock received by former Iridium stockholders will be subject to the performance of the Combined Company, including the risks affecting Rocket Lab’s existing business. Iridium stockholders should review the risks applicable to Rocket Lab’s business, including those described in Rocket Lab’s filings with the SEC that are incorporated by reference into this proxy statement/prospectus. See the section titled “Where You Can Find More Information” beginning on page 149.

 

The completion of the Mergers may result in a loss of customers, distributors, suppliers, vendors, landlords and other business partners and may result in the termination of existing contracts.

 

Following the Mergers, some of the customers, distributors, suppliers, vendors, landlords and other business partners of Iridium may terminate or scale back their current or prospective business relationships with Rocket Lab. Some customers, including the U.S. government, may not wish to source a larger percentage of their needs from a single company. In addition, Iridium has contracts with customers, distributors, suppliers, vendors, landlords and other business partners that may require it to obtain consents from these other parties in connection with the Mergers, which may not be obtained on favorable terms or at all. If relationships with customers, distributors, suppliers, vendors, landlords and other business partners are adversely affected by the Mergers, or if Rocket Lab, following the Mergers, loses the benefits of the contracts of Iridium, Rocket Lab’s business and financial performance could suffer.

 

The Combined Company operates in highly regulated industries, and its inability to obtain, maintain, or renew required governmental authorizations, or any increase in regulatory scrutiny associated with its expanded operations, could adversely affect its business.

 

The Combined Company will rely on a wide range of governmental authorizations, including FCC and non-U.S. regulatory authorizations, and export authorizations under the ITAR and EAR. The integration of Rocket Lab’s operations with Iridium’s operations will increase the Combined Company’s regulatory footprint and may result in additional or heightened oversight.

 

The change in ownership of Iridium’s FCC authorizations, combined with Rocket Lab’s operations and personnel located outside the United States and Iridium’s provision of services to U.S. government and defense customers, may trigger review of foreign ownership and national security considerations by the FCC and relevant executive branch agencies.

 

The Combined Company will be required to fund the eventual replacement of Iridium’s satellite constellation, and these substantial future capital requirements, coinciding with Rocket Lab’s own capital programs, could strain the Combined Company’s financial resources.

 

Iridium’s existing satellite constellation has a finite operational life, and maintaining continuity and quality of service will ultimately require the design, construction, and launch of a next-generation constellation — a substantial, long-lead capital commitment. If the Combined Company is unable to fund constellation replacement on the anticipated timing or terms, if replacement costs exceed expectations, or if it elects to launch the next-generation constellation using Rocket Lab’s own launch vehicles and those vehicles are delayed or unavailable, the Combined Company’s ability to maintain service continuity, retain subscribers, and compete effectively could be adversely affected, which could have a material adverse effect on its business, financial condition, and results of operations.

 

Competition in the satellite communications industry, including from direct-to-device services, and subscriber churn could erode Iridium’s recurring revenue, on which the Combined Company will depend.

 

A significant portion of the Combined Company’s cash flow, and its ability to service the indebtedness incurred in connection with the Mergers, will depend on Iridium’s recurring, subscription-based revenue. Competitors to the Iridium business may have more extensive capital resources than the Combined Company, and current and new competitors may develop new technologies, or new equipment, including new and proposed LEO constellations, satellite direct-to-device (D2D) services, other mobile satellite services (MSS), terrestrial and other alternatives, that could successfully compete with Iridium’s offerings sooner or to a greater extent than Rocket Lab currently anticipates. Competitive pressure, technological change, pricing pressure, or increased subscriber churn

 

31

 

 

could reduce Iridium’s subscriber base and revenue, which could have a material adverse effect on the Combined Company’s business, financial condition, and results of operations and on its ability to service its indebtedness.

 

The Combined Company’s ability to use U.S. federal and state net operating loss (“NOL”) carryforwards and certain other tax attributes may be limited following the Mergers.

 

On December 31, 2025, Rocket Lab had U.S. federal NOL carryforwards of $840.9 million, $57.1 million of which begin to expire in varying amounts beginning in 2034, and $783.7 million of which will carryforward indefinitely and are available to offset up to 80% of future taxable income each year. Rocket Lab also had state NOL carryforwards of $549.4 million as of December 31, 2025.

 

Under Sections 382 and 383 of the Code, if a corporation undergoes an “ownership change,” the corporation’s ability to use its pre-change U.S. federal NOL carryforwards and other tax attributes (such as research tax credits) to offset its post-change income and taxes may be limited. In general, an “ownership change” occurs if there is a greater than 50 percentage point change (by value) in a corporation’s equity ownership by certain stockholders over a rolling three-year period. Similar provisions of state tax law may also apply to limit our use of accumulated state tax attributes. It is possible that the issuance of stock in the Mergers may increase the probability that the Combined Company experiences or will experience one or more ownership changes. If the Combined Company experiences one or more ownership changes, the Combined Company’s ability to use Rocket Lab’s pre-change NOL carryforwards or other pre-change tax attributes to offset U.S. federal and state taxable income may be subject to limitations, which could potentially result in increased future tax liability.

 

Risks Relating to the Support Agreement

 

In connection with the Merger Agreement, each of Iridium’s directors, in their capacity as stockholders of Iridium collectively beneficially holding an aggregate of 1,729,592 shares of Iridium Common Stock, representing approximately 1.6% of Iridium’s outstanding voting power as of June 24, 2026, have entered into a Support Agreement with Rocket Lab pursuant to which they have agreed, among other things, to vote their shares in favor of the adoption of the Merger Agreement. While the Support Agreement reduces the number of additional votes needed to obtain the Iridium Stockholder Approval, it does not guarantee that the requisite vote will be obtained. The Support Agreement terminates automatically upon, among other things, the termination of the Merger Agreement in accordance with its terms, a change in the Iridium recommendation or an Adverse Recommendation Change.

 

Other Risk Factors of Rocket Lab and Iridium

 

Rocket Lab’s and Iridium’s businesses are and will be subject to the risks described above. In addition, Rocket Lab and Iridium are and will continue to be subject to the risks described in Rocket Lab’s and Iridium’s respective Annual Reports on Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2025, respectively, as updated by subsequent Quarterly Reports on Form 10-Q and Current Reports on Form 8-K, all of which are filed with the SEC and incorporated by reference into this proxy statement/prospectus. For the location of information incorporated by reference into this proxy statement/prospectus, see “Where You Can Find More Information” beginning on page 149.
