Later that day on June 23, 2026, at the instruction of Iridium, representatives of Evercore contacted representatives of Deutsche Bank. The representatives of Evercore conveyed the Iridium Board’s position that the Third Rocket Lab Offer did not provide sufficient value certainty given the significant stock consideration in the deal, and that Rocket Lab would need to provide increased downside protection and/or increase the headline purchase price in order for the Iridium Board to proceed with a transaction with Rocket Lab. After negotiation, at the instruction of Rocket Lab, the representatives of Deutsche Bank communicated Rocket Lab’s agreement that the purchase price would be increased to $54.00 per share, payable $27.00 per share in cash and $27.00 per share in the form of shares of Rocket Lab Common Stock, and also, on Rocket Lab’s behalf, requested that Iridium commit to exclusivity with Rocket Lab. The representatives of Evercore communicated Iridium’s agreement that Iridium (i) would commit to exclusivity with Rocket Lab until June 29, 2026 and (ii) would agree to a “Company termination fee” equal to 3.75% of transaction equity value. 

 

Also on June 23, 2026, representatives of Evercore received an email from Party A’s financial advisor requesting a call to discuss Iridium’s sale process. Consistent with the Iridium Board discussion at the meeting earlier that day, after discussion with Iridium and Davis Polk, the representatives of Evercore did not engage in response to such outreach.

 

Also on June 23, 2026, Wilson Sonsini shared with Davis Polk an initial draft of a support agreement. Thereafter until the execution of the merger agreement on June 28, 2026, the parties and their advisors exchanged drafts of the support agreement and negotiated the terms of the support agreement.

 

On June 24, 2026, representatives of Iridium and representatives of Evercore received outreach from Party A and its representatives. Representatives of Iridium and Evercore did not engage with such outreach based on, among other things, (1) Iridium’s commitment to negotiate exclusively with Rocket Lab, (2) the Iridium Board’s view that a more favorable transaction could be negotiated with Rocket Lab relative to Party A’s proposal and (3) the risk that engaging with Party A at that time could jeopardize the successful execution of a transaction with Rocket Lab.

 

From June 24, 2026 through June 26, 2026, at the instruction of Iridium and Rocket Lab, respectively, representatives of Evercore held calls with representatives of Deutsche Bank to discuss the collar mechanism. The representatives of Evercore indicated that agreeing to a mutually acceptable collar for the purpose of enhancing value certainty for Iridium stockholders was a key gating item to executing a transaction. On June 26, 2026, Rocket Lab agreed to adjust the collar such that the value of the stock consideration would be fixed if the trading price of Rocket Lab shares at the time of the consummation of the transaction was within 25% above or below their value at signing, with the value at signing to be the five-day trailing VWAP as of June 26, 2026.

 

On June 28, 2026, the Iridium Board held a special meeting to evaluate the terms and conditions of the proposed transaction with Rocket Lab and to determine whether to approve the proposed transaction. Members of management and representatives of Davis Polk and Evercore were present. Representatives of Evercore provided an update on the status of discussions with Rocket Lab, including the negotiation of the collar mechanism.

 

72

 

 

Representatives of Davis Polk, among other things, reviewed with the Iridium Board its fiduciary duties under Delaware law (including in the context of the proposed merger) and provided an overview of key terms of the proposed merger agreement. Representatives of Evercore reviewed and discussed with the Iridium Board their financial analysis of the proposed transaction, including the proposed merger consideration of $54.00 per share paid to Iridium stockholders as $27.00 per share in cash and $27.00 per share in the form of Rocket Lab shares (subject to the 25% collar mechanism), which represented (i) an 89% premium to Iridium’s share price of $28.52 as of April 1, 2026 (the day prior to market speculation regarding the potential Amazon-Globalstar Transaction) and (ii) a 24% premium to Iridium’s closing price of $43.52 as of June 26, 2026 (the last trading day prior to the date of such meeting), and implied a $6.0 billion equity value and $8.1 billion total enterprise value for Iridium. Representatives of Evercore also noted to the Iridium Board that representatives of Party A had made outreach to both representatives of Evercore and to representatives of Iridium since the last meeting of the Iridium Board, but that Party A had not submitted a revised proposal. The Iridium Board concurred in the determination not to respond to Party based on, among other things, (1) Iridium’s commitment to negotiate exclusively with Rocket Lab, (2) the Iridium Board’s view that a more favorable transaction could be negotiated with Rocket Lab relative to Party A’s proposal and (3) the risk that engaging with Party A at that time could jeopardize the successful execution of a transaction with Rocket Lab. Subsequently, representatives of Evercore rendered to the Iridium Board Evercore’s oral opinion which was subsequently confirmed by delivery of a written opinion dated June 28, 2026, that, as of the date of such opinion and based upon and subject to the assumptions, limitations, qualifications and conditions described in Evercore’s written opinion, the merger consideration to be received by holders of Iridium Common Stock in the First Merger was fair, from a financial point of view, to such holders. A copy of the written opinion rendered by Evercore to the Iridium Board is attached hereto as Annex C. After extensive deliberations, the Iridium Board unanimously (i) determined that the Merger Agreement and the transactions contemplated by the Merger Agreement, including the Mergers, on the terms and subject to the conditions set forth in the Merger Agreement, are fair to and in the best interests of Iridium and its stockholders, (ii) declared the Merger Agreement and the transactions contemplated by the Merger Agreement, including the Mergers, advisable, (iii) approved the Merger Agreement, the execution and delivery by Iridium of the Merger Agreement, the performance by Iridium of the agreements contained in the Merger Agreement and the consummation of the transactions contemplated by the Merger Agreement, including the Mergers, on the terms and subject to the conditions contained in the Merger Agreement, (iv) directed that the adoption of the Merger Agreement be submitted to a vote at a meeting of Iridium’s stockholders in accordance with the terms of the Merger Agreement and (v) resolved to recommend adoption of the Merger Agreement and the transactions contemplated by the Merger Agreement in accordance with the terms of the Merger Agreement, including the Mergers, to the stockholders of Iridium.

 

Shortly thereafter on June 28, 2026, Iridium and Rocket Lab finalized and executed the Merger Agreement and the related documentation.

 

The following morning, on June 29, 2026, Iridium and Rocket Lab issued a joint press release announcing execution of the Merger Agreement.

 

Iridium’s Reasons for the Mergers; Recommendation of the Iridium Board of Directors

 

By unanimous vote, the Iridium Board, at a meeting held on June 28, 2026, (a) determined that the Merger Agreement and the transactions contemplated by the Merger Agreement, including the Mergers, on the terms and subject to the conditions set forth in the Merger Agreement, are fair to and in the best interests of Iridium and its stockholders, (b) declared the Merger Agreement and the transactions contemplated by the Merger Agreement, including the Mergers, advisable, (c) approved the Merger Agreement, the execution and delivery by Iridium of the Merger Agreement, the performance by Iridium of the agreements contained in the Merger Agreement and the consummation of the transactions contemplated by the Merger Agreement, including the Mergers, on the terms and subject to the conditions contained in the Merger Agreement, (d) directed that the adoption of the Merger Agreement be submitted to a vote at a meeting of Iridium’s stockholders in accordance with the terms of the Merger Agreement and (e) resolved to recommend adoption of the Merger Agreement and the transactions contemplated by the Merger Agreement in accordance with the terms of the Merger Agreement, including the Mergers, to the stockholders of Iridium. The Iridium Board unanimously recommends that Iridium stockholders vote “FOR” the Merger Agreement Proposal, “FOR” the Merger-Related Compensation Proposal and “FOR” the Adjournment Proposal.

 

In reaching its determinations and recommendations, the Iridium Board consulted extensively with Iridium’s senior management and financial and legal advisors and considered a range of factors and scenarios. Factors that weighed in favor of the Mergers (not in any relative order of importance) include:

 

73

 

 

Greater Stockholder Value and Return Potential. The attractive value and nature of the consideration to be received in the First Merger by Iridium’s stockholders, including:

 

·the fact that the Merger Agreement was the product of arm’s length negotiations, as well as the Iridium Board’s belief, based on these negotiations and the increases in Rocket Lab’s proposals, that these were the most favorable terms to Iridium and its stockholders in the aggregate on which Rocket Lab was willing to transact and the risk that prolonging or expanding the sale process further could have resulted in the loss of an opportunity to consummate a transaction with Rocket Lab either on the terms of the Merger Agreement, including, among other things, the valuation represented by the Merger Consideration, or at all;

 

·the Iridium Board’s determination that the value offered to Iridium’s stockholders pursuant to the First Merger is more favorable to Iridium’s stockholders than the potential value from other alternatives reasonably available to Iridium, including remaining an independent public company, after reviewing Iridium’s business, financial condition, results of operations, market trends, competitive landscape and execution risks with executing its standalone strategic plan, and discussions with Iridium’s senior management and advisors and that there is attendant risk that if Iridium remained independent, Iridium Common Stock might not trade at levels equal to or greater than the value of the Merger Consideration in the near term, over an extended period of time or at all;

 

·that the Iridium Board conducted extensive outreach to potential acquirers and solicited interested parties pursuant to a sale process, that such process did not result in significant interest, with the only other material engagement being from a counterparty that offered a significantly lower purchase price, had not completed its due diligence, declined to negotiate the draft merger agreement provided to it in the sale process and did not offer comparable closing certainty, and that there was likewise no assurance otherwise that a more favorable opportunity to sell Iridium would arise later or through any alternative transaction;

 

·the fact that the announcement of the SpaceX-Echostar Transaction and Amazon-Globalstar Transaction had led to market speculation of a sale transaction involving Iridium, and the fact that Space Exploration Technologies Corp.’s (“SpaceX”) initial public offering (and public news reports preceding the SpaceX initial public offering) had precipitated enthusiasm in the market for space assets generally, contributing to the trading price of Iridium Common Stock increasing to a 52-week high;

 

·the fact that 50% of the Merger Consideration is expected to be paid in Rocket Lab Common Stock (subject to the collar mechanism described herein), which, as described below, allows Iridium’s stockholders to participate in future growth of the combined company, including any potential appreciation and synergies that may be realized by the combined company, which the Iridium Board viewed as an important opportunity for Iridium’s stockholders to enhance long term returns while maintaining liquidity should any of Iridium’s stockholders choose not to retain their shares of Rocket Lab Common Stock;

 

·the fact that 50% of the Merger Consideration is expected to be paid in cash, giving Iridium’s stockholders the opportunity to realize liquidity and near-term value certainty.

 

·that the Merger Consideration represents an implied premium of approximately 24% over Iridium Common Stock’s closing price on June 26, 2026, the last trading day before the Merger Agreement was announced, a premium of 15% over the one-month volume weighted average on the same date, a premium of 30% over the three-month volume weighted average on the same date, and a premium of 89% over the closing price on the trading day prior to the leak of the Amazon-Globalstar Transaction by the Financial Times;

 

·that the collar applicable to the stock consideration protects the value of the stock component of the Merger Consideration in the event of a decline in Rocket Lab’s stock price within the collar during the pendency of the Mergers while permitting Iridium’s stockholders to participate in increases in Rocket Lab’s stock price above the collar during the pendency of the Mergers;

 

·the Iridium Board’s knowledge of Rocket Lab, taking into account publicly available information regarding Rocket Lab and the results of Iridium’s due diligence review of Rocket Lab; and

 

74

 

 

·subject to certain limitations including a condition based on the trading price of Rocket Lab Common Stock, that the transaction is intended to qualify as a “reorganization” within the meaning of Section 368(a) of the Code if the Equity Threshold Condition is satisfied, and taxation on the portion of the Merger Consideration paid in Rocket Lab Common Stock may be deferred for U.S. federal income tax purposes.

 

Benefits of a Combined Company: Greater Scale and Financial Strength. The belief of the Iridium Board that Rocket Lab, following the Mergers, would be well positioned to achieve further free cash flow growth and generate superior returns for Iridium’s former stockholders through the stock component of the Merger Consideration, including as a result of:

 

·the benefits associated with creating a vertically integrated end-to-end space company spanning launch, spacecraft, spectrum, and on-orbit communications services through a proprietary network, especially in the context of a competitive industry where vertically integrated companies appear to be best positioned for long-term success, and including the significant expected annual operating synergies associated with the following:

 

-eliminating the current Iridium business’ third-party launch costs for constellation deployment and replenishment and capturing launch margin internally while guaranteeing orbital access as launch capacity tightens, ensuring continuity of service to customers;

 

-accelerating growth and new market opportunities by positioning the combined company to construct and deliver next-generation satellite communications, resilient PNT, and emerging defense and commercial space services in a more cost-efficient manner;

 

-providing Rocket Lab with immediate access to a proven constellation of LEO satellites and an established global communications customer base, furthering a long-term strategic vision to expand beyond launch services and spacecraft manufacturing into a vertically-integrated space applications company with recurring revenue from satellite services; and

 

-building on Rocket Lab’s and Iridium’s long-standing national defense work;

 

·creating a combined entity with a diversified financial profile and recurring cash flow streams, providing substantial cash flow to fund growth and respond to an evolving competitive environment;

 

·the expectation that the Mergers would be accretive to the combined company’s earnings per share, operating cash flow and free cash flow in 2027, as well as highly accretive in the mid- to long-term; and

 

·the combined workforce is expected to continue to increase efficiency and have an enhanced ability to provide value for stockholders of the combined company.

 

Dividends. The Iridium Board reviewed and considered the fact that Iridium could continue to return value to Iridium’s stockholders through quarterly dividends paid to Iridium’s stockholders in the ordinary course of business until the First Effective Time.

 

Opportunity to Receive Competing Acquisition Proposals and to Terminate the Merger Agreement in Order to Accept a Superior Proposal. The Iridium Board considered the terms of the Merger Agreement related to Iridium’s ability to respond to acquisition proposals and determined that the provisions of the Merger Agreement would not deter or preclude any third party from making an acquisition proposal. In this regard, the Iridium Board considered that:

 

·subject to compliance with the applicable provisions of the Merger Agreement, the Iridium Board may, prior to receipt of the required stockholder approval, engage in negotiations and furnish information with regard to any acquisition proposal made by a third party that the Iridium Board determines, in good faith, after consultation with Iridium’s outside legal counsel and financial advisor, constitutes or would reasonably be expected to lead to a superior proposal, and the failure to take any of the foregoing actions would reasonably be expected to violate the directors’ fiduciary duties under applicable law;

 

·subject to its compliance with the applicable provisions of the Merger Agreement, and to a four business day period to negotiate with Rocket Lab with regard to any adjustment to the terms and conditions of

 

75

 

 

the Merger Agreement, the Iridium Board may terminate the Merger Agreement to accept a superior proposal and enter into a definitive agreement with respect to such superior proposal, to the extent that the failure to terminate the Merger Agreement would be reasonably likely to violate the directors’ fiduciary duties under applicable law and subject to payment of a termination fee; and

 

·the termination fee of $223,620,000, which equals approximately 3.75% of the equity value implied in the Merger Consideration, is reasonable in light of the circumstances and the overall terms of the Merger Agreement, and would not discourage acquisition proposals from credible third parties willing and able to make such proposals.

 

Opinion of Iridium’s Financial Advisor. The oral opinion of Evercore rendered to the Iridium Board on June 28, 2026, which was subsequently confirmed in Evercore’s written opinion dated June 28, 2026, that as of the date of such opinion and based upon and subject to the assumptions, limitations, qualifications and conditions described in Evercore’s written opinion, the Merger Consideration to be received by holders of Iridium Common Stock in the First Merger was fair, from a financial point of view, to such holders, as more fully described below in the section entitled “The Mergers—Opinion of Iridium’s Financial Advisor” beginning on page 81 and the full text of the written opinion of Evercore attached as Annex C to this proxy statement;

 

Interim Operating Covenants. The Iridium Board reviewed and considered the restrictions imposed on Iridium’s business and operations during the pendency of the Mergers and concluded that such restrictions are reasonable and not unduly burdensome.

 

Terms of the Merger Agreement. The Iridium Board reviewed and considered the terms of the Merger Agreement, taken as a whole, including the parties’ representations, warranties and covenants, and the circumstances under which the Merger Agreement may be terminated, and concluded that such terms are reasonable to Iridium and Iridium’s stockholders. The Iridium Board noted in particular the likelihood that the First Merger will be consummated, based upon, among other things, the number of conditions to the First Merger, the absence of a financing condition or any condition based upon Rocket Lab stockholder approval, the likelihood of obtaining required regulatory approvals and contractual commitments by Rocket Lab to use its reasonable best efforts to obtain such regulatory approvals and the remedies available under the Merger Agreement to Iridium in the event of any breaches by Rocket Lab.

 

Terms of the Support Agreement. The Iridium Board reviewed the terms and conditions of the Support Agreement, including the fact that (i) the directors and officers who entered into the Support Agreement represent approximately 1.6% of the outstanding shares of Iridium Common Stock as of June 24, 2026 and (ii) that the Support Agreement terminates upon a termination of the Merger Agreement, the effectiveness of any amendment to the Merger Agreement that decreases the Merger Consideration or is otherwise materially adverse to Iridium’s stockholders, or upon the public announcement by Iridium that the Iridium Board has withdrawn, modified or qualified, in any matter adverse to Rocket Lab, its recommendation of the Merger Agreement and the Mergers.

 

Stockholder Approval and Appraisal Rights. The Iridium Board considered the fact that the Mergers would be subject to the required stockholder approval and that Iridium’s stockholders would be free to evaluate the Mergers and vote for or against the adoption of the Merger Agreement at the special meeting and the availability of statutory appraisal rights to Iridium’s stockholders who do not vote in favor of the adoption of the Merger Agreement and otherwise comply with all required procedures applicable to appraisal rights under Section 262 of the DGCL.

 

The Iridium Board also considered a number of potentially negative factors in its deliberations concerning the Merger Agreement, the Mergers and the other transactions contemplated by the Merger Agreement, including the following (not in any relative order of importance):

 

Risks Associated with Regulatory Approval. The Mergers are conditioned on the absence of a legal restraint prohibiting the consummation of the Mergers in certain jurisdictions, the expiration or termination of the waiting period under the HSR Act and the receipt of certain other required regulatory approvals (or, as applicable, the expiration of waiting periods with respect thereto). While each party is required to use reasonable best efforts to take all actions necessary to resolve any objections asserted by a governmental authority with respect to the consummation of the Mergers, and is required to defend and contest any litigation pursued by a governmental authority in objection of the consummation of the Mergers, Rocket Lab is not obligated to accept or agree to certain divestiture or other remedies in obtaining regulatory approval nor is Rocket Lab obligated to compensate Iridium if regulatory approval of the Mergers is not obtained.

 

76

 

 

Risks Associated with Receipt of Rocket Lab Stock as Consideration for the First Merger. The Iridium Board considered several risks associated with the fact that 50% of the Merger Consideration is expected to be paid in Rocket Lab Common Stock (subject to the collar mechanism described herein), including the risk that a significant decrease in the price of Rocket Lab Common Stock on Nasdaq from the date of the Merger Agreement to the effective time could affect both the number of shares and value of Rocket Lab Common Stock that Iridium’s stockholders will receive as part of the Merger Consideration, and the history of significant volatility in the price of Rocket Lab Common Stock on Nasdaq, combined with the fact that Iridium is not permitted to terminate the Merger Agreement solely because of a decline in the trading price of Rocket Lab Common Stock. While the collar mitigates certain of these risks, it does not provide protection against decreases in Rocket Lab’s stock price below the collar, and Iridium’s stockholders will not participate in increases in Rocket Lab’s stock price within the collar.

 

Lack of a Fixed Exchange Ratio. Because the exchange ratio for the common stock consideration is subject to a collar rather than determined pursuant to a fixed exchange ratio, Iridium’s stockholders cannot be certain as to the amount of Rocket Lab stock that they will receive and will be limited in the extent to which they participate in increases in Rocket Lab’s stock price above the collar during the pendency of the Mergers.

 

Interim Operating Covenants. The Iridium Board reviewed and considered the restrictions imposed on Iridium’s business and operations during the pendency of the Mergers (including covenants that Iridium operate in the ordinary course of business and refrain from taking certain actions without Rocket Lab’s consent) and, although it concluded that such restrictions are reasonable and not unduly burdensome, such restrictions may delay or prevent Iridium from undertaking business opportunities that may arise or other actions it could potentially otherwise take with respect to the operations of Iridium pending the consummation of the Mergers

 

Risks Associated with the Pendency of the Mergers. The Iridium Board reviewed and considered the risks and contingencies relating to the announcement and pendency of the Mergers (including the likelihood of litigation or other opposition challenging the Mergers and the other transactions contemplated by the Merger Agreement) and the risks and costs to Iridium if the Mergers are not completed in a timely manner or if the Mergers do not close at all, including potential employee attrition, retention and motivation, the impact on Iridium’s relationships with customers, suppliers, service providers and other third parties and the effect termination of the Merger Agreement may have on the trading price of Iridium Common Stock and Iridium’s operating results.

 

Possible Failure to Integrate. The Iridium Board reviewed and considered the potential challenges and difficulties in integrating the operations of Iridium and Rocket Lab and the risk that operational efficiencies between the two companies, or other anticipated benefits and synergies of the Mergers, might not be realized or might take longer to realize than expected.

 

Possible Deterrence of Acquisition Proposals and Incurrence of a Termination Fee to Terminate the Merger Agreement in Order to Accept a Superior Proposal. The Iridium Board considered:

 

·the restrictions in the Merger Agreement on Iridium’s ability to terminate the Merger Agreement in connection with the receipt of a superior proposal, including the fact that the Iridium Board must (i) provide four business days’ written notice to Rocket Lab of its intention to make an adverse change to its recommendation with respect to the Mergers in order to provide Rocket Lab with an opportunity to match a superior proposal and (ii) if requested by Rocket Lab, negotiate in good faith with Rocket Lab during such period, and the discouraging effect this may have on potential bidders;

 

·the fact that Iridium may be required to pay Rocket Lab a $223,620,000 termination fee under certain circumstances after the date of the Merger Agreement, including if the Iridium Board withdraws its recommendation to Iridium’s stockholders to vote in favor of the adoption of the Merger Agreement and the Mergers or because Iridium materially and intentionally breaches the “no-shop” restrictions in the Merger Agreement; and

 

·the potential effect of the termination fee to deter other potential bidders from making an acquisition proposal for Iridium or acquiring Iridium for twelve months if the Merger Agreement is terminated in certain circumstances.

 

Merger Costs. The Iridium Board considered the significant costs associated with the completion of the Mergers, including Iridium senior management’s time and energy and potential opportunity cost that will be incurred by the combined company as a result of the Mergers.

 

77

 

 

Iridium Will Cease Existing as an Independent Public Company. The Iridium Board considered that Iridium stockholders would lose the opportunity to realize the potential long-term value of the successful execution of Iridium’s current strategy as an independent public company.

 

Tax Treatment of the Merger Consideration. The Iridium Board considered the fact that the tax treatment of any gains arising from the receipt of the Merger Consideration, at least to the extent of the cash component of the Merger Consideration, would generally be taxable to Iridium’s stockholders for U.S. federal income tax purposes.

 

Other Risks. The Iridium Board considered risks of the type and nature described under the sections entitled “Cautionary Note Regarding Forward-Looking Statements” and “Risk Factors” beginning on pages 53 and 23, respectively.

 

The foregoing discussion is not intended to be an exhaustive list of the information and considered by the Iridium Board in its consideration of the Mergers but includes the material positive factors and material negative factors considered by the Iridium Board in that regard. In view of the number and variety of factors, the amount of information considered and the complexity of these matters, the Iridium Board did not find it useful and did not attempt to quantify, rank or assign any relative or specific weights to the various factors that it considered. Individual members of the Iridium Board may have given different weights to different factors. The Iridium Board considered all these factors as a whole, and overall considered the factors to be favorable to, and to support, its unanimous determination.

 

In considering the Iridium Board’s recommendation to adopt the Merger Agreement, Iridium’s stockholders should be aware that the executive officers and directors of Iridium have certain interests in the Mergers that may be different from, or in addition to, the interests of Iridium’s stockholders generally, as more fully described below in the section titled “—Interests of Iridium Directors and Executive Officers in the Mergers.” The Iridium Board was aware of these interests and considered them when adopting the Merger Agreement and recommending that Iridium’s stockholders vote to adopt the Merger Agreement.

 

Certain Iridium Unaudited Prospective Financial Information

 

Other than in connection with Iridium’s regular earnings press releases, Iridium does not, as a matter of course, publicly disclose long-term consolidated forecasts as to future performance, earnings or other results because of, among other reasons, the uncertainty, unpredictability and subjectivity of the underlying assumptions and estimates underlying such forecasts. In the course of evaluating the Mergers and strategic alternatives thereto, Iridium’s management prepared certain unaudited financial projections regarding Iridium’s future performance for the second fiscal half of 2026 and the fiscal years 2027 through fiscal year 2030 on a standalone basis. A preliminary version of these projections (the “initial Iridium management forecast”) was initially made available to Rocket Lab on February 12, 2026 at its request in connection with Rocket Lab’s due diligence review of Iridium. The initial Iridium management forecast was subsequently revised including (1) to reflect illustrative impacts of the Aireon Transaction (the “Iridium/Aireon management forecast”) and certain other matters described in the section in this proxy statement/prospectus titled “—Background of the Mergers” beginning on page 64 and (2) to prepare a version of the Iridium/Aireon management forecast that extended into fiscal year 2035 to account for capital expenditure for expected constellation upgrades (the “Iridium extended period management forecast” and, collectively with the initial Iridium management forecast and the Iridium/Aireon management forecast, the “Iridium unaudited prospective financial information”). The Iridium extended period management forecast was identical to the Iridium/Aireon management forecast except that the Iridium extended period management forecast included an additional extended projection period for fiscal years 2031 through 2035. Iridium provided, and the Iridium Board approved, the Iridium extended period management forecast for Evercore’s use, in connection with Evercore’s financial analyses and opinion (see the sections described above in this proxy statement/prospectus titled “The Mergers—Opinion of Iridium’s Financial Advisor” beginning on page 81 of this proxy statement/prospectus). The Iridium/Aireon management forecast was also made available to Rocket Lab at its request in connection with Rocket Lab’s due diligence review of Iridium. The Iridium extended period management forecast was not provided to Rocket Lab. For more information on the preparation and use of the Iridium unaudited prospective financial information, see the section described above in this proxy statement/prospectus titled “—Background of the Mergers” beginning on page 64.

 

The summaries of the Iridium unaudited prospective financial information are included in this proxy statement/prospectus to give Iridium’s stockholders access to non-public information that was provided to the Iridium Board, Evercore and Rocket Lab as described above, and are not intended to influence your decision whether to vote in

 

78

 

 

favor of the Merger Agreement proposal or any other proposal at the special meeting. The inclusion of the Iridium unaudited prospective financial information should not be regarded as an indication that any of Iridium or its advisors or other representatives or any other recipient of this information considered, or now considers, this information to be necessarily predictive of actual future performance or events, or that it should be construed as financial guidance, and the Iridium unaudited prospective financial information forth below should not be relied on as such.

 

While presented with numeric specificity, the Iridium unaudited prospective financial information reflects numerous estimates and assumptions that are inherently uncertain and may be beyond the control of Iridium, including, among others, Iridium’s assumptions about Iridium’s goals and strategies; Iridium’s future business development, financial condition and results of operations; uncertainties regarding customer demand for Iridium’s products and services, including demand from the U.S. government; Iridium’s ability to maintain the health, capacity and content of its satellite constellation; the development of and market for Iridium’s products and services; increased competition; changes in trade policy, including tariff rates, as well as general industry and economic conditions; and legal, governmental and technological factors and other matters described in the sections titled “Cautionary Note Regarding Forward-Looking Statements”, “Where You Can Find More Information”, and “Risk Factors”, beginning on pages 53, 149 and 23, respectively. The foregoing is a summary of certain key assumptions and estimates and does not purport to be a comprehensive overview of all assumptions and estimates reflected in the Iridium unaudited prospective financial information. The Iridium unaudited prospective financial information reflects both assumptions as to certain business decisions that are subject to change and, in many respects, subjective judgment, and thus is susceptible to multiple interpretations and periodic revisions based on actual performance and business developments. Iridium can give no assurance that the Iridium unaudited prospective financial information and the underlying estimates and assumptions will be realized. In addition, since the Iridium unaudited prospective financial information covers multiple years, such information by its nature becomes more speculative with each successive year. This information constitutes “forward-looking statements” and actual results may differ materially and adversely from those projected.

 

The Iridium unaudited prospective financial information was not prepared with a view toward compliance with published guidelines of the SEC regarding projections or GAAP or the guidelines established by the American Institute of Certified Public Accountants for preparation or presentation of prospective financial information. Neither KPMG LLP, Iridium’s independent registered public accounting firm, nor any other independent accountants, has audited, reviewed, examined, compiled or applied agreed-upon procedures with respect to the Iridium unaudited prospective financial information and accordingly, neither KPMG LLP nor any other independent accountants expresses an opinion or any other form of assurance with respect thereto. The reports of KPMG LLP incorporated by reference into this proxy statement/prospectus relate to Iridium’s previously issued financial statements. They do not extend to the Iridium unaudited prospective financial information and should not be read to do so.

 

The Iridium unaudited prospective financial information includes certain financial measures which are each a “non-GAAP financial measure,” meaning that they are financial performance measures that are not calculated in accordance with GAAP. The non-GAAP financial measures used in the Iridium unaudited prospective financial information were relied upon by Evercore for purposes of its opinion and by the Iridium Board in connection with its evaluation of the Mergers. Please see the table below for a description of how Iridium defines these non-GAAP financial measures for purposes of the Iridium unaudited prospective financial information in this section. The SEC rules which would otherwise require a reconciliation of a non-GAAP financial measure to a GAAP financial measure do not apply to non-GAAP financial measures included in disclosures relating to a proposed business combination such as the Mergers if the disclosure is included in a document such as this proxy statement/prospectus. In addition, reconciliations of non-GAAP financial measures were not relied upon by Evercore for purposes of its opinion or by the Iridium Board in connection with its evaluation of the Mergers. Accordingly, Iridium has not provided a reconciliation of the financial measures included in the Iridium unaudited prospective financial information to the relevant GAAP financial measures. Non-GAAP financial measures should not be considered in isolation from, or as a substitute for, financial information presented in compliance with GAAP, and non-GAAP financial measures as used by Iridium may not be comparable to similarly titled amounts used by other companies. Furthermore, there are limitations inherent in non-GAAP financial measures because they exclude charges and credits that are required to be included in a GAAP presentation. Accordingly, this non-GAAP financial measure should be considered together with, and not as an alternative to, financial measures prepared in accordance with GAAP.

The Iridium unaudited prospective financial information does not take into account all the possible financial and other effects on Iridium of the Mergers, the effect on Iridium of any business or strategic decision or action that has been or will be taken as a result of the Merger Agreement having been executed, or the effect of any business or strategic decisions or actions that would likely have been taken if the Merger Agreement had not been executed, but which were instead altered, accelerated, postponed or not taken in anticipation of the Mergers. Opinion of Iridium’s Financial Advisor

 

Iridium retained Evercore to act as financial advisor in connection with the proposed Mergers. As part of this engagement, the Iridium Board requested that Evercore evaluate the fairness to the holders of Iridium Common Stock, from a financial point of view, of the Merger Consideration to be received by such holders in the First Merger. At a meeting of the Iridium Board held on June 28, 2026, Evercore rendered to the Iridium Board its oral opinion, subsequently confirmed by delivery of a written opinion dated June 28, 2026, that, as of the date of such opinion and based upon and subject to the assumptions, limitations, qualifications and conditions described in Evercore’s written opinion, the Merger Consideration to be received by holders of Iridium Common Stock in the First Merger was fair, from a financial point of view, to such holders.

 

The full text of the written opinion of Evercore, dated June 28, 2026, which sets forth, among other things, the procedures followed, assumptions made, matters considered and qualifications and limitations on the scope of review undertaken in rendering its opinion, is attached as Annex C and is incorporated herein by reference into this proxy statement/prospectus in its entirety. The summary of the opinion of Evercore in this proxy statement/prospectus is qualified in its entirety by reference to the full text of the written opinion. You are urged to read Evercore’s opinion carefully and in its entirety. Evercore’s opinion was addressed to, and provided for the information and benefit of, the Iridium Board (in its capacity as such) in connection with its evaluation of the proposed Mergers. The opinion does not constitute a recommendation to the Iridium Board or to any other persons in respect of the Mergers, including as to how any holder of shares of Iridium Common Stock should vote or act in respect of the Mergers. Evercore’s opinion does not address the relative merits of the Mergers as compared to other business or financial strategies that might be available to Iridium, nor does it address the underlying business decision of Iridium to engage in the Mergers. 

 

In connection with rendering its opinion, Evercore, among other things:

 

·reviewed certain publicly available business and financial information relating to Iridium and Rocket Lab that Evercore deemed to be relevant, including publicly available research analysts’ estimates;

 

·reviewed certain internal projected financial data relating to Iridium prepared and furnished to Evercore by the management of Iridium, as approved for Evercore’s use by Iridium (the “Iridium Forecasts”);

 

·reviewed certain publicly available financial forecasts relating to Rocket Lab as approved for Evercore’s use by Iridium (the “Rocket Lab Public Forecasts” and, together with the Iridium Forecasts, the “Forecasts”);

 

·discussed with management of Iridium their assessment of the past and current operations of Iridium and Rocket Lab, the current financial condition and prospects of Iridium and Rocket Lab, and the Forecasts;

 

·discussed with management of Rocket Lab publicly available information relating to the past and current operations of Rocket Lab and the current financial condition and prospects of Rocket Lab;

 

·reviewed the reported prices and the historical trading activity of Iridium Common Stock and Rocket Lab Common Stock;

 

81

 

 

·compared the financial performance of Iridium and Rocket Lab and their respective stock market trading multiples with those of certain other publicly traded companies that Evercore deemed relevant;

 

·compared the financial performance of Iridium and the valuation multiples relating to the Mergers with the financial terms, to the extent publicly available, of certain other transactions that Evercore deemed relevant;

 

·reviewed the financial terms and conditions of a draft, dated June 28, 2026 of the Merger Agreement; and

 

·performed such other analyses and examinations and considered such other factors that Evercore deemed appropriate.

 

For purposes of Evercore’s analysis and opinion, Evercore assumed and relied upon the accuracy and completeness of the financial and other information publicly available, and all of the information supplied or otherwise made available to, discussed with, or reviewed by Evercore, without any independent verification of such information (and Evercore did not assume responsibility or liability for any independent verification of such information), and further relied upon the assurances of the management of Iridium that they were not aware of any facts or circumstances that would make such information inaccurate or misleading. With respect to the Iridium Forecasts, Evercore assumed with the consent of the Iridium Board that they were reasonably prepared on bases reflecting the best currently available estimates and good faith judgments of the management of Iridium as to the future financial performance of Iridium. In addition, as the Iridium Board was aware, Evercore was not provided with, and it did not have access to financial forecasts for Rocket Lab prepared by the management of Rocket Lab. Accordingly, with the consent of the Iridium Board, Evercore assumed that the Rocket Lab Public Forecasts provided a reasonable basis upon which to evaluate the future financial performance of Rocket Lab and Evercore relied on the Rocket Lab Public Forecasts in performing its analyses. Evercore expressed no view as to the Forecasts or the assumptions on which they were based.

 

For purposes of Evercore’s analysis and opinion, Evercore assumed, in all respects material to its analysis, that the final executed Merger Agreement would not differ from the draft Merger Agreement reviewed by Evercore, that the representations and warranties of each party contained in the Merger Agreement were true and correct, that each party would perform all of the covenants and agreements required to be performed by it under the Merger Agreement and that all conditions to the consummation of the Mergers would be satisfied without waiver or modification thereof. Evercore further assumed, in all respects material to its analysis, that all governmental, regulatory or other consents, approvals or releases necessary for the consummation of the Mergers would be obtained without any delay, limitation, restriction or condition that would have an adverse effect on Iridium, Rocket Lab or the consummation of the Mergers or reduce the contemplated benefits to the holders of Iridium Common Stock of the Mergers.

 

Evercore did not conduct a physical inspection of the properties or facilities of Iridium or Rocket Lab and did not make or assume any responsibility for making any independent valuation or appraisal of the assets or liabilities (including any contingent, derivative or other off-balance sheet assets and liabilities) of Iridium or Rocket Lab, nor was Evercore furnished with any such valuations or appraisals, nor did Evercore evaluate the solvency or fair value of Iridium or Rocket Lab under any state or federal laws relating to bankruptcy, insolvency or similar matters. Evercore’s opinion was necessarily based upon information made available to Evercore as of the date of its opinion and financial, economic, market and other conditions as they existed and as could be evaluated on the date of its opinion. Developments subsequent to Evercore’s opinion could affect its opinion and Evercore did not and does not have any obligation to update, revise or reaffirm its opinion.

 

Evercore was not asked to pass upon, and expressed no opinion with respect to, any matter other than the fairness to the holders of Iridium Common Stock, from a financial point of view, of the Merger Consideration. Evercore did not express any view on, and its opinion did not address, the fairness of the proposed transaction to, or any consideration received in connection therewith by, the holders of any other class of securities, creditors or other constituencies of Iridium, nor as to the fairness of the amount or nature of any compensation to be paid or payable to any of the officers, directors or employees of Iridium, or any class of such persons, whether relative to the Merger Consideration or otherwise. Discounted Cash Flow Analysis

 

Evercore performed a discounted cash flow analysis of Iridium to calculate the estimated present value of the unlevered, after-tax free cash flows that Iridium was forecasted to generate during Iridium’s fiscal years 2026 through 2035 based on the Iridium Forecasts. Evercore calculated terminal values for Iridium by applying a range of perpetuity growth rates of 2.5% to 3.5%, which range was selected by Evercore based on Evercore’s professional judgment and experience, to estimate the unlevered, after-tax free cash flows that Iridium was forecasted to generate in the terminal year based on the Iridium Forecasts.

 

The cash flows and terminal values, in each case, were then discounted to present value as of June 30, 2026, using discount rates ranging from 9.0% to 10.0%, representing an estimate of Iridium’s weighted average cost of capital, to derive a range of implied enterprise values for Iridium. Based on these ranges of implied enterprise

values, Iridium’s estimated net debt as of June 30, 2026, the present value of Iridium net operating losses and R&D tax credit benefits (calculated using a discount rate of 11.0%, which was based on an estimate of Iridium’s cost of equity, as estimated by Evercore based on its professional judgment and experience) and the number of fully diluted shares of Iridium Common Stock, in each case as provided to Evercore by Iridium’s management, this analysis indicated a range of implied equity values per Iridium Common Stock of $29.97 to $45.54 compared to the closing price of Iridium Common Stock of $28.52 per share on April 1, 2026 (the last trading day prior to a report by Financial Times regarding the Amazon-Globalstar Transaction), the closing price per share of Iridium Common Stock of $43.52 on June 26, 2026, and the implied value of the Merger Consideration of $54.00 per share of Iridium Common Stock.

Present Value of Future Share Price Analysis

 

Evercore performed an illustrative analysis of the implied present value of the future price per share of Rocket Lab Common Stock, which is designed to provide an indication of the present value of a theoretical future value of Rocket Lab as a function of Rocket Lab’s estimated future revenue and its assumed multiple of enterprise value to LTM revenue.

 

In calculating the implied present value of the future price per share of Rocket Lab Common Stock, Evercore first calculated ranges of implied enterprise values of Rocket Lab by multiplying Rocket Lab’s estimated LTM revenue as of the end of calendar year 2031, based on the Rocket Lab Public Forecasts by an illustrative enterprise value to LTM revenue multiple range of 20.0x to 40.0x, which range was selected based on Evercore’s professional judgment and experience, to derive an implied future enterprise value reference range for Rocket Lab. Evercore then added to this range of implied enterprise values Rocket Lab’s net cash, in each case, as based on the Rocket Lab Public Forecasts, to calculate a reference range of implied future equity values for Rocket Lab. Evercore then divided the implied future equity values of Rocket Lab by an estimate of the number of fully diluted outstanding shares of Rocket Lab Common Stock as of the end of calendar year 2031 to calculate a reference range of implied future equity values per share for Rocket Lab. Evercore then discounted the implied future equity values per share to June 30, 2026 using discount rates ranging from 15.0% to 18.0%, which were based on an estimate of Rocket Lab’s cost of equity, as estimated by Evercore based on its professional judgment and experience. This analysis indicated a range of implied equity values per share of Rocket Lab Common Stock of $46.23 to $102.45, compared to the closing price of Rocket Lab Common Stock of $84.54 on June 26, 2026.

Interests of Iridium Directors and Executive Officers in the Mergers

 

In considering the recommendation of the Iridium Board to approve the Merger Agreement Proposal, Iridium stockholders should be aware that Iridium’s directors and executive officers have interests in the Mergers that may be different from, or in addition to, those of Iridium stockholders generally and that may create a potential conflict of interest. The Iridium Board was aware of and considered these interests, among other matters, in evaluating and negotiating the Merger Agreement and the Mergers, in approving the Merger Agreement, and in recommending the approval of the Merger Agreement by Iridium stockholders. Iridium stockholders should take these interests into account in deciding whether to vote “FOR” the Merger Agreement Proposal. These interests are described below, and certain of them are quantified within the narrative disclosure. The Mergers will constitute a “change in control” for purposes of the compensation arrangements described below. The amounts presented in the following discussion do not reflect the impact of applicable withholding or other taxes. Treatment of Iridium Equity Awards Held by Iridium’s Directors and Executive Officers

 

The treatment of outstanding Iridium equity awards held by Iridium’s non-employee directors and executive officers in connection with the Mergers is described below.

 

The summary below sets forth the treatment of Iridium equity awards held by Iridium’s directors and executive officers under the Merger Agreement.

 

·Iridium RSU Awards and Iridium PSU Awards. Each Iridium RSU Award and Iridium PSU Award that is outstanding immediately prior to the First Effective Time will be assumed by Rocket Lab and converted into an Assumed Iridium RSU Award subject to the same terms and conditions as applied to the applicable Iridium RSU Award or Iridium PSU Award immediately prior to the First Effective Time (including the same vesting and leaver provisions), except that each such Assumed Iridium RSU Award will cover a whole number of shares of Rocket Lab Common Stock equal to the number of shares of Iridium Common Stock covered by such Iridium RSU Award or Iridium PSU Award immediately prior to the First Effective Time (which, in the case of Iridium PSU Awards, will assume satisfaction of applicable performance-based vesting conditions at target levels) multiplied by the Equity Award Exchange Ratio (with the result rounded down to the nearest whole share), and each Assumed Iridium RSU Award will vest in full in the event of a termination of employment without cause within 12 months following the First Effective Time (in addition to any other provisions that apply to the corresponding Iridium RSU Award or Iridium PSU Award, including under the Severance Plan).

 

·Iridium Option Awards. Each Iridium Option Award that is outstanding and unexercised immediately prior to the First Effective Time will be fully vested and exercisable and canceled and converted into the right to receive the Merger Consideration in respect of each share of Iridium Common Stock covered by such Iridium Option Award, calculated net of the exercise price or strike price, as applicable, less applicable withholdings.

 

In addition, under the terms of Iridium’s non-employee director compensation program, upon a termination of service other than for cause, a director’s unvested Iridium RSUs will vest on a pro-rata basis, based on the number of partial and full calendar quarters served in the year of termination. Further, certain non-employee directors have elected to defer settlement of vested Iridium RSUs, the terms of which provide for settlement upon the earlier of a termination of service or a change in control of Iridium.

 

No Iridium executive officer or director holds Iridium CSAR Awards. Ms. McBride is the only executive officer or director who holds Iridium Options, all of which are fully vested.

 

The estimated aggregate value (on a pre-tax basis) of the Iridium equity awards held by the executive officers who are not named executive officers in the event of a qualifying termination following the Mergers is $8,223,626. The estimated aggregate value of the Iridium equity awards held by Iridium’s non-employee directors upon a termination of service following the Mergers (including pro-rata vesting of unvested Iridium RSU Awards and settlement of vested and deferred Iridium RSU Awards) is $37,711,442.

Executive Severance Arrangements

 

Executive Severance Plan

 

Each of Iridium’s executive officers is a participant in the Severance Plan, under which, if an executive officer’s employment is terminated by Iridium (or a successor) without “cause” or by the executive with “good reason” (each as defined in the Severance Plan), either within the three months prior to, or 24 months following, a change in control of Iridium, he or she will receive the following payments and benefits, subject to the executive’s execution and non-revocation of a release of claims and compliance with any applicable restrictive covenants:

 

·a cash amount equal to the sum of the (i) the executive officer’s then-current base salary and (ii) then-current target annual bonus opportunity, multiplied by 1.5X (2X in the case of Mr. Desch), paid in a lump sum;

 

·an annual target bonus for the year in which the termination occurs, paid in a lump sum;

 

·payment of COBRA premiums for the executive officer and his or her eligible dependents for a period of up to 12 months; and

 

·accelerated vesting of all outstanding Iridium equity awards (with applicable performance conditions deemed satisfied in accordance with the applicable award agreement).

 

The Severance Plan also provides that if an executive officer would be subject to an excise tax under Section 4999 of the Code, the benefits to such executive will be reduced to the amount that does not trigger the excise tax, unless the executive would retain greater value (on an after-tax basis) by receiving all benefits and paying the applicable excise, income and payroll taxes.

 

The aggregate value of the cash severance payments and benefits (not including accelerated vesting of equity awards, which amounts are provided under “—Treatment of Iridium Equity Awards” above) that would be paid or become payable to the executive officers who are not named executive officers if they all experienced a qualifying termination of employment at the First Effective Time would have been approximately $2,629,853. See the section titled “—Quantification of Potential Payments and Benefits to Iridium’s Named Executive Officers in Connection with the Mergers” beginning on page 93 for the estimated amounts that each of the named executive officers would receive under the Severance Plan upon a qualifying termination in connection with the Mergers.

 

Quantification

 

See the section titled “—Quantification of Potential Payments and Benefits to Iridium’s Named Executive Officers in Connection with the Mergers” beginning on page 93 below for the estimated severance amounts for each named executive officer.

 

Retention Program

 

Under the Merger Agreement, Iridium may establish a cash-based retention program (the “Retention Program”) and may grant awards thereunder to certain employees, including certain executive officers. Awards granted under the Retention Program will vest and be payable as to 60% of the award at the Closing and the remaining 40% of the award will vest and be payable on the six-month anniversary of the Closing, subject to continued employment through the applicable vesting date, except as described below. In the event the Merger Agreement is terminated and the Mergers are not consummated, 100% of the retention award will vest and become payable on the later of such date or June 28, 2027. In the event of a recipient’s termination of employment prior to the Closing under circumstances that would make them eligible for severance under an applicable severance plan, policy or arrangement, the recipient will receive payment of the first 60% portion of the award, and if such termination occurs on or after the Closing, then the recipient will receive payment of the second 40% portion of the award. As of the date of this proxy statement/prospectus, Iridium has not granted any retention awards to executive officers who are not named executive officers. See the section titled “—Quantification of Potential Payments and Benefits to Iridium’s Named Executive Officers in Connection with the Mergers” beginning on page 93 for the retention awards payable to the named executive officers as of the date of this proxy statement/prospectus.

280G Mitigation Actions

 

Prior to the Closing, Iridium, in consultation with Rocket Lab, may implement the following strategies to mitigate any issues resulting from the application of Sections 280G and 4999 of the Code: (i) entering into and/or valuing the restrictive covenants applicable to any individual, (ii) the acceleration into a prior year, to the extent permissible under Section 409A of the Code, of compensation that otherwise would vest or become payable at or prior to the First Effective Time and (iii) amending or entering into agreements to incorporate “best after tax cutback” provisions. Any such tax planning strategies will not include a gross-up of any excise taxes under Section 4999 of the Code. As of the date of this proxy statement/prospectus, the implementation of any such tax planning strategies has not been determined.

 

Indemnification and Insurance

 

The Merger Agreement provides certain continuation rights with respect to directors’ and officers’ liability insurance for the executive officers and non-employee directors of Iridium intended to provide for continued coverage for at least six years following the First Effective Time.

 

New Compensation Arrangements with Rocket Lab

 

Any Iridium executive officers and directors who become officers, directors or employees of Rocket Lab or who otherwise are retained by Rocket Lab to provide services may enter into new individualized compensation arrangements effective as of the First Effective Time and may participate following the First Effective Time in cash or equity incentive or other benefit plans maintained by Rocket Lab or any of its affiliates. As of the date of this proxy statement/prospectus, no compensation arrangements between such persons and Rocket Lab and/or its affiliates have been established or discussed.
