Director and Officer Indemnification

 

Under the Merger Agreement, certain indemnification and insurance rights exist in favor of the current and former directors and officers of Iridium and its subsidiaries, including rights to continued indemnification and to coverage under directors’ and officers’ liability insurance for a specified period following the completion of the Mergers. For more information about these rights, see the section titled “The Mergers—Interests of Iridium Directors and Executive Officers in the Mergers—Indemnification and Insurance” beginning on page 93.

 

Accounting Treatment of the Mergers

 

Rocket Lab and Iridium prepare their respective financial statements in accordance with GAAP. The Mergers will be accounted for as a business combination, with Rocket Lab as the accounting acquirer and Iridium as the accounting acquiree, using the acquisition method of accounting in accordance with Accounting Standards Codification 805, Business Combinations. Rocket Lab has been determined to be the accounting acquirer based on the Merger Consideration and composition of the Rocket Lab Board following the Mergers. The acquisition method of accounting will generally result in the recognition of Iridium’s assets acquired and liabilities assumed at their estimated fair values as of the date of the completion of the Mergers. The excess of the consideration transferred over the identifiable net assets acquired will be allocated to goodwill.

 

Regulatory Approvals Required for the Mergers

 

Completion of the Mergers is subject to the satisfaction or waiver of certain regulatory conditions, including the receipt of the required approval of the FCC and the receipt of certain other required regulatory approvals. Iridium and Rocket Lab have agreed to use their respective reasonable best efforts to obtain all regulatory approvals required to consummate the Mergers.

 

Antitrust. Under the HSR Act and the rules promulgated thereunder, the Mergers may not be completed until notification and report forms have been filed with the Antitrust Division of the U.S. Department of Justice (the “Antitrust Division”) and the FTC and the applicable waiting period has expired or been terminated. Iridium and

 

96

 

 

Rocket Lab are required under the Merger Agreement to file their respective HSR Act notification and report forms within ten business days after the date of the Merger Agreement, and to request early termination of the applicable waiting period. Iridium and Rocket Lab filed their respective notification and report forms under the HSR Act on July 13, 2026, and requested early termination of the waiting period. The applicable waiting period under the HSR Act expired at 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time on August 12, 2026. At any time before or after the Mergers are completed, notwithstanding the expiration of the applicable waiting period under the HSR Act, the Antitrust Division, the FTC or others could take action under the antitrust laws, including seeking to enjoin the completion of the Mergers, to rescind the Mergers or to require the divestiture of assets of Rocket Lab, Iridium or their respective subsidiaries.

  

Communications Laws; FCC. Because Iridium and its subsidiaries hold licenses and authorizations issued by the FCC, the completion of the Mergers requires the prior consent of the FCC to the transfer of control of those licenses and authorizations, including Iridium’s space station authorization, gateway earth station authorizations, blanket earth station authorizations, experimental authorizations and international Section 214 authorization. Under the Merger Agreement, Iridium and Rocket Lab are required to make the appropriate filings with the FCC within 30 business days after the date of the Merger Agreement. Iridium and Rocket Lab filed the applicable FCC applications on August 10, 2026. In connection with its review, the FCC may refer the transaction to the Committee for the Assessment of Foreign Participation in the United States Telecommunications Services Sector, commonly known as “Team Telecom,” which reviews national security and law enforcement concerns that may be raised by foreign participation in the U.S. telecommunications services sector, and if Team Telecom requests that conditions be imposed on the parties, the approval of Team Telecom is also required. The Mergers also require compliance with, and filings, registrations or notifications under, other applicable Satellite and Communications Laws, including with the International Telecommunication Union.

 

Foreign telecommunications and investment approvals. The completion of the Mergers is also conditioned on the receipt of specified regulatory approvals relating to the transfer or continued effectiveness of certain of Iridium’s non-U.S. telecommunications licenses and authorizations, and specified foreign investment approvals, in each case as set forth in the Merger Agreement. These include approvals, to the extent required by applicable law, relating to Iridium’s telecommunications licenses and authorizations in Chile, France, Spain, Switzerland and the United Arab Emirates, and, solely to the extent the relevant governmental authority affirmatively confirms that its approval is required prior to the completion of the Mergers, in Australia, New Zealand and the United Kingdom. In addition, the Mergers are subject to the receipt of approvals under the foreign investment laws of Australia, New Zealand and the United Kingdom, and, to the extent required as a result of changes in applicable law after the date of the Merger Agreement, Canada. Under the Merger Agreement, the parties are required to make the filings necessary to obtain these approvals within 60 business days after the date of the Merger Agreement, or, for other required notifications and filings under applicable competition laws, foreign investment laws and Satellite and Communications Laws, as promptly as practicable after the date of the Merger Agreement and in any event within the required statutory periods.

 

National security; facility clearances. Iridium, Rocket Lab and/or certain of their respective subsidiaries hold facility security clearances subject to the NISPOM, which is administered by the U.S. Department of War, Defense Counterintelligence and Security Agency (the “DCSA”). If the DCSA requests that Rocket Lab, Iridium or any of Iridium’s subsidiaries enter into a written commitment to mitigate or negate any foreign ownership, control or influence arising as a result of the Mergers, completion of the Mergers is conditioned on either the DCSA’s written acknowledgment that it has accepted a foreign ownership, control or influence mitigation plan proposed by Rocket Lab, or the execution and delivery to the DCSA of the requested commitment notice or commitment letter.

 

Efforts; divestitures. Iridium and Rocket Lab have agreed to use their respective reasonable best efforts to obtain the Required Regulatory Approvals as promptly as practicable, and Rocket Lab, after consulting with and considering in good faith the views of Iridium, has final decision-making authority with respect to the strategy for obtaining those approvals. If objections are asserted by a governmental authority, or a proceeding is instituted or threatened challenging the Mergers, the parties have agreed to use reasonable best efforts to resolve such objections, including, if requested by Rocket Lab, agreeing to hold separate, divest or license assets, terminate or modify existing relationships, or accept limitations on the conduct of their respective businesses (each, a “Divestiture Action”), and to defend against any such proceeding through litigation and pursue all avenues of administrative and judicial appeal. However, Rocket Lab is not required to take, agree to or propose any Divestiture Action that

 

97

 

 

(i) would reasonably be expected to be material to Iridium and its subsidiaries, taken as a whole, to Rocket Lab and its subsidiaries, taken as a whole, or to the Combined Company following the Mergers, taken as a whole, and (ii) is not conditioned on the completion of the Mergers. Iridium may not take, agree to or propose any Divestiture Action without Rocket Lab’s prior written consent, and at Rocket Lab’s request Iridium is required to agree to a Divestiture Action so long as it is conditioned on the completion of the Mergers. Rocket Lab is responsible for all filing fees payable to governmental authorities in connection with these regulatory filings.

 

Neither Iridium nor Rocket Lab can provide any assurance that the Required Regulatory Approvals will be obtained, or that they will be obtained without the imposition of conditions, or as to the timing of any such approvals. See “Risk Factors—Risks Relating to the Mergers” beginning on page 23 and “The Merger Agreement—Regulatory Undertakings” beginning on page 124.

 

Financing the Mergers

 

Rocket Lab intends to fund the cash component of the Merger Consideration through a combination of cash from its balance sheet and other debt and equity financing sources. Iridium’s obligations to complete the Mergers are not conditioned on Rocket Lab obtaining any financing.

 

Bridge Facility

 

The Bridge Facility will be available in a single drawing on the Closing Date (as defined in the Commitment Letter) and the proceeds will be used to finance the Cash Consideration to holders of Iridium Common Stock in the Mergers, to refinance the Iridium Credit Agreement and for other purposes not prohibited by the Commitment Letter.

 

The terms of the Bridge Facility will be set forth in definitive loan documentation that will be consistent with the Commitment Letter. The Bridge Facility will also be subject to affirmative and negative covenants, events of default and other customary terms consistent with the specified documentation standards.

 

The Commitment Letter provides that, on or prior to the Closing Date, the commitments under the Bridge Facility, or, to the extent funded after the Closing Date, the loans under the Bridge Facility, will be reduced or prepaid, as applicable, with proceeds from the Debt Financing or Equity Financing.

 

Termination of Iridium’s Existing Debt

 

In connection with the Mergers, the parties intend to terminate and payoff the commitments and outstanding indebtedness under each of the Aireon Credit Agreement and the Aireon Seller Loan Agreement.

 

In connection with the Commitment Letter, Rocket Lab may elect to amend the Iridium Credit Agreement to, among other things, permit the existing loans thereunder to remain outstanding after the consummation of the Mergers. To the extent that such amendment is not elected by Rocket Lab or the lenders under the Iridium Credit Agreement do not consent to such amendments, Rocket Lab expects to repay the loans under the Iridium Credit Agreement at Closing with proceeds from the Bridge Facility, Debt Financing or Equity Financing or a combination thereof. The terms and timing of any such transactions have not been determined as of August 26, 2026, the date of this proxy statement/prospectus.

 

Appraisal Rights in the Mergers

 

Record holders and beneficial owners of Iridium Common Stock who comply with the procedures set forth in Section 262 and summarized below will be entitled to appraisal rights if the First Merger is completed. Under Section 262 of the DGCL, record holders and beneficial owners of shares of Iridium Common Stock with respect to which appraisal rights are properly demanded and perfected and not withdrawn or lost are entitled to have such shares of Iridium Common Stock appraised by the Delaware Court of Chancery. Shares of Iridium Common Stock held by record holders and beneficial owners who properly exercise appraisal rights in accordance with Section 262 of the DGCL will not be converted into the right to receive the Merger Consideration, but instead will be canceled and represent the right to receive, in lieu of the Merger Consideration, a cash payment that is equal to the fair value of their shares of Iridium Common Stock at the First Effective Time (exclusive of any element of value arising from the accomplishment or expectation of the First Merger), as determined by the Delaware Court of Chancery, together with interest, if any as determined in accordance with Section 262 of the DGCL (the “appraisal payment”). The fair value of such shares of Iridium Common Stock could be more than, less than or equal to the Merger Consideration. Iridium is required to send a notice to that effect to each record holder, as of the record date for giving notice of the

 

98

 

 

special meeting, of Iridium Common Stock not less than 20 days prior to the special meeting and include in the notice a copy of Section 262 of the DGCL or information directing the stockholders to a publicly available electronic resource at which Section 262 of the DGCL may be accessed without subscription or cost. This proxy statement/prospectus constitutes Iridium’s notice to the record holders of Iridium Common Stock that appraisal rights are available in connection with the First Merger, and the full text of Section 262 of the DGCL may be accessed without subscription or cost at the following publicly available website: https://delcode.delaware.gov/title8/c001/sc09/index.html#262.

 

The following is intended as a brief summary of the material provisions of Section 262 of the DGCL, which sets forth the procedures for demanding statutory appraisal rights. This summary, however, is not a complete statement of the applicable requirements, and is qualified in its entirety by reference to Section 262 of the DGCL. All references in Section 262 of the DGCL to “stockholder” and in this summary to a “stockholder” or “holder” are to the record holder of shares of Iridium Common Stock, all such references to a “beneficial owner” are to a person who is the beneficial owner of Iridium Common Stock held either in voting trust or by a nominee on behalf of such person and all such references to “person” means any individual, corporation, partnership, unincorporated association or other entity. If you wish to consider exercising your appraisal rights, you should carefully review the text of Section 262 of the DGCL. Failure to comply timely and properly with the requirements of Section 262 of the DGCL may result in the loss of your appraisal rights under the DGCL. This notice does not constitute any legal or other advice, nor does it constitute a recommendation that holders or beneficial owners of Iridium Common Stock exercise their appraisal rights under Section 262 of the DGCL. YOU ARE STRONGLY ENCOURAGED TO CONSULT A LEGAL ADVISOR BEFORE ATTEMPTING TO EXERCISE YOUR APPRAISAL RIGHTS.

 

Record holders and beneficial owners of Iridium Common Stock who desire to exercise their appraisal rights must do all of the following: (i) not vote in favor of the adoption of the Merger Agreement, (ii) deliver in the manner set forth below a written demand for appraisal of such holder’s or beneficial owner’s shares of Iridium Common Stock to the Secretary of Iridium before the vote on the Merger Agreement Proposal at the special meeting is taken, (iii) continuously hold of record or beneficially own, as applicable, such shares of Iridium Common Stock from the date of making the demand through completion of the First Merger and (iv) otherwise comply with the requirements of Section 262 of the DGCL. A vote against the merger proposal will not be sufficient to perfect your rights to appraisal without complying with the other procedures described herein.

 

A demand for appraisal must be executed by or for the holder of record or beneficial owner, as applicable. The demand should set forth, fully and correctly, the person’s identity and that the stockholder intends thereby to demand the appraisal of such stockholder’s shares.

 

As required by Section 262 of the DGCL, a demand for appraisal must be in writing and must reasonably inform Iridium of the identity of the record holder or beneficial owner and of such holder’s or beneficial owner’s intention to seek appraisal of the holder’s or beneficial owner’s shares.

 

Record holders and beneficial owners of Iridium Common Stock who elect to demand appraisal of their shares must mail or deliver their written demand to:

 

Iridium Communications Inc.

1676 International Drive Suite 1100

McLean, VA 22102

Attention: Kathleen A. Morgan

 

The written demand for appraisal should specify the stockholder’s name and mailing address. In addition, in the case of a demand for appraisal of a beneficial owner, the demand must also (1) reasonably identify the holder of record of the shares for which the demand is made, (2) be accompanied by documentary evidence of the beneficial owner’s ownership of stock (such as a brokerage or securities account statement containing such information or a letter from the broker or other record holder of such shares confirming such information) and a statement that such documentary evidence is a true and correct copy of what it purports to be and (3) provide an address at which such beneficial owner consents to receive notices given by the surviving corporation under Section 262 of the DGCL and the verified list required by subsection (f) of Section 262 of the DGCL (discussed further below). Whether made by a holder of record or a beneficial owner, the written demand must reasonably inform Iridium that the Iridium holder of record or beneficial owner intends thereby to demand an appraisal of his, her or its shares. The written demand must be received by Iridium prior to the vote on the Merger Agreement Proposal at the special meeting. Neither voting

 

99

 

 

(in person or by proxy) against, abstaining from voting on or failing to vote on the Merger Agreement Proposal will alone suffice to constitute a written demand for appraisal within the meaning of Section 262 of the DGCL. In addition, the holder or beneficial owner must not vote its shares of Iridium Common Stock in favor of adoption of the Merger Agreement Proposal. An executed proxy by a record holder that does not contain voting instructions will, unless revoked, be voted in favor of adoption of the Merger Agreement Proposal and will cause the stockholder’s right of appraisal to be lost. Therefore, an Iridium stockholder who desires to exercise appraisal rights should either (x) refrain from executing and submitting the enclosed proxy card or (y) vote by proxy against the adoption of the Merger Agreement Proposal or affirmatively register an abstention with respect thereto. In the case of a beneficial owner, brokers, banks and other nominees that hold shares of Iridium Common Stock in “street name” for their customers do not have discretionary authority to vote on the Merger Agreement Proposal without specific voting instructions from the beneficial owner on such proposal, but such brokers, banks or other nominees will vote such shares as instructed if the beneficial owner provides such instructions. If a beneficial owner of shares held in “street name” instructs such person’s broker, bank or other nominee to vote such person’s shares in favor of the Merger Agreement Proposal, and does not revoke such instruction prior to the vote on the Merger Agreement Proposal, then such shares will be voted in favor of the Merger Agreement Proposal, and it will cause such beneficial owner to lose his, her or its right to appraisal and will nullify any previously delivered written demand for appraisal. Therefore, a beneficial owner who wishes to exercise appraisal rights must either not provide any instructions to such person’s broker, bank or other nominee how to vote on the Merger Agreement Proposal or must instruct such broker, bank or other nominee to vote against the Merger Agreement Proposal or abstain from voting on such proposal.

 

Within 120 days after completion of the First Merger, either the Surviving Entity, or any holder or beneficial owner of shares of Iridium Common Stock who has timely and properly demanded appraisal of such person’s shares and who has complied with the requirements of Section 262 of the DGCL and is otherwise entitled to appraisal rights, may commence an appraisal proceeding by filing a petition in the Delaware Court of Chancery, with a copy served on the Surviving Entity in the case of a petition filed by a stockholder or beneficial owner, demanding a determination of the fair value of the shares of all persons who have properly demanded appraisal. There is no present intent on the part of the Surviving Entity to file an appraisal petition, and stockholders or beneficial owners seeking to exercise appraisal rights should not assume that the Surviving Entity will file such a petition or that the Surviving Entity will initiate any negotiations with respect to the fair value of such shares. Accordingly, record holders and beneficial owners of Iridium Common Stock who desire to have their shares appraised should initiate any petitions necessary for the perfection of their appraisal rights within the time periods and in the manner prescribed in Section 262 of the DGCL. If no such petition is filed within that 120-day period, appraisal rights will be lost for such person.

 

Within 120 days after completion of the First Merger, any holder or beneficial owner of shares of Iridium Common Stock who has complied with the applicable provisions of Section 262 of the DGCL will be entitled, upon written request, to receive from the Surviving Entity a statement setting forth the aggregate number of shares of Iridium Common Stock not voting in favor of the First Merger and with respect to which demands for appraisal were received by the Surviving Entity and the aggregate number of holders or beneficial owners holding or owning such shares (provided that, in the case of a demand made by a beneficial owner in such person’s name, the record holder of such shares shall not be considered a separate stockholder holding such shares for purposes of such aggregate number). Such statement must be given within 10 days after the written request therefor has been received by the Surviving Entity (as the surviving entity) or within 10 days after the expiration of the period for delivery of demands for appraisal, whichever is later.

 

If a petition for appraisal is duly filed by a holder or beneficial owner of Iridium Common Stock and a copy of the petition is served upon the Surviving Entity, then the Surviving Entity will be obligated, within 20 days after receiving service of a copy of the petition, to file with the Delaware Register in Chancery in which the petition was filed a duly verified list containing the names and addresses of all persons who have demanded an appraisal of their shares of Iridium Common Stock and with whom agreements as to the value of their shares of Iridium Common Stock have not been reached. Upon the filing of any such petition, the Delaware Court of Chancery may order the Delaware Register in Chancery to provide notice of the time and place fixed for the hearing on the petition to the Surviving Entity and all of the persons shown on the verified list. The costs of these notices are borne by the Surviving Entity.

 

After notice to persons who have demanded appraisal, if such notice is ordered by the Delaware Court of Chancery, the Delaware Court of Chancery will conduct a hearing upon the petition and determine those persons

 

100

 

 

who have complied with Section 262 of the DGCL and who have become entitled to appraisal rights. The Delaware Court of Chancery may require the persons who have demanded an appraisal for their shares and who hold stock represented by certificates to submit their certificates of stock to the Register in Chancery for notation thereon of the pendency of the appraisal proceedings; and if any person fails to comply with such direction, the Delaware Court of Chancery may dismiss the proceedings as to such person. Assuming shares of Iridium Common Stock remain listed on a national securities exchange immediately before the First Merger (which we expect to be the case), the Delaware Court of Chancery must dismiss an appraisal proceeding as to all holders or beneficial owners of Iridium Common Stock who assert appraisal rights unless (i) the total number of shares entitled to appraisal rights which have been pursued and perfected exceeds 1% of the outstanding shares of the class or series eligible for appraisal as measured in accordance with subsection (g) of Section 262 of the DGCL, or (ii) the value of the consideration provided in the First Merger (i.e., the Merger Consideration) for such total number of shares seeking appraisal exceeds $1.0 million, or (iii) the First Merger was approved pursuant to Section 253 or Section 267 of the DGCL (which, with respect to this clause (iii), we do not expect to be the case). Given that the shares of Iridium Common Stock are listed on Nasdaq (and assuming such shares remain so listed up until the First Effective Time), then the Delaware Court of Chancery is expected to dismiss any appraisal proceedings as to all holders of Iridium Common Stock who are otherwise entitled to appraisal rights unless one of the ownership thresholds identified in clause (i) or clause (ii) above is satisfied. Where proceedings are not dismissed, and after determining the persons entitled to an appraisal, the appraisal proceeding will be conducted, as to the shares of Iridium Common Stock owned by such holders or beneficial owners of Iridium Common Stock, in accordance with the rules of the Delaware Court of Chancery, including any rules specifically governing appraisal proceedings.

 

In determining fair value and the amount of the appraisal payment, if any, the Delaware Court of Chancery is required to take into account all relevant factors. In Weinberger v. UOP, Inc., the Supreme Court of Delaware discussed the factors that could be considered in determining fair value in an appraisal proceeding, stating that “proof of value by any techniques or methods which are generally considered acceptable in the financial community and otherwise admissible in court” should be considered and that “[f]air price obviously requires consideration of all relevant factors involving the value of a company.” The Delaware Supreme Court has stated that in making this determination of fair value the court must consider market value, asset value, dividends, earnings prospects, the nature of the enterprise and any other facts which could be ascertained as of the date of the merger that throw any light on future prospects of the merged corporation. The Delaware Supreme Court has indicated that transaction price is one of the relevant factors the Court of Chancery may consider in determining “fair value” and that absent deficiencies in the sale process the transaction price should be given “considerable weight.” Section 262 of the DGCL provides that fair value is to be determined “exclusive of any element of value arising from the accomplishment or expectation of the merger.” In Cede & Co. v. Technicolor, Inc., the Delaware Supreme Court stated that such exclusion is a “narrow exclusion [that] does not encompass known elements of value,” but which rather applies only to the speculative elements of value arising from such accomplishment or expectation. In Weinberger, the Delaware Supreme Court construed Section 262 of the DGCL to mean that “elements of future value, including the nature of the enterprise, which are known or susceptible of proof as of the date of the merger and not the product of speculation, may be considered.”

 

Unless the Delaware Court of Chancery in its discretion determines otherwise for good cause shown, and except as provided in subsection (h) of Section 262 of the DGCL, interest from the effective date through the date of payment of the judgment will be compounded quarterly and will accrue at 5% over the Federal Reserve discount rate (including any surcharges) as established from time to time during the period between the effective date and the date of payment of the judgment (or in certain circumstances described herein, on the difference between the amount determined to be the fair value and the amount paid by the Surviving Entity in the First Merger to each person entitled to appraisal prior to the entry of judgment in the appraisal proceeding) as described further below.

 

At any time before the entry of judgment in the proceedings, the Surviving Entity has the right to make a voluntary cash payment to each person entitled to appraisal an amount in cash, in which case, interest will accrue thereafter as provided in Section 262 of the DGCL only upon the sum of (i) the difference, if any, between the amount so paid and the fair value of the shares as determined by the Delaware Court of Chancery, and (ii) interest theretofore accrued, unless paid at that time. When the appraisal payment is determined, the Delaware Court of Chancery will direct the payment of such value to the persons entitled thereto upon such terms and conditions as the Delaware Court of Chancery may order. The Delaware Court of Chancery’s decree may be enforced as other decrees in such court may be enforced.

 

101

 

 

Record holders and beneficial owners of Iridium Common Stock considering seeking appraisal should be aware that the fair value of their shares of Iridium Common Stock could be more than, less than or equal to the Merger Consideration, and that opinions of investment banking firms as to the fairness from a financial point of view of the consideration payable in a transaction are not opinions as to fair value under Section 262 of the DGCL. Each of Rocket Lab, the Surviving Entity and Iridium reserves the right to assert, in any appraisal proceeding, that for purposes of Section 262 of the DGCL, the “fair value” of a share of Iridium Common Stock is less than the Merger Consideration, and the Surviving Entity reserves the right to make a voluntary cash payment pursuant to subsection (h) of Section 262.

 

Upon application by the Surviving Entity or by any holder or beneficial owner of shares of Iridium Common Stock entitled to participate in the appraisal proceeding, the Delaware Court of Chancery may, in its discretion, proceed to trial upon the appraisal prior to the final determination of the persons entitled to an appraisal. Any person whose name appears on the verified list filed by the Surviving Entity pursuant to subsection (f) of Section 262 of the DGCL may participate fully in all proceedings until it is finally determined that such person is not entitled to appraisal rights under Section 262 of the DGCL. The Delaware Court of Chancery will direct the payment of the fair value of the shares, together with interest, if any, by the Surviving Entity to the persons entitled thereto. Payment shall be so made to each such person upon such terms and conditions as the Delaware Court of Chancery may order. The Delaware Court of Chancery’s decree may be enforced as other decrees in such Court may be enforced.

 

The costs of the appraisal proceeding may be determined by the Delaware Court of Chancery and taxed upon the parties as the Delaware Court of Chancery deems equitable in the circumstances. Upon application of a person whose name appears on the verified list who participated in the proceeding and incurred expenses in connection therewith (which we refer to as an “Application”), the Delaware Court of Chancery may also order that all or a portion of such expenses, including, without limitation, reasonable attorneys’ fees and the fees and expenses of experts, be charged pro rata against the value of all the shares entitled to an appraisal that were not dismissed pursuant to the terms of Section 262 of the DGCL or subject to an award pursuant to a reservation of jurisdiction (a “Reservation”) for any Application. In the absence of such a determination of assessment, each party bears its own expenses.

 

If any person who demands appraisal of his, her or its shares of Iridium Common Stock under Section 262 of the DGCL fails to perfect, or loses or validly withdraws, such person’s right to appraisal, such person’s shares of Iridium Common Stock will be deemed to have been converted at the First Effective Time into the right to receive the Merger Consideration as provided in the Merger Agreement, without any interest thereon. A person will fail to perfect, or effectively lose, such person’s right to appraisal if no petition for appraisal is filed within 120 days after the effective time of the First Merger, if neither of the ownership thresholds identified above has been satisfied in respect of those seeking appraisal rights with respect to the shares of Iridium Common Stock, or if the person delivers to the Surviving Entity a written withdrawal of such person’s demand for appraisal and an acceptance of the Merger Consideration as provided in the Merger Agreement in accordance with Section 262 of the DGCL.

 

From and after the date of completion of the First Merger, any holder or beneficial owner of Iridium Common Stock who has duly demanded appraisal in compliance with Section 262 of the DGCL will not, after completion of the First Merger, be entitled to vote for any purpose any shares subject to such demand or to receive payment of dividends or other distributions on such shares, except for dividends or distributions payable to stockholders of record at a time prior to the effective date of the First Merger.

 

Within 10 days after the First Effective Time, the Surviving Entity must give notice of the date that the First Merger became effective to each holder of Iridium Common Stock who has properly filed a written demand for appraisal, who did not vote in favor of the proposal to adopt the Merger Agreement and who has otherwise complied with Section 262 of the DGCL and any beneficial owner who has demanded appraisal in such person’s name pursuant to Section 262 of the DGCL. At any time within 60 days after the First Effective Time, any holder or beneficial owner of Iridium Common Stock who has demanded appraisal and who has not commenced an appraisal proceeding or joined that proceeding as a named party will have the right to withdraw such person’s demand for appraisal and to accept the Merger Consideration to which the person is entitled pursuant to the First Merger. After this period, a holder or beneficial owner of Iridium Common Stock may withdraw such person’s demand for appraisal only with the written approval of the Surviving Entity. Notwithstanding the foregoing, no petition timely filed in the Delaware Court of Chancery demanding appraisal will be dismissed as to any person without the approval of the Delaware Court of Chancery, and that approval may be conditioned upon such terms as the Delaware Court of Chancery deems just, including, without limitation, a Reservation; provided, however, that the foregoing

 

102

 

 

will not affect the right of any record holder or beneficial owner of Iridium Common Stock who has not commenced an appraisal proceeding or joined the proceeding as a named party to withdraw such person’s demand for appraisal and to accept the terms offered upon the merger within 60 days after completion of the First Merger as summarized in the second sentence of this paragraph.

 

If no petition for appraisal is filed with the Delaware Court of Chancery within 120 days after completion of the First Merger, appraisal will cease and all record holders and beneficial owners of Iridium Common Stock will be entitled only to receive the Merger Consideration as provided for in the Merger Agreement.

 

The foregoing is only a brief summary of Section 262 of the DGCL that sets forth the procedures for demanding statutory appraisal rights. This summary, however, is not a complete statement of all applicable requirements and is qualified in its entirety by reference to Section 262 of the DGCL, a copy of which may be accessed without subscription or cost at the following publicly available website: https://delcode.delaware.gov/title8/c001/sc09/index.html#262.

 

Failure to comply with all the procedures set forth in Section 262 of the DGCL may result in the loss of a holder’s or beneficial owner’s statutory appraisal rights. Consequently, if you wish to exercise your appraisal rights, you are strongly urged to consult a legal advisor before attempting to exercise your appraisal rights.

 

Nasdaq Listing of Rocket Lab Common Stock; Delisting and Deregistration of Iridium Common Stock

 

Rocket Lab Common Stock is currently listed on Nasdaq under the symbol “RKLB.” Under the Merger Agreement, Rocket Lab must use its commercially reasonable efforts to cause the shares of Rocket Lab Common Stock to be issued as part of the Merger Consideration to be listed on Nasdaq, and approval of those shares for listing on Nasdaq is a condition to the completion of the Mergers. Prior to the First Effective Time, Iridium must cooperate with Rocket Lab and use its commercially reasonable efforts to take, or cause to be taken, all actions, and do or cause to be done all things reasonably necessary, proper or advisable under applicable law and the rules and policies of Nasdaq to enable the delisting of Iridium Common Stock from Nasdaq and the deregistration of Iridium Common Stock under the Exchange Act as promptly as practicable after the First Effective Time.

 

Expected Timing of the Mergers

 

Rocket Lab and Iridium currently expect the Mergers to be completed in mid-2027, subject to the receipt of certain required approvals under applicable Competition Laws, Foreign Investment Laws and Satellite and Communications Laws (including any required FCC approvals and, if applicable, Team Telecom review), the receipt of the Iridium Stockholder Approval and the satisfaction or waiver of the other conditions to Closing contained in the Merger Agreement. However, neither Rocket Lab nor Iridium can predict the actual date on which the Mergers will be completed because completion is subject to conditions beyond each company’s control, and it is possible that such conditions could result in the Mergers being completed earlier or later than expected, or not being completed at all.

 

Material U.S. Federal Income Tax Consequences of the Mergers

 

The following is a general discussion of the material U.S. federal income tax consequences of the Mergers to U.S. Holders (as defined below) of Iridium Common Stock that exchange their Iridium Common Stock for Rocket Lab Common Stock and cash in the Mergers.

 

This discussion is based upon the Code, its legislative history, Treasury Regulations promulgated under the Code and judicial and administrative rulings and decisions, all as in effect on the date of this proxy statement/prospectus. These authorities may change, possibly retroactively, or be subject to differing interpretations, and any such change or differing interpretation could affect the accuracy of the statements and conclusions set forth in this discussion.

 

The following discussion applies only to U.S. Holders (as defined below) who hold such shares as a capital asset within the meaning of Section 1221 of the Code (generally, property held for investment). This discussion is not a complete description of all of the U.S. federal income tax consequences of the Mergers and, in particular, does not address any tax consequences arising under the Medicare contribution tax on net investment income nor does it address any tax consequences arising under the laws of any U.S. state, local or non-U.S. jurisdiction, any U.S. federal

 

103

 

 

estate, gift, generation skipping tax considerations, or under any U.S. federal laws other than those pertaining to the income tax (including in connection with the ownership and disposition of any Rocket Lab Common Stock received by a U.S. Holder in the Mergers). Further, this discussion does not purport to consider all aspects of U.S. federal income taxation that might be relevant to U.S. Holders in light of their particular circumstances and does not apply to U.S. Holders subject to special treatment under the U.S. federal income tax laws (such as, for example, dealers or brokers in securities, commodities or foreign currencies, traders in securities that elect to apply a mark-to-market method of accounting, banks and certain other financial institutions, insurance companies, mutual funds, tax-exempt organizations, holders subject to the alternative minimum tax provisions of the Code, partnerships, S corporations or other pass-through entities or investors therein, regulated investment companies, real estate investment trusts, controlled foreign corporations, passive foreign investment companies, former citizens or residents of the United States, U.S. expatriates, holders whose functional currency is not the U.S. dollar, holders who hold Iridium Common Stock as part of a hedge, straddle, constructive sale or conversion transaction or other integrated investment, retirement plans, individual retirement accounts, or other tax-deferred accounts, holders who acquired Iridium common stock pursuant to the exercise of employee stock options, through a tax qualified retirement plan or otherwise as compensation, holders who actually or constructively own more than 5% of Iridium Common Stock or holders who actually or constructively hold shares of both Rocket Lab and Iridium).

 

For purposes of this discussion, a “U.S. Holder” means a beneficial owner of shares of Iridium Common Stock that is, for U.S. federal income tax purposes either:

 

·an individual who is a citizen or resident of the United States;

 

·a corporation or other entity taxable as a corporation created or organized in the United States or under the laws of the United States or of any state thereof or the District of Columbia;

 

·a trust if (a) a U.S. court is able to exercise primary supervision over the administration of such trust and one or more “United States persons” (within the meaning of Section 7701(a)(30) of the Code) have the authority to control all substantial decisions of the trust or (b) the trust has a valid election in effect under applicable Treasury Regulations to be treated as a United States person; or

 

·an estate the income of which is includable in gross income for U.S. federal income tax purposes regardless of its source.

 

Beneficial owners of Iridium Common Stock that are not U.S. Holders should consult their own tax advisors as to the U.S. federal income tax consequences of the Mergers.

 

If an entity or an arrangement treated as a partnership or pass-through entity for U.S. federal income tax purposes holds shares of Iridium Common Stock, the U.S. federal income tax consequences to a partner or owner in such partnership or pass-through entity generally will depend on the status of the partner or owner and the activities of the partner or owner and partnership or pass-through entity. Any entity or arrangement treated as a partnership or pass-through entity for U.S. federal income tax purposes that holds shares of Iridium Common Stock, and any persons that, for U.S. federal income tax purposes, are treated as partners or owners in such partnership or pass-through entity, should consult their own tax advisors with respect to the tax consequences of the Mergers in their specific circumstances.

 

This discussion is not tax advice and does not purport to be a complete analysis or discussion of all U.S. federal income tax considerations relating to the Mergers. Determining the actual tax consequences of the Mergers to you may be complex and will depend on your specific situation and factors not within Rocket Lab’s or Iridium’s control. You should consult your own tax advisor as to the specific tax consequences of the Mergers to you in your particular circumstances, including the applicability and effect of the alternative minimum tax and any state, local, non-U.S. or other tax laws and of changes, if any, in those laws.

 

In General

 

The U.S. federal income tax consequences of the Mergers will depend on, among other considerations, whether the Rocket Lab Common Stock paid to Iridium stockholders represents at least a certain minimum percentage of the value of the total consideration paid to Iridium stockholders, as required by the Continuity of Interest Requirement. For this purpose, Rocket Lab and Iridium intend to treat the Mergers, taken together, as meeting the Continuity of Interest Requirement and as a “reorganization” within the meaning of Section 368(a) of the Code, if the Equity Threshold Condition is satisfied (the “Intended Tax Treatment”).

 

104

 

 

If the Equity Threshold Condition is not satisfied, the Second Merger will not be effectuated and the transaction will be treated as a taxable sale of Iridium Common Stock by its holders described under Section 1001 of the Code in exchange for Rocket Lab Common Stock and cash (the “Alternative Tax Treatment”). No assurance can be given that the Equity Threshold Condition will be met or that the Mergers will qualify for the Intended Tax Treatment. The completion of the Mergers is not conditioned on the Mergers qualifying for the Intended Tax Treatment. Whether the Mergers qualify for the Intended Tax Treatment or Alternative Tax Treatment depends on facts that may not be known until after the Closing Date.

 

In the opinion of Davis Polk, counsel to Iridium, if the Rocket Lab Common Stock received by holders of Iridium Common Stock as part of the Merger Consideration (valued as of the completion of the Mergers) represents at least forty percent (40%) of the total value of all Merger Consideration received by the holders of Iridium Common Stock (for the avoidance of doubt, taking into account any payments made to dissenting stockholders of Iridium Common Stock) the Mergers should, taken together as a single integrated transaction, qualify for the Intended Tax Treatment. However, no assurance can be given that the IRS will not assert, or that a court would not sustain, that the Mergers do not qualify for the Intended Tax Treatment. Davis Polk’s opinion is based on certain assumptions as well as representations, warranties and covenants of Iridium, Merger Sub I, Merger Sub II and Rocket Lab.

 

While no specific guidance sets forth the minimum percentage necessary to satisfy the Continuity of Interest Requirement, it should, in Davis Polk’s opinion, be satisfied if the value of Rocket Lab Common Stock received in the Mergers (valued as of the completion of the Mergers) represents at least 40% of the total value of the Merger Consideration. Under the Merger Agreement, Rocket Lab and Iridium intend to determine the value of the Rocket Lab Common Stock received in respect of Iridium Common Stock for this purpose using the Parent Common Share Value Metric (which is the greatest of five separately specified stock price measurements, the latest of which is measured on the trading day immediately following the Closing Date). However, neither the IRS nor the U.S. Treasury Department has issued definitive guidance regarding the determination of the value of common stock received in a transaction like ours, in which the amount of stock paid is subject to a collar. Accordingly, the IRS may challenge our determination that the Continuity of Interest Requirement is met.

 

Because the value of Rocket Lab Common Stock may fluctuate, a substantial decline in the value of the Rocket Lab Common Stock from its value as of the execution of the Merger Agreement on June 28, 2026, could cause the value of all Rocket Lab Common Stock received by holders of Iridium Common Stock in the Mergers to represent less than 40% of the total value of the Merger Consideration received by holders of Iridium Common Stock in the Mergers (for a description of how the Exchange Ratio operates across various Rocket Lab stock prices, including the collar floor of $67.50 and ceiling of $112.50, see “The Merger Agreement—Merger Consideration Received by Iridium Stockholders; Withholding Rights” beginning on page 109). Accordingly, no assurance can be given that the Mergers will qualify for the Intended Tax Treatment.

 

Although Rocket Lab and Iridium have covenanted in the Merger Agreement not to take any action that would reasonably be expected to prevent or impede the Mergers from qualifying for the Intended Tax Treatment, the Closing is not conditioned on the receipt of any opinion of counsel as to the qualification of the Mergers for the Intended Tax Treatment.

 

Neither Rocket Lab nor Iridium intends to request a ruling from the IRS regarding the U.S. federal income tax consequences of the Mergers. Accordingly, even if Iridium and Rocket Lab treat the Mergers consistently with the Intended Tax Treatment, no assurance can be given that the IRS will not challenge that treatment or that a court would not sustain such a challenge. If the IRS successfully challenges the Intended Tax Treatment, U.S. Holders will be treated as if they sold their Iridium Common Stock in a fully taxable transaction (as described below under “Tax Consequences if the Mergers Fail to Qualify as a Tax-Free Reorganization”).

 

Tax Consequences of the Mergers Generally

 

Neither Iridium nor Rocket Lab will recognize gain or loss for U.S. federal income tax purposes as a result of the Mergers.

 

A U.S. Holder who acquired different blocks of Iridium Common Stock at different times and at different prices generally must apply the rules described in the following sections separately to each identifiable block of shares of Iridium Common Stock. A U.S. Holder that holds Iridium Common Stock with differing bases or holding periods should consult the U.S. Holder’s tax advisor with regard to identifying the

 

105

 

 

particular shares of Iridium Common Stock and identifying the bases or holding periods of the particular shares of Rocket Lab Common Stock received in the Mergers.

 

Tax Consequences to U.S. Holders if the Mergers Qualify for the Intended Tax Treatment

 

Assuming that the Mergers qualify for the Intended Tax Treatment, a U.S. Holder that exchanges shares of Iridium Common Stock for a combination of Rocket Lab Common Stock and cash in the Mergers generally will not recognize any realized loss but will recognize any realized gain equal to the lesser of (i) the excess, if any, of the amount of cash (excluding the amount of any cash in lieu of a fractional share of Rocket Lab Common Stock) plus the fair market value of the Rocket Lab Common Stock (including any fractional share of Rocket Lab Common Stock deemed received and redeemed for cash, as discussed below) received in exchange for such shares of Iridium Common Stock in the Mergers, over such holder’s tax basis in the shares of Iridium Common Stock exchanged therefor and (ii) the amount of cash (excluding the amount of any cash in lieu of a fractional share of Rocket Lab Common Stock) received by such holder in exchange for such shares of Iridium Common Stock.

 

Generally, such U.S. Holder’s aggregate tax basis in the Rocket Lab Common Stock received by such U.S. Holder in the Mergers (including any fractional share of Rocket Lab Common Stock deemed received and redeemed for cash, as discussed below) will equal such U.S. Holder’s aggregate tax basis in the shares of Iridium Common Stock exchanged therefor, increased by the amount of taxable gain, if any, recognized by such U.S. Holder in the exchange of such shares, and decreased by the amount of cash received by such U.S. Holder (excluding the amount of any cash in lieu of a fractional share of Rocket Lab Common Stock) in exchange for such shares of Iridium Common Stock. A U.S. Holder’s holding period in the Rocket Lab Common Stock received (including any fractional share of Rocket Lab Common Stock deemed received and redeemed for cash, as discussed below) will include the holding period for the holder’s shares of Iridium Common Stock surrendered in exchange therefor.

 

Cash in Lieu of Fractional Shares. A U.S. Holder that receives cash in lieu of a fractional share of Rocket Lab Common Stock will generally be treated as having received such fractional share and then as having sold to Rocket Lab that fractional share of Rocket Lab Common Stock for cash. Gain or loss will generally be recognized based on the difference between the amount of cash received in lieu of the fractional share of Rocket Lab Common Stock and the portion of the U.S. Holder’s aggregate adjusted tax basis in the shares of Iridium Common Stock exchanged therefor that is allocable to the fractional share.

 

Capital Gain. Subject to the discussion below under “—Possible Dividend Treatment,” any gain recognized with respect to the exchange of Iridium Common Stock in the Mergers (if the Intended Tax Treatment applies) will generally be capital gain. Such gain will generally be long-term capital gain if the U.S. Holder’s holding period for its Iridium Common Stock surrendered in the Mergers exceeds one year at the First Effective Time. Long-term capital gains of certain non-corporate U.S. Holders, including individuals, are generally taxed at preferential rates.

 

Whether the requirements for the Mergers to qualify for the Intended Tax Treatment are met may not be known at the time of the special meeting, and whether Rocket Lab the Equity Threshold Condition has been met may not be determined until after the Closing. However, Iridium will not resolicit stockholder votes in the event that the Mergers fail to qualify for the Intended Tax Treatment.

 

Tax Consequences to U.S. Holders if the Mergers Fail to Qualify as a Tax-Free Reorganization

 

If the Equity Threshold Condition is not satisfied or the Mergers otherwise fail to qualify for the Intended Tax Treatment, under the Alternative Tax Treatment, a U.S. Holder whose shares of Iridium Common Stock are converted into the right to receive the Merger Consideration generally will recognize capital gain or loss in an amount equal to the difference between (i) the sum of the fair market value of the shares of Rocket Lab Common Stock and the amount of Cash Consideration received in the Mergers (including cash received in lieu of fractional shares of Rocket Lab Common Stock) and (ii) the U.S. Holder’s tax basis in the Iridium Common Stock surrendered. Additionally, a U.S. Holder’s holding period in shares of Rocket Lab Common Stock received in the First Merger would begin on the day following the First Merger.

 

Any gain or loss recognized by a U.S. Holder would generally be long-term capital gain or loss if the U.S. Holder’s holding period in a particular block of Iridium Common Stock exceeds one year as of the First Effective Time. Long-term capital gain of certain non-corporate U.S. Holders (including individuals) is currently eligible for preferential U.S. federal income tax rates. The deductibility of capital losses is subject to certain limitations.

 

106

 

 

Information Reporting and Backup Withholding

 

Under certain circumstances the receipt of the Merger Consideration in exchange for Iridium Common Stock pursuant to the Mergers may be subject to information reporting and backup withholding at a rate of 24%. To prevent backup withholding, U.S. Holders should timely furnish proof of an applicable exemption, such as through furnishing a properly completed IRS Form W-9 or successor form (or appropriate substitute) certifying that such U.S. Holder is a “United States person” (within the meaning of the Code), that the taxpayer identification number provided is correct and that such U.S. Holder is not subject to backup withholding and otherwise complying with all the applicable requirements of the backup withholding rules. The IRS may impose a penalty upon a U.S. Holder that fails to provide the correct taxpayer identification number. Any amounts withheld under the backup withholding rules are not an additional tax and will generally be allowed as a refund or credit against a U.S. Holder’s U.S. federal income tax liability, if any, provided that such holder timely furnishes the required information to the IRS.

  

The preceding discussion is intended only as a general discussion of material U.S. federal income tax consequences of the Mergers. The preceding discussion is not a complete analysis or discussion of all potential tax effects that may be important to you. You should consult your own tax advisors as to the specific tax consequences of the Mergers including tax return reporting requirements, the applicability and effect of U.S. federal, state, local, non-U.S. and other tax laws and the effect of any proposed changes in the tax laws.

 

Litigation Related to the Mergers

 

Stockholders may file lawsuits challenging the Mergers, which may name Rocket Lab, Iridium, members of the boards of directors of Rocket Lab or Iridium, or others as defendants.

 

No assurance can be made as to the outcome of such lawsuits, including the amount of costs associated with defending claims or any other liabilities that may be incurred in connection with the litigation of any claims. If plaintiffs are successful in obtaining an injunction prohibiting the parties from completing the Mergers on the agreed-upon terms, such an injunction may delay the completion of the Mergers or may prevent the Mergers from being completed altogether. Even if such a lawsuit is unsuccessful, defending against these claims can result in substantial costs, and lawsuits could prevent or delay the completion of the Mergers.

Structure of the Mergers

 

The Merger Agreement provides that, on the terms and subject to the conditions set forth in the Merger Agreement, and in accordance with the DGCL, the parties will complete two mergers. In the First Merger, Merger Sub I will merge with and into Iridium, with Iridium continuing as the Surviving Corporation. If the Second Merger Condition is satisfied, immediately following the First Effective Time, or if the Equity Threshold Condition (but not the Second Merger Condition) is satisfied, on the second trading day following the First Effective Time, the Surviving Corporation will merge with and into Merger Sub II, with Merger Sub II in accordance with the DGCL and the DLLCA surviving as the Surviving Entity of the Second Merger. Following the Second Merger, the Surviving Entity will be a wholly-owned indirect subsidiary of Rocket Lab. If the Second Merger does not occur (including the case in which neither the Second Merger Condition nor the Equity Threshold Condition is satisfied), then references in the Merger Agreement to the “Mergers” will refer solely to the First Merger, and Iridium will be treated as the Surviving Entity for all purposes of the Merger Agreement. The two-step structure is intended, among other things, to facilitate the qualification of the Mergers, taken together, as a “reorganization” within the meaning of Section 368(a) of the Code.

 

At the First Effective Time, the governing documents of the Surviving Corporation will be the certificate of incorporation and bylaws of Merger Sub I, as in effect immediately prior to the First Effective Time. The directors and officers of Merger Sub I immediately prior to the First Effective Time will be the initial directors and officers of the Surviving Corporation, in each case, until their respective successors are duly elected or appointed and qualified or until their earlier death, resignation or removal. At the Second Effective Time, the governing documents of the Surviving Entity will be the certificate of formation and limited liability company agreement of Merger Sub II, as in effect immediately prior to the Second Effective Time. The officers of Merger Sub II immediately prior to the Second

 

108

 

 

Effective Time will be the initial officers of the Surviving Entity, in each case, until their respective successors are duly elected or appointed and qualified or until their earlier death, resignation or removal.

 

Closing

 

The Closing will take place through the electronic exchange of the applicable documents and signature pages, using PDF or electronic signatures, as soon as reasonably practicable, but in any event no later than three business days after the date on which the conditions to the Mergers described under “—Conditions to the Mergers” beginning on page 127 have been satisfied or, to the extent permissible, waived by the party or parties entitled to the benefit of such conditions (other than those conditions that by their nature are to be satisfied at the Closing, but subject to the satisfaction or waiver of those conditions at the Closing), or at such other place, at such other time or on such other date as Rocket Lab and Iridium may mutually agree in writing. The Closing Date is the date on which the Closing occurs.

 

Merger Consideration Received by Iridium Stockholders; Withholding Rights

 

Effects of the Mergers

 

At the First Effective Time, by virtue of the First Merger and without any action on the part of Rocket Lab, Merger Sub I, Merger Sub II, Iridium or the holders of any securities:

 

·Each share of Iridium Common Stock outstanding immediately prior to the First Effective Time (other than (x) shares held by Iridium as treasury shares or owned by Rocket Lab, Merger Sub I, Merger Sub II or any other subsidiary of Rocket Lab, which will be canceled and cease to exist without any payment, (y) shares held by any subsidiary of Iridium, which will be converted into shares of the Surviving Corporation such that each subsidiary owns the same percentage of the outstanding capital stock in the Surviving Corporation immediately following the First Effective Time as such subsidiary owned in Iridium immediately prior to the First Effective Time, and (z) Dissenting Shares) will be automatically converted into the right to receive the Merger Consideration, consisting of: (i) $27.00 in cash, without interest, and (ii) a number of validly issued, fully paid and nonassessable shares of Rocket Lab Common Stock equal to the Exchange Ratio, plus any cash in lieu of fractional shares of Rocket Lab Common Stock as provided under the Merger Agreement.

 

·Upon such conversion, all shares of Iridium Common Stock so converted will cease to be outstanding, will be canceled and retired, and will represent only the right to receive the applicable Merger Consideration and any cash to be paid in lieu of fractional shares of Rocket Lab Common Stock.

 

·Each share of Iridium Common Stock held by Iridium as a treasury share or owned by Rocket Lab, Merger Sub I, Merger Sub II or any other subsidiary of Rocket Lab immediately prior to the First Effective Time will be canceled and cease to exist, and no payment will be made with respect thereto.

 

·Each share of Iridium Common Stock held by any subsidiary of Iridium immediately prior to the First Effective Time will be converted into such number of common shares of the Surviving Corporation such that each such subsidiary owns the same percentage of the outstanding capital stock of the Surviving Corporation immediately following the First Effective Time as it owned in Iridium immediately prior to the First Effective Time.

 

·Each share of common stock of Merger Sub I outstanding immediately prior to the First Effective Time will be converted into and become one share of common stock of Iridium as the Surviving Corporation.

Potential Adjustments to the Merger Consideration to Prevent Dilution

 

If, during the period between the date of the Merger Agreement and the First Effective Time, any change in the outstanding number or class of shares of capital stock of Iridium or Rocket Lab occurs by reason of any reclassification, recapitalization, stock split or combination, exchange or readjustment of shares, or any stock dividend thereon with a record date during such period, the Merger Consideration, the Exchange Ratio (and its determination), the Equity Award Exchange Ratio (and its determination) and any other similarly dependent items will be equitably adjusted to provide holders of shares of Iridium Common Stock and Rocket Lab the same economic effect as contemplated by the Merger Agreement prior to such event. Changes resulting from the exercise or settlement of equity awards, and grants of equity compensation not prohibited by the terms of the Merger Agreement, will not result in any adjustment. This provision does not permit Iridium or Rocket Lab to take any action with respect to its securities that is otherwise prohibited by the Merger Agreement.

 

Withholding

 

Each of the Surviving Corporation, the Surviving Entity, Rocket Lab, Iridium, Merger Sub II and their respective Affiliates (as defined in the Merger Agreement) and agents (including the Exchange Agent) is entitled to deduct and withhold from any amounts otherwise payable pursuant to the Merger Agreement such amounts as are required to be deducted or withheld under the Code or any other applicable law relating to Taxes. Any amounts so

deducted or withheld shall be paid over to the appropriate Taxing Authority and will be treated for all purposes of the Merger Agreement as having been paid to the person in respect of which such deduction or withholding was made.

 

Conversion of Shares; Exchange of Certificates; No Fractional Shares

 

Deposit of Merger Consideration

 

The shares of Iridium Common Stock will be exchanged in accordance with the procedures described below.

 

Prior to the Closing Date, Rocket Lab will appoint a bank or trust company or other person reasonably acceptable to Iridium to act as the Exchange Agent and enter into an exchange agent agreement, reasonably acceptable to Iridium, with the Exchange Agent for the purpose of exchanging certificates and uncertificated shares and paying the aggregate Merger Consideration under the Merger Agreement. Prior to the First Effective Time, Rocket Lab will make available to the Exchange Agent evidence of book-entry shares representing the shares of Rocket Lab Common Stock issuable in respect of shares of Iridium Common Stock, together with the cash necessary to pay the cash portion of the Merger Consideration. Any cash constituting part of the Merger Consideration may be invested by the Exchange Agent as directed by Rocket Lab, provided that no such investment or loss thereon will affect the amounts payable to former holders of Iridium Common Stock, and Rocket Lab will promptly deposit additional funds with the Exchange Agent to the extent necessary to make the required payments. Any interest and other income resulting from such investments will be paid to the Surviving Corporation, the Surviving Entity or Rocket Lab, as Rocket Lab directs. The aggregate cash portion of the Merger Consideration as so deposited with the Exchange Agent will not be used for any purpose other than to fund payments pursuant to the Merger Agreement.

 

Exchange Procedures

 

As promptly as practicable after the First Effective Time (and in any event within three business days thereafter), Rocket Lab will send, or cause the Exchange Agent to send, to each holder of record, as of the First Effective Time, of shares of Iridium Common Stock (i) a letter of transmittal and instructions (which will specify that the delivery will be effected, and risk of loss and title will pass, only upon proper delivery of certificates, or affidavits of loss in lieu thereof, or transfer of uncertificated shares to the Exchange Agent) and (ii) instructions for use in effecting the surrender of certificates or the transfer of uncertificated shares in exchange for payment of the Merger Consideration, in such form as Rocket Lab and Iridium may reasonably agree and which will be finalized prior to the First Effective Time.

 

Each former Iridium holder who surrenders to the Exchange Agent a certificate (or an affidavit of loss in lieu thereof), together with a duly completed and executed letter of transmittal and such other documents as may reasonably be required by the instructions thereto, or who transfers uncertificated shares by receipt of an “agent’s message” by the Exchange Agent, will be entitled to receive in exchange therefor the Merger Consideration payable in respect of the shares of Iridium Common Stock so surrendered or transferred (less any applicable withholding), together with any cash in lieu of fractional shares and any dividends or distributions such holder has the right to receive as described below. The shares of Rocket Lab Common Stock constituting part of the Merger Consideration will be issued in uncertificated book-entry form, unless a physical certificate is required under applicable law, and any certificates so surrendered will be canceled. No interest will be paid or will accrue on any cash payable upon surrender or transfer. Until surrendered or transferred as contemplated by the Merger Agreement, each certificate and uncertificated share will represent, from and after the First Effective Time, only the right to receive the Merger Consideration and any dividends or distributions as described below. At the First Effective Time, the stock transfer books of Iridium will be closed, and there will be no further registration of transfers of shares of Iridium Common Stock that were outstanding immediately prior to the First Effective Time. If, after the First Effective Time, certificates or uncertificated shares are presented to the Surviving Corporation, the Surviving Entity or the Exchange Agent, they will be canceled and exchanged for the Merger Consideration and the right to receive any dividends or distributions provided for by, and in accordance with, the procedures set forth in the Merger Agreement.

 

Distributions With Respect to Unexchanged Shares

 

No dividends or other distributions with respect to shares of Rocket Lab Common Stock issued in the Mergers, and no cash payable in lieu of fractional shares, will be paid to the holder of any unsurrendered certificates or

 

111

 

 

untransferred uncertificated shares until such certificates (including via affidavits of loss in lieu thereof, if applicable) or uncertificated shares are surrendered or transferred as described under “—Exchange Procedures.” Following such surrender or transfer, there will be paid, without interest, to the record holder (i) the amount of any cash payable in lieu of fractional shares to which such holder is entitled and (ii) the amount of all dividends or other distributions with a record date after the First Effective Time theretofore paid or payable with respect to such shares of Rocket Lab Common Stock. Any portion of the Merger Consideration made available to the Exchange Agent that remains unclaimed by former holders of shares of Iridium Common Stock twelve months after the First Effective Time will be returned to Rocket Lab upon demand, and any such holder who has not by then surrendered or transferred its shares will thereafter look only to Rocket Lab for payment of the Merger Consideration and any such dividends or distributions, in each case without interest and subject to applicable abandoned property, escheat and similar laws.

 

No Fractional Shares

 

No fractional shares of Rocket Lab Common Stock will be issued in the Mergers. All fractional shares of Rocket Lab Common Stock that a holder of shares of Iridium Common Stock would otherwise be entitled to receive will be aggregated, and each holder otherwise entitled to a fractional share will instead receive a cash payment, without interest, equal to the product of (i) the Rocket Lab Stock Price and (ii) the fraction of a share of Rocket Lab Common Stock to which such holder would otherwise have been entitled.

 

Lost, Stolen or Destroyed Certificates

 

In the case of any certificate that has been lost, stolen or destroyed, upon the making of an affidavit of that fact by the person claiming such certificate to be lost, stolen or destroyed, in a form reasonably acceptable to Rocket Lab and the Exchange Agent, and, the Exchange Agent will require payment of a replacement fee and the posting by such person of a bond in such reasonable amount as Rocket Lab or the Exchange Agent may direct as indemnity against any claim with respect to such certificate, the Exchange Agent will pay, in exchange for such lost, stolen or destroyed certificate, the Merger Consideration to be paid in respect of the shares of Iridium Common Stock represented by such certificate.

 

Dissenting Shares

 

Appraisal Rights

 

Notwithstanding anything in the Merger Agreement to the contrary, shares of Iridium Common Stock that are issued and outstanding immediately prior to the First Effective Time and that are held by a stockholder of record or owned by a beneficial owner who has not voted in favor of, or consented in writing to, the adoption of the Merger Agreement and who has properly and validly demanded, and not withdrawn or lost, appraisal rights for such shares in accordance with Section 262 of the DGCL will not be converted into, or represent the right to receive, the Merger Consideration. Instead, such persons will be entitled to receive payment of the appraised value of such shares as determined in accordance with Section 262 of the DGCL.

 

If any holder of record or beneficial owner of Dissenting Shares fails to perfect, or effectively withdraws or otherwise loses, such person’s appraisal rights under Section 262 of the DGCL, then, as of the First Effective Time, each such Dissenting Share will be deemed to have been converted into, and to have become exchangeable solely for, the right to receive the Merger Consideration, without interest, upon surrender of the certificate or transfer of the uncertificated shares that formerly evidenced such Iridium Common Stock in the manner described under “—Exchange Procedures” (or, in the case of a lost, stolen or destroyed certificate, upon delivery of an affidavit in accordance with the Merger Agreement).

 

Iridium is required to give Rocket Lab prompt notice of any demands for appraisal received by Iridium, any withdrawals of such demands and any other related instruments served on Iridium pursuant to the DGCL in respect of Dissenting Shares, and Rocket Lab has the right to participate in all negotiations and proceedings with respect to such demands. Iridium may not, without the prior written consent of Rocket Lab, make any payment with respect to, or settle or offer to settle, any such demands for appraisal.

 

For a more detailed description of the appraisal rights available to holders of Iridium Common Stock and the procedures required to perfect such rights under Section 262 of the DGCL, see the section titled “The Mergers—Appraisal Rights in the Mergers” beginning on page 98. Treatment of Iridium Equity Awards

 

Iridium RSU Awards and Iridium PSU Awards. Each Iridium RSU Award and Iridium PSU Award that is outstanding immediately prior to the First Effective Time will be assumed by Rocket Lab and converted into an Assumed Iridium RSU Award subject to the same terms and conditions as applied to the applicable Iridium RSU Award or Iridium PSU Award immediately prior to the First Effective Time (including the same vesting and leaver provisions), except that each such Assumed Iridium RSU Award will cover a whole number of shares of Rocket Lab Common Stock equal to the number of shares of Iridium Common Stock covered by such Iridium RSU Award or Iridium PSU Award immediately prior to the First Effective Time (which, in the case of Iridium PSU Awards, will assume satisfaction of applicable performance-based vesting conditions at target levels) multiplied by the Equity Award Exchange Ratio (with the result rounded down to the nearest whole share), and each Assumed Iridium RSU Award will vest in full in the event of a termination of employment without cause within 12 months following the First Effective Time (in addition to any other provisions that apply to the corresponding Iridium RSU Award or Iridium PSU Award, including under the Severance Plan).

 

Iridium Option Awards and Iridium CSAR Awards. Each Iridium Option Award or Iridium CSAR Award that is outstanding and unexercised immediately prior to the First Effective Time will be fully vested and exercisable and canceled and converted into the right to receive the Merger Consideration in respect of each share of Iridium Common Stock covered by such Iridium Option Award or Iridium CSAR Award, calculated net of the exercise price or strike price, as applicable, less applicable withholdings; provided that the Merger Consideration payable with respect to any Iridium CSAR Award will be paid solely in cash, with the stock portion converted into cash based on the Rocket Lab Stock Price.

 

Representations and Warranties

 

Iridium makes various representations and warranties with respect to itself and its subsidiaries to Rocket Lab, Merger Sub I and Merger Sub II in the Merger Agreement that are subject in some cases to exceptions and qualifications. These representations and warranties relate to, among other things:

 

·due organization, valid existence and good standing of Iridium and its subsidiaries under the laws of the State of Delaware and corporate power and qualification to carry on their respective businesses;

 

·corporate authorization to enter into the Merger Agreement and complete the transactions contemplated by the Merger Agreement, and the required vote of the Iridium stockholders to obtain the Iridium stockholder approval;

 

·governmental authorization;

 

·absence of any breach of organizational documents, law or certain material agreements as a result of the contemplated transactions contemplated by the Merger Agreement;

 

·capitalization of Iridium;

 

·ownership and organization of subsidiaries;

 

·filings with the SEC and internal controls and procedures;

 

·financial statements;

 

·disclosure documents;

 

·absence of certain changes since March 31, 2026;

 

·absence of undisclosed material liabilities;

 

·compliance with applicable laws and permits;

 

·telecommunications permits, Iridium satellites and ground stations;

·investigations and litigation;

 

·title to properties;

 

·intellectual property and data privacy;

 

·tax matters;

 

·matters relating to the Intended Tax Treatment of the Mergers;

 

·employee benefit plans;

 

·employee and labor matters;

 

·environmental matters;

 

·material contracts;

 

·insurance;

 

·government contracts;

In addition, Rocket Lab, Merger Sub I and Merger Sub II make representations and warranties to Iridium. These representations and warranties relate to, among other things:

 

·due organization, valid existence and good standing of Rocket Lab, Merger Sub I and Merger Sub II and power and qualification to carry on their respective businesses, and the limited purpose and activities of Merger Sub I and Merger Sub II;

 

·corporate authorization to enter into the Merger Agreement and complete the transactions contemplated by the Merger Agreement;

 

·governmental authorization, including matters relating to foreign ownership, control or influence and Rocket Lab’s facility security clearance;

 

·absence of any breach of organizational documents, law or certain material agreements as a result of the contemplated transactions contemplated by the Merger Agreement;

 

·capitalization of Rocket Lab;

 

·capitalization of Merger Sub I and Merger Sub II;

 

·filings with the SEC and internal controls and procedures;

 

·financial statements;

 

·disclosure documents;

·litigation;
