·finders’ or brokers’ fees;

 

·solvency of the surviving entities following the Mergers;

The representations and warranties in the Merger Agreement do not survive the consummation of the Mergers or termination of the Merger Agreement. Many of the representations and warranties in the Merger Agreement are qualified by a “knowledge,” “materiality” or “material adverse effect” standard (that is, they will not be deemed to be untrue or incorrect unless their failure to be true or correct, individually or in the aggregate, would, as the case may be, be material or have a material adverse effect). For purposes of the Merger Agreement, a “Company Material Adverse Effect” or “Parent Material Adverse Effect,” as applicable, means any Effect that, individually or in the aggregate, (A) has had or would reasonably be expected to have a material adverse effect on the financial condition, business, assets, properties or results of operations of Iridium and its subsidiaries or Rocket Lab and its subsidiaries, as applicable, taken as a whole, or (B) would reasonably be expected to prevent, materially impair or materially delay the ability of Iridium, Rocket Lab, Merger Sub I or Merger Sub II, as applicable, to consummate the Mergers. None of the following, among other things, alone or in combination, will be deemed to constitute, or be taken into account in determining whether there has been, a material adverse effect for purposes of clause (A) above:

 

·changes or prospective changes in GAAP or the interpretation thereof;

 

·changes or prospective changes in applicable law or the interpretation thereof;

 

·general economic, political, regulatory, legal or tax conditions in the United States or any other country or region, including changes in financial, credit, securities, commodities or currency markets (including changes in interest or exchange rates) and any government shutdowns;

 

·tariffs, sanctions, trade policies, executive orders or similar applicable laws, orders or policies, or any trade disputes, “trade wars” or similar actions, or any threats of any of the foregoing;

 

·changes or conditions generally affecting any of the industries in which Iridium or Rocket Lab, as applicable, or their respective subsidiaries operate;

 

·geopolitical conditions, the outbreak or escalation of hostilities, acts of war, armed conflict, sabotage, terrorism, cyberattacks, protests, riots, strikes, global health conditions (including any epidemic, pandemic or disease outbreak) or fires, floods, earthquakes, weather events or other disasters, or any action taken by any governmental authority in response to any of the foregoing;

 

·the execution, delivery and performance of the Merger Agreement or the announcement or consummation of the transactions contemplated by the Merger Agreement or the identity of, or any facts or circumstances relating to, the other party or its affiliates (including the impact on relationships with customers, suppliers, service providers, employees, governmental authorities or other persons, and any related stockholder or derivative litigation);

 

·any failure to meet any internal or published budgets, projections, forecasts or predictions of financial performance or integration synergies for any period;

 

·changes in the price or trading volume of the applicable party’s securities or changes in its credit ratings;

 

·any actions expressly required to be taken, or expressly prohibited from being taken, pursuant to the terms of the Merger Agreement (other than the ordinary-course conduct covenant); and

 

·any Effect arising out of any of the matters set forth in the corresponding disclosure schedule.

 

With respect to the failures and changes described in the clauses relating to meeting projections and changes in stock price, trading volume or credit ratings, the underlying facts giving rise to or contributing to such failure

or change (if not otherwise excluded) may be taken into account in determining whether there has been, or would reasonably be expected to be, a material adverse effect. In addition, in the case of the first six clauses above, to the extent the applicable Effect is disproportionately adverse to Iridium or Rocket Lab, as applicable, and their respective subsidiaries, taken as a whole, relative to others in the industry or industries in which they operate, only the incremental disproportionate adverse impact may be taken into account in determining whether a material adverse effect has occurred or would reasonably be expected to occur.

 

Covenants and Agreements

 

Conduct of Business

 

Each of Rocket Lab and Iridium agreed to covenants restricting, subject to specified exceptions, the conduct of its respective business between signing and the First Effective Time (or earlier termination of the Merger Agreement).

 

Interim Operations of Iridium

 

From the date of the Merger Agreement until the First Effective Time, except with the prior written consent of Rocket Lab (such consent not to be unreasonably withheld, conditioned or delayed), as required or expressly contemplated or permitted by the Merger Agreement, as set forth in the confidential disclosures exchanged between Iridium and Rocket Lab, or as required by applicable law, Iridium will, and will cause its subsidiaries to, (i)(A) use commercially reasonable efforts to conduct its business in the ordinary course of business, (B) use reasonable best efforts to preserve substantially intact in all material respects its current business organization, lines of business, material permits, the Iridium Satellites, the Iridium Satellite Constellation (Iridium’s satellites in orbit, together with the related operations, infrastructure and assets used to provide global coverage and operate Iridium’s business) and all other material assets, and (C) use commercially reasonable efforts to keep available the services of its and their respective current officers and other key employees and preserve in all material respects its relationships with material customers, suppliers, distributors, manufacturers, resellers, landlords, creditors, licensors, licensees, employees, governmental authorities and other persons with which it has material business relations. No action (or failure to act) with respect to a matter addressed by any of the specific restrictions described below will constitute a breach of the general obligations described in the preceding sentence unless that action or failure to act would independently constitute a breach of the applicable specific restriction.

 

In addition, during the same period and subject to the same exceptions, Iridium will not, and will cause its subsidiaries not to:

 

·amend its certificate of incorporation, bylaws or other similar organizational documents (other than immaterial changes to the organizational documents of Iridium’s subsidiaries);

 

·(i) split, combine or reclassify any shares of its capital stock, (ii) declare, set aside or pay any dividend or other distribution (whether in cash, shares or property or any combination thereof) in respect of its capital stock, other than (x) quarterly dividends paid to Iridium’s stockholders in the ordinary course of business and (y) dividends or other such distributions by a wholly owned subsidiary to Iridium or another wholly owned subsidiary, or (iii) redeem, repurchase or otherwise acquire or offer to redeem, repurchase or otherwise acquire any Iridium securities, except as required by the terms of Iridium equity awards;

 

·issue, deliver or sell, or authorize the issuance, delivery or sale of, any Iridium securities or securities of its subsidiaries, other than the issuance of (i) any Iridium equity awards in the ordinary course of business under Iridium’s stock plans, (ii) Iridium Common Stock upon the vesting, exercise or settlement of Iridium equity awards in accordance with their terms, or (iii) subsidiary securities to Iridium or a wholly owned subsidiary;

 

·acquire (by merger, consolidation, acquisition of shares or assets or otherwise), directly or indirectly, any securities or businesses, other than (i) pursuant to existing contracts or commitments set forth in the confidential disclosures exchanged between Iridium and Rocket Lab or (ii) in connection with treasury cash management practices in the ordinary course of business;

 

116

 

 

·enter into any new material line of business outside the existing business of Iridium and its subsidiaries;

 

·sell, lease, assign, license or otherwise transfer, abandon or otherwise dispose, voluntarily permit to lapse or expire, or encumber or subject to any lien (in each case, other than liens permitted under the Merger Agreement) any of its businesses, property or assets, other than (i) pursuant to contracts in effect as of the date of the Merger Agreement, (ii) transfers among Iridium and its subsidiaries that do not result in material taxes, costs or other liabilities, or (iii) with respect to intellectual property, natural statutory expirations of Iridium-owned intellectual property and non-exclusive licenses or sublicenses granted in the ordinary course of business;

 

·make or authorize any capital expenditure other than capital expenditures provided for in the capital expenditure budgets set forth in the confidential disclosures exchanged between Iridium and Rocket Lab;

 

·make any material loans, advances or capital contributions to, or investments in, any other person, other than (i) intercompany loans, advances, contributions or investments among Iridium and its wholly owned subsidiaries that do not result in material taxes, costs or other liabilities, and (ii) trade credit and similar loans and advances to customers and suppliers in the ordinary course of business that are not material;

 

·(x) incur, assume or guarantee any indebtedness for borrowed money (or guarantees thereof) in excess of $5,000,000, other than (i) borrowings under Iridium’s existing credit agreement as in effect on the date of the Merger Agreement or (ii) indebtedness incurred between Iridium and any of its wholly owned subsidiaries or between any of such wholly owned subsidiaries and guarantees thereof, in each case that do not result in material taxes, costs or other liabilities, or (y) terminate or amend Iridium’s existing credit agreement in any manner materially adverse to Rocket Lab;

 

·other than in connection with stockholder proceedings relating to the Merger Agreement or the transactions contemplated by it (which are addressed separately), commence or settle any proceeding requiring a payment by Iridium in excess of $1,000,000 individually or $5,000,000 in the aggregate (net of amounts covered by insurance or third-party indemnification), and provided the payment, discharge, settlement or satisfaction of such proceeding does not include material equitable relief or a material non-monetary obligation or an admission of material wrongdoing;

 

·enter into, materially amend or waive a material right under, or terminate, a Material Contract, other than in the ordinary course of business, and, in the case of entering into a contract, subject to a further restriction on entering into any contract that would (had it existed at signing) have been a Material Contract of specified types — namely, contracts relating to the acquisition or disposition of material securities, assets or businesses; agreements with affiliates, directors, executive officers or holders of 5% or more of Iridium’s shares; contracts that limit in any material respect the freedom of Iridium or its subsidiaries to compete or that contain material exclusivity, “most favored nation” or similar preferential provisions; material partnership, joint venture, joint development or strategic alliance contracts; contracts creating a lien on a material Telecommunications Permit; contracts under which Iridium or its subsidiaries has granted a lien on its assets or equity interests; and contracts under which Iridium or its subsidiaries has material indemnification obligations;

 

·other than as required by the terms of an Iridium benefit plan or as set forth in the confidential disclosures exchanged between Iridium and Rocket Lab, (i) grant, increase or amend any change-of-control, retention, transaction-related, severance or termination pay, (ii) accelerate the vesting, funding or payment of any compensation or benefits (including any Iridium equity award), (iii) increase the salary, wages or other compensation or benefits of any Iridium service provider, (iv) establish, adopt, terminate or materially amend any Iridium benefit plan, or (v) hire or terminate any Iridium service provider at the level of vice president or above, other than terminations for cause;

 

·become a party to, establish, adopt, materially amend, commence participation in or terminate any collective bargaining agreement or other agreement with a labor union, works council or similar organization;

 

·effectuate a “plant closing” or “mass layoff” (each as defined in the WARN Act) requiring notice under the WARN Act;

 

117

 

 

·adopt a plan of complete or partial liquidation, dissolution, restructuring, recapitalization or other reorganization (other than the Mergers);

 

·change its methods of accounting, except as required by concurrent changes in GAAP or in Regulation S-X under the Exchange Act;

 

·with respect to real property, (i) agree to purchase or sell any interest in real property, (ii) grant a security interest (other than a permitted lien) in any real property, (iii) enter into any lease, sublease, license or other occupancy agreement with respect to any real property other than in the ordinary course of business, (iv) materially amend, waive a material right under, or exercise a material extension or expansion right under, any Iridium lease other than in the ordinary course of business, or (v) violate or terminate any Iridium lease;

 

·with respect to taxes, (i) make (other than consistent with past practice), change or revoke any material tax election, (ii) change any tax accounting period, (iii) amend any U.S. federal income or other material tax return, (iv) make any material change in its methods of tax accounting, (v) enter into any material tax sharing or similar arrangement (other than ordinary-course commercial agreements not primarily related to tax, or arrangements solely among Iridium and its subsidiaries) or any closing agreement, (vi) settle or compromise any material tax claim, audit or assessment, or (vii) surrender any right to claim a material tax refund;

 

·take any action that would reasonably be expected to prevent the Mergers from qualifying for the Intended Tax Treatment, provided that Iridium is not required to take, or refrain from taking, any action in order to satisfy the Equity Threshold Condition;

 

·with respect to the Iridium Satellites and the Iridium Satellite Constellation and Iridium’s telecommunications licenses and authorizations issued by telecommunications regulators (the “Telecommunications Permits”), (i) re-orbit or dispose of any Iridium Satellite or materially change its operation of any Iridium Satellite or the Iridium Satellite Constellation in an adverse manner, other than in exigent operational circumstances beyond Iridium’s control (and, except in the case of such circumstances, only after obtaining any required prior governmental authorization); (ii) intentionally take or fail to take any action that would reasonably be expected to result in material degradation, disruption or other adverse modification of the Iridium Satellite Constellation; (iii) transfer, assign, sell, lease, license, encumber, surrender, abandon, allow to lapse, fail to make required filings for, fail to renew, or fail to prosecute or defend any Telecommunications Permit material to Iridium’s business; (iv) intentionally take or fail to take any action that would reasonably be expected to result in the material loss, impairment, suspension, revocation, cancellation or non-renewal of any material Telecommunications Permit; (v) grant or incur any lien (other than a permitted lien) on any material Telecommunications Permit; or (vi) seek or permit any assignment, modification or partition of any material Telecommunications Permit; or

 

·commit to do any of the foregoing.

 

Interim Operations of Rocket Lab

 

From the date of the Merger Agreement until the First Effective Time, except with the prior written consent of Iridium (such consent not to be unreasonably withheld, conditioned or delayed), as required or expressly contemplated by the Merger Agreement, as set forth in the confidential disclosures exchanged between Iridium and Rocket Lab, or as required by applicable law, Rocket Lab will, and will cause its subsidiaries to, use commercially reasonable efforts to conduct its business in the ordinary course of business. No action (or failure to act) with respect to a matter addressed by any of the specific restrictions described below will constitute a breach of that general obligation unless that action or failure to act would independently constitute a breach of the applicable specific restriction. In addition, during the same period and subject to the same exceptions, Rocket Lab will not:

 

·amend its certificate of incorporation or bylaws (i) in a manner that would reasonably be expected to impair the rights of Iridium’s stockholders relative to the existing holders of Rocket Lab Common Stock or (ii) in a manner that would prevent, materially impair or materially delay the ability of Rocket Lab, Merger Sub I or Merger Sub II to consummate the Mergers;

 

118

 

 

·(i) split, combine, subdivide, reduce or reclassify any shares of its capital stock, or (ii) declare, set aside or pay any dividend or other distribution in respect of its capital stock;

 

·merge or consolidate Rocket Lab, Merger Sub I or Merger Sub II, or adopt a plan of complete or partial liquidation, dissolution, restructuring, recapitalization, merger, consolidation or other reorganization of Rocket Lab, Merger Sub I or Merger Sub II (other than the Mergers);

 

·take or fail to take any action that would reasonably be expected to prevent the Mergers from qualifying for the Intended Tax Treatment, provided that Rocket Lab is not required to take, or refrain from taking, any action in order to satisfy the Equity Threshold Condition; or

 

·agree, resolve or commit to do any of the foregoing.

 

No Shop

 

Immediately following the execution of the Merger Agreement, Iridium agreed to cease, and to cause its subsidiaries, directors, officers and financial advisors to cease, and to use reasonable best efforts to cause its and its subsidiaries’ other representatives to cease, any existing solicitation of, or discussions or negotiations with, any third party relating to any Acquisition Proposal or potential Acquisition Proposal. Within 48 hours after the execution of the Merger Agreement, Iridium agreed to request that each person that had previously executed a confidentiality agreement in connection with its consideration of an Acquisition Proposal return or destroy the information furnished to it and to terminate that person’s access to any physical or electronic data rooms relating to a possible Acquisition Proposal.

 

An “Acquisition Proposal” means (other than the Mergers) any indication of interest, proposal or offer from any person or group, other than Rocket Lab and its subsidiaries, relating to any (i) direct or indirect acquisition of assets of Iridium or its subsidiaries (including securities of Iridium’s subsidiaries) equal to 20% or more of the consolidated assets of Iridium, or to which 20% or more of the revenues or earnings of Iridium on a consolidated basis are attributable, (ii) direct or indirect acquisition or issuance of 20% or more of any class of equity or voting securities of Iridium, or of equity or voting securities of Iridium or its subsidiaries representing, directly or indirectly, 20% or more of Iridium’s consolidated assets, revenues or earnings, (iii) tender offer or exchange offer that, if consummated, would result in a person or group beneficially owning 20% or more of any class of equity or voting securities of Iridium or any equity or voting securities of Iridium representing 20% or more of the consolidated assets of Iridium and its subsidiaries or 20% or more of the revenues or earnings of Iridium and its subsidiaries on a consolidated basis, or (iv) merger, consolidation, share exchange, business combination, joint venture, reorganization, recapitalization, liquidation, dissolution or similar transaction involving Iridium or any of its subsidiaries that would result in a person or group acquiring 20% or more of Iridium’s consolidated assets, revenues or earnings or 20% or more of any class of its equity or voting securities.

 

Except as described below, until the earlier of the termination of the Merger Agreement and the First Effective Time, Iridium will not, and will cause its subsidiaries, directors, officers and financial advisors not to, and will use reasonable best efforts to cause its and its subsidiaries’ other representatives not to, directly or indirectly:

 

·solicit, initiate or take any action to knowingly facilitate or encourage the submission of any inquiry or proposal that constitutes, or would reasonably be expected to lead to, any Acquisition Proposal;

 

·solicit, initiate or participate in any discussions or negotiations with, furnish any material nonpublic information relating to Iridium or any of its subsidiaries to, afford access to the business, properties, assets, books, records or representatives of Iridium or any of its subsidiaries to, or otherwise knowingly cooperate with, any third party, in each case relating to any inquiry or proposal that constitutes, or would reasonably be expected to lead to, any Acquisition Proposal;

 

·effect an Adverse Recommendation Change; or

 

·approve, authorize, recommend or enter into any letter of intent, memorandum of understanding, agreement in principle, merger agreement, acquisition agreement or other similar arrangement relating to an Acquisition Proposal, other than an acceptable confidentiality agreement.

 

119

 

 

The Merger Agreement does not prohibit Iridium from waiving any “standstill” or similar restriction to the extent required to allow a third party to confidentially submit an Acquisition Proposal, but only to the extent the Iridium Board determines in good faith, after consultation with its outside legal counsel and financial advisor, that the failure to do so would reasonably be expected to violate the directors’ fiduciary duties under applicable law.

 

An “Adverse Recommendation Change” means any of the following: (i) withdrawing, withholding, qualifying or modifying, or failing to include in the proxy statement/prospectus, the recommendation of the Iridium Board that Iridium stockholders adopt the Merger Agreement; (ii) authorizing, adopting, approving, recommending or otherwise declaring advisable, or publicly proposing to do so, any Acquisition Proposal; (iii) failing to publicly recommend against a publicly disclosed Acquisition Proposal upon Rocket Lab’s request (though Iridium is not required to do so more than once per Acquisition Proposal or per material modification of it); or (iv) failing to recommend, in a Schedule 14D-9, against any Acquisition Proposal that is a tender or exchange offer within 10 business days after its commencement.

 

Exceptions. Notwithstanding these restrictions, at any time prior to receipt of the Iridium Stockholder Approval:

 

·Iridium and its representatives may, subject to entry into an acceptable confidentiality agreement and prior written notice to Rocket Lab, engage in discussions or negotiations with, and furnish nonpublic information and afford access to, a third party that has made a bona fide Acquisition Proposal that did not arise from a material breach of the non-solicitation provisions, if the Iridium Board determines in good faith, after consultation with its outside legal counsel and financial advisor, that the Acquisition Proposal constitutes or would reasonably be expected to lead to a Superior Proposal and that failure to take such action would reasonably be expected to violate the directors’ fiduciary duties under applicable law. Any nonpublic information provided to the third party that was not previously provided to Rocket Lab must be provided to Rocket Lab within 24 hours; and

 

·subject to the notice and matching-rights procedures described below, the Iridium Board may (i) in response to such a bona fide written Acquisition Proposal, effect an Adverse Recommendation Change or terminate the Merger Agreement to concurrently enter into a definitive agreement providing for the Superior Proposal, if the board determines in good faith, after consultation with its outside legal counsel, that the Acquisition Proposal constitutes a Superior Proposal and that failure to act would reasonably be expected to violate the directors’ fiduciary duties under applicable law, or (ii) in response to an Intervening Event, effect an Adverse Recommendation Change, if the board determines in good faith, after consultation with its outside legal counsel and financial advisor, that failure to do so would reasonably be expected to violate the directors’ fiduciary duties under applicable law.

 

A “Superior Proposal” means a bona fide written Acquisition Proposal (substituting “50%” for each reference to “20%” in the definition of that term) that did not arise from a material breach of the non-solicitation provisions and that the Iridium Board determines in good faith, after consultation with its outside legal counsel and financial advisor, is more favorable from a financial point of view to Iridium’s stockholders than the Mergers, taking into account all relevant financial, regulatory, financing, conditionality, legal and other factors and any changes to the terms of the Merger Agreement proposed by Rocket Lab.

 

An “Intervening Event” generally means a material event, fact, circumstance, development or occurrence that was not known to or reasonably foreseeable by the Iridium Board as of the date of the Merger Agreement (or the consequences or magnitude of which were not known or reasonably foreseeable) and that becomes known to the board before receipt of the Iridium Stockholder Approval, and that does not relate to an Acquisition Proposal. An Intervening Event does not include Iridium’s exceeding revenue or earnings forecasts or changes in the market price or trading volume of Iridium Common Stock (although the underlying causes may be considered).

 

Required notices. Prior to the earlier of the termination of the Merger Agreement and the First Effective Time, Iridium is required to notify Rocket Lab in writing promptly (and in any event within 24 hours) of its receipt of any Acquisition Proposal, or any offer, inquiry, request, proposal or indication of interest that could reasonably be expected to lead to an Acquisition Proposal, or any amendment or modification to the material terms of any of the foregoing. The notice must include, to the extent then known, the identity of the third party, the material terms and conditions (including any draft definitive documentation), and copies of documents and written communications setting forth the material terms.

 

120

 

 

Matching rights. Neither the Iridium Board nor Iridium may effect an Adverse Recommendation Change in response to a Superior Proposal or an Intervening Event, or terminate the Merger Agreement to enter into a definitive agreement for a Superior Proposal, unless: (i) Iridium has notified Rocket Lab in writing, at least four business days in advance, of its intention to take the action, specifying the reasons and (in the case of a Superior Proposal) attaching the proposed agreements and related information (or, for an Intervening Event, a reasonably detailed description of the facts); (ii) during that four-business-day period, Iridium and its representatives have negotiated with Rocket Lab in good faith (to the extent Rocket Lab wishes to negotiate) over any adjustments to the Merger Agreement that Rocket Lab proposes; and (iii) at the end of the period, the Iridium Board has considered in good faith any binding revisions proposed by Rocket Lab and determined in good faith, after consultation with its outside legal counsel and financial advisors, that the Acquisition Proposal remains a Superior Proposal (or that the Intervening Event still warrants the change) and that failure to act would reasonably be expected to violate the directors’ fiduciary duties under applicable law. If the financial or other material terms of the Superior Proposal change, a new notice is required and a new negotiation period begins, which is three business days for each such subsequent change.

 

In addition, the non-solicitation provisions do not prevent Iridium or its board of directors from taking and disclosing to Iridium’s stockholders a position contemplated by Rules 14d-9 and 14e-2(a) under the Exchange Act, issuing a customary “stop, look and listen” communication, making any disclosure to stockholders that the board determines in good faith is legally required, or contacting a person that has made an Acquisition Proposal solely to clarify its terms or to inform the person of the restrictions in the non-solicitation provisions. However, any such disclosure relating to an Acquisition Proposal that does not expressly reaffirm the Iridium board’s recommendation will be deemed an Adverse Recommendation Change (other than a “stop, look and listen” communication).

 

Employee Benefits

 

From the First Effective Time and ending on the date that is 12 months thereafter (or such earlier date that any continuing Iridium employee terminates employment), Rocket Lab shall cause each employee of Iridium or its subsidiaries as of immediately prior to the First Effective Time whose employment continues as of the First Effective Time (each, a “Continuing Employee”) to receive (i) an annual rate of salary and wages that is no less favorable than the annual rate of salary and wages provided to such Continuing Employee as of immediately prior to the First Effective Time, (ii) target cash incentive opportunities (excluding any equity compensation, change in control and retention benefits or similar payments) that are no less favorable than the target cash incentive opportunities provided to such Continuing Employee prior to the First Effective Time (provided that Rocket Lab, in its discretion and to the extent (and on the same basis as is) generally applicable to annual incentives payable to other employees of Rocket Lab and its affiliates, may cause payments with respect to any such earned cash incentives to be paid in the form of cash or fully vested shares of Rocket Lab Common Stock, or a combination thereof), (iii) severance benefits and protections no less favorable than those described in the disclosure schedule to the Merger Agreement and (iv) all other compensation and employee benefits that are substantially comparable in the aggregate to all other compensation and employee benefits provided to similarly situated employees of Rocket Lab and its subsidiaries (excluding any equity compensation, change in control and retention benefits or similar payments and defined benefit pension and retiree medical or life insurance benefits).

 

To the extent the short-term incentive bonuses for a Continuing Employee for the performance period in which the First Effective Time occurs (or the immediately preceding performance period) remain unpaid as of Closing, Rocket Lab shall pay bonuses provided under Iridium’s applicable short-term performance bonus program for such applicable fiscal year in which the First Effective Time occurs (or the immediately preceding performance period) to such Continuing Employee based on the incentive award earned by such Continuing Employee based on the actual level of performance for the applicable performance period as provided under such incentive plan (the “Short-Term Incentives”). Any such Short-Term Incentives shall be paid by Rocket Lab or a subsidiary of Rocket Lab (including the Surviving Entity), subject to applicable withholding, at the time or times that the Short-Term Incentives would normally be paid by Iridium, but in all events within 60 days following the end of the applicable period relating to the Short-Term Incentives; provided that in the event of a Continuing Employee’s termination of employment (i) under circumstances that entitle the Continuing Employee to severance benefits under a severance plan or agreement or (ii) otherwise by Rocket Lab or any of its subsidiaries without “cause”, in each case, following the First Effective Time, any such Short-Term Incentive applicable to such Continuing Employee as of the time of such termination shall be paid on a pro-rated basis, based on such Continuing Employee’s service through the applicable performance period, and calculated based on actual achievement of the Short-Term Incentives for the applicable performance

 

121

 

 

period determined in accordance with the Merger Agreement, subject to the Continuing Employee’s execution and non-revocation of a release of claims (and provided that no such payment to any terminated Continuing Employee shall be made if it would result in a duplication of benefits with respect to any pro-rated bonus payout under any material Iridium compensation and benefit arrangement (an “Iridium Company Plan”)).

 

Rocket Lab shall cause the Surviving Entity and any of its subsidiaries (and any of their respective third-party insurance providers or third-party administrators) to use commercially reasonable efforts to (i) waive all limitations as to any pre-existing condition or waiting periods with respect to participation and coverage requirements applicable to each Continuing Employee under any employee benefit plan in which such Continuing Employees may be eligible to participate as of or after the First Effective Time, to the extent pre-existing conditions and waiting periods did not apply or were satisfied under a similar Iridium Company Plan prior to the First Effective Time, and (ii) credit each Continuing Employee, as of and after the First Effective Time, for any copayments, deductibles, offsets or similar payments made under the relevant group health plan of Iridium or any of its subsidiaries during the plan year that includes the First Effective Time for purposes of satisfying any applicable copayment, deductible, offset or similar requirements under the comparable group health plans of Rocket Lab, Merger Sub I, Merger Sub II or any of their respective subsidiaries (including the Surviving Entity and its subsidiaries). In addition, as of the First Effective Time, Rocket Lab shall use commercially reasonable efforts to cause the Surviving Entity and any applicable subsidiary to give all Continuing Employees full credit for such Continuing Employees’ service with Iridium or any of its subsidiaries for all purposes (including eligibility, vesting, accruals and determination of level of benefits) under any compensation and benefit plans, programs, policies, agreements and arrangements maintained by Rocket Lab, Merger Sub I, Merger Sub II or an applicable subsidiary (including the Surviving Entity and its subsidiaries) in which any Continuing Employee may be eligible to participate after the First Effective Time, to the same extent and for the same purpose that such service was credited for under any similar Iridium Company Plan immediately prior to the First Effective Time, provided that such credit for service shall not apply to the extent it would result in a duplication of benefits or compensation or credit with respect to any benefit that is frozen as to eligibility, accrual or any other respect.

 

Director and Officer Liability

 

Without limiting any other rights that any Indemnified Person may have pursuant to any employment agreement or indemnification agreement, for six years after the First Effective Time, Rocket Lab shall cause the Surviving Entity and the Surviving Corporation to indemnify and hold harmless the present and former directors, officers and other fiduciaries of Iridium and its subsidiaries and any individuals serving in such capacity at or with respect to other persons at Iridium’s or its subsidiaries’ request (each, an “Indemnified Person”) from and against any losses, damages, liabilities, costs, expenses (including attorneys’ fees), judgments, fines, penalties and amounts paid in settlement (including all interest, assessments and other charges paid or payable in connection with or in respect of any thereof) in respect of the Indemnified Persons’ having served in any such capacity prior to the First Effective Time, in each case to the fullest extent permitted by the DGCL or provided under the Iridium Certificate of Incorporation and the Iridium Bylaws or other organizational documents of Iridium or any of its subsidiaries in effect as of the date of the Merger Agreement. If any Indemnified Person is made party to any proceeding arising out of or relating to matters that would be indemnifiable pursuant to the immediately preceding sentence, Rocket Lab will, and will cause the Surviving Entity and the Surviving Corporation to, advance fees, costs and expenses (including attorneys’ fees and disbursements) as incurred by such Indemnified Person in connection with and prior to the final disposition of such proceeding.

 

For six years after the First Effective Time, Rocket Lab will cause to be maintained in effect provisions in the certificate of incorporation, bylaws or other organizational documents of the Surviving Entity and its subsidiaries (or in such documents of any successor to the business of the Surviving Entity or any such subsidiary) regarding elimination of liability of directors, indemnification of directors, officers and other fiduciaries and advancement of fees, costs and expenses that are no less advantageous to the intended beneficiaries than the corresponding provisions in existence on the date of the Merger Agreement. Rocket Lab will also cause the Surviving Entity and its subsidiaries to, honor and comply with their respective obligations under any indemnification agreement with any Indemnified Person that was made available to Rocket Lab, and not amend, repeal or otherwise modify any such agreement in any manner that would adversely affect any right of any Indemnified Person thereunder.

 

Prior to the First Effective Time, Iridium will, or if Iridium is unable to, Rocket Lab will cause the Surviving Entity as of the First Effective Time to, obtain and fully pay the premium for the noncancelable “tail” or “runoff”

 

122

 

 

extension of the directors’ and officers’ liability coverage of Iridium’s existing directors’ and officers’ insurance policies and Iridium’s existing fiduciary liability insurance policies (collectively, “D&O Insurance”), which D&O Insurance will (i) be for a claims reporting or discovery period of at least six years from and after the First Effective Time with respect to any claim related to any period of time at or prior to the First Effective Time, (ii) be from Iridium’s current insurance carrier with respect to D&O Insurance or, if unavailable, from an insurance carrier with the same or better credit rating as Iridium’s current insurance carrier with respect to D&O Insurance and (iii) have terms, conditions, retentions and limits of liability that are no less favorable than the coverage provided under Iridium’s existing policies as of the date of the Merger Agreement with respect to any actual or alleged error, misstatement, misleading statement, act, omission, neglect, breach of duty or any matter claimed against an Indemnified Person by reason of his or her having served in such capacity that existed or occurred at or prior to the First Effective Time (including in connection with the Merger Agreement or the transactions contemplated by the Merger Agreement). However, Iridium, Rocket Lab and the Surviving Entity will not be required to expend for such D&O Insurance an aggregate premium amount in excess of 300% of the premium amount per annum for Iridium’s existing directors’ and officers’ insurance policies and Iridium’s existing fiduciary liability insurance policies. If the aggregate premiums of such insurance coverage exceed such amount, the Surviving Entity shall be obligated to obtain a policy with the greatest coverage available, with respect to matters occurring prior to the First Effective Time, for a cost not exceeding such amount.

 

If Rocket Lab or the Surviving Entity or any of its successors or assigns (i) consolidates with or merges into any other person and is not the continuing or surviving corporation or entity of such consolidation or merger or (ii) transfers or conveys all or substantially all of its properties and assets to any person, then, in each such case, to the extent necessary, proper provision shall be made so that the successors and assigns of Rocket Lab or the Surviving Entity, as the case may be, shall assume the obligations set forth in the provisions described in this section titled “—Director and Officer Liability”. The provisions described in this section titled, “—Director and Officer Liability” are intended to be in addition to any rights such person may have under the Iridium Certificate of Incorporation, the Iridium Bylaws or the certificate of incorporation or bylaws of any of Iridium’s subsidiaries, under the DGCL or under any agreement of any Indemnified Person with Iridium or any of its subsidiaries that was made available to Rocket Lab.

 

Other Covenants

 

The Merger Agreement contains certain other covenants and agreements, including covenants and agreements relating to, among other matters:

 

·confidentiality and access to information;

 

·delisting of Iridium Common Stock from Nasdaq and deregistration under the Exchange Act;

 

·approvals, consents, waivers and confirmations from certain third parties;

 

·listing of the Rocket Lab Common Stock to be issued in the Mergers on Nasdaq;

 

·cooperation regarding public announcements; and

 

·Rule 16b-3 exemptions for certain transactions by directors and officers.

 

Iridium Stockholder Meeting and Recommendation of Iridium’s Board of Directors

 

Iridium will (a) promptly after the registration statement is declared effective by the SEC, duly call and give notice of, and commence mailing of the proxy statement/prospectus to the holders of Iridium Common Stock as of the record date established for, a meeting of holders of Iridium Common Stock for purposes of seeking Iridium Stockholder Approval, (b) initiate a “broker search” in accordance with Rule 14a-13 of the Exchange Act as necessary to cause Iridium to comply with its obligations set forth in the foregoing clause ‎(a) and (c) as soon as reasonably practicable following the commencement of the mailing of the proxy statement/prospectus pursuant to the foregoing clause ‎(a), convene and hold the special meeting no sooner than 25 days and no later than 35 days after the mailing of the proxy statement/prospectus to the holders of Iridium Common Stock, in each case in accordance with the DGCL and applicable requirements of Nasdaq and other applicable law. Iridium may adjourn or postpone the special meeting to a later date (1) with the prior written consent of Rocket Lab or (2) to the extent Iridium believes in good faith that such adjournment or postponement is reasonably necessary (a) to ensure that any required

 

123

 

 

supplement or amendment to the proxy statement/prospectus is provided to the holders of Iridium Common Stock within a reasonable amount of time in advance of the special meeting, (b) to allow reasonable additional time to solicit additional proxies necessary to obtain Iridium Stockholder Approval, (c) to ensure that there are sufficient shares of Iridium Common Stock represented (either in person or by proxy) and voting to constitute a quorum necessary to conduct the business of the special meeting or (d) otherwise where required to comply with applicable law (including fiduciary duties). Iridium may also adjourn or postpone the special meeting to a later date designated by Rocket Lab to the extent Iridium believes in good faith that such adjournment or postponement is reasonably necessary (1) to allow reasonable additional time to solicit additional proxies necessary to obtain the Iridium Stockholder Approval or (2) to ensure that there are sufficient shares of Iridium Common Stock represented (either in person or by proxy) and voting to constitute a quorum necessary to conduct the business of the special meeting. However, Iridium shall not, and shall not be required to, adjourn or postpone the special meeting for more than 10 days each time without the prior written consent of Rocket Lab.

 

Except as permitted by the provisions described in the section titled “—No Shop” and this section titled “—Iridium Special Meeting and Recommendation of the Iridium Board,” the Iridium Board shall recommend that the holders of Iridium Common Stock adopt the Merger Agreement and Iridium shall (i) subject to the provisions described in the section titled “—No Shop,” include the recommendation of the Iridium Board in the proxy statement/prospectus, (ii) use its reasonable best efforts to obtain the Iridium Stockholder Approval and (iii) otherwise comply in all material respects with all legal requirements applicable to such meeting. At the special meeting, Iridium shall submit a proposal to obtain the Iridium Stockholder Approval and shall not submit any other proposal (other than a “say on golden parachute compensation” proposal and a customary proposal to adjourn the special meeting) without the prior written consent of Rocket Lab.

 

Regulatory Undertakings

 

Subject to the terms and conditions of the Merger Agreement and this section titled “—Regulatory Undertakings,” Iridium and Rocket Lab will use reasonable best efforts to take, and shall cause their respective affiliates to use reasonable best efforts to take, all actions, and do, or cause to be done, all things necessary, proper or advisable under applicable law to consummate the transactions contemplated by the Merger Agreement as soon as practicable (and in any event, at least five business days prior to the End Date), including (i) preparing and filing as promptly as practicable with any governmental authority or other third party all documentation to effect all necessary, proper or advisable filings, notices, petitions, statements, registrations, submissions of information, applications and other documents and (ii) obtaining and maintaining all approvals, consents, registrations, permits, authorizations and other confirmations required to be obtained from any governmental authority that are necessary, proper or advisable to consummate the transactions contemplated by the Merger Agreement, including any notices, authorizations, registrations, approvals, orders, permits, confirmations and consents from any governmental authority that are necessary in connection with the consummation of the transactions contemplated by the Merger Agreement, including to maintain in full force and effect any permits or government contracts following the consummation of the transactions contemplated by the Merger Agreement in accordance with its terms.

 

In furtherance of the foregoing, Iridium and Rocket Lab are required to, and are required to also cause their respective affiliates, as appropriate, to:

 

·

make an appropriate filing of a Notification and Report Form pursuant to the HSR Act with respect to the transactions contemplated by the Merger Agreement with the FTC and the Antitrust Division as promptly as practicable and in any event within ten (10) business days after the date of the Merger Agreement (and such filings shall request early termination of any applicable waiting period under the HSR Act);

 

·make an appropriate filing(s) with the FCC with respect to the transactions contemplated by the Merger Agreement as promptly as practicable and in any event within thirty (30) business days after the date of the Merger Agreement;

 

·make appropriate filing(s) with respect to the transactions contemplated by the Merger Agreement as required to obtain the Required Regulatory Approvals set forth on the confidential schedules delivered between the parties as promptly as practicable and in any event within sixty (60) business days after the date of the Merger Agreement;

 

124

 

 

·make any other required or appropriate notifications, reports and filings pursuant to the other applicable Competition Laws, Foreign Investment Laws or Satellite and Communications Laws as promptly as practicable after the date of the Merger Agreement (and in any event within the required statutory periods under applicable law); and

 

·make any other applications and filing(s) with respect to the transactions contemplated by the Merger Agreement in connection with the Required Regulatory Approvals or as reasonably determined by Rocket Lab (in consultation with Iridium) to be required under applicable law as promptly as practicable after the date of the Merger Agreement (and in any event within the required statutory periods under applicable law), and in each case, furnish to the other party as promptly as practicable all information within its (or its affiliates’) control requested by such other party and required for such other party to make any application or other filing to be made by it pursuant to any applicable law in connection with the transactions contemplated by the Merger Agreement.

 

Rocket Lab and Iridium will (and will cause their respective affiliates to) respond as promptly as practicable to any inquiries received from the FTC, the Antitrust Division, the FCC, the DCSA or any other governmental authority for additional information or documentary material that may be requested pursuant to the HSR Act or any other applicable Competition Laws, Foreign Investment Laws, Satellite and Communications Laws, the NISPOM or other applicable laws, and will cooperate and consult with each other to determine the actions, communications, decisions and strategy for obtaining any consents, clearances, registrations, approvals, permits, waivers, expirations or terminations of waiting periods and authorizations, under the HSR Act, any other Competition Law, any Foreign Investment Law, any Satellite and Communications Law, the NISPOM or any other applicable law in connection with the transactions contemplated by the Merger Agreement, including any Required Regulatory Approvals. However, Rocket Lab will, after consulting with Iridium and considering in good faith the views of Iridium, have final decision-making authority with respect to such actions, communications, decisions and strategy. No party will extend any waiting period under the HSR Act or under any other applicable Competition Laws, Foreign Investment Laws, Satellite and Communications Laws, the NISPOM or other applicable law or enter into any agreement with the FTC, the Antitrust Division, the FCC, the DCSA or any other governmental authority not to consummate the transactions contemplated by the Merger Agreement, except with the prior written consent of the other parties (which will not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned or delayed).

 

If any objections are asserted by a governmental authority with respect to the transactions contemplated by the Merger Agreement under the HSR Act, any other applicable Competition Law, any Foreign Investment Law, any Satellite and Communications Law, the NISPOM or in connection with any Required Regulatory Approval, or if any Proceeding is instituted or threatened by any governmental authority challenging any of the transactions contemplated by the Merger Agreement, Rocket Lab and Iridium will use reasonable best efforts to take, or cause to be taken (including by causing their affiliates to take), all actions necessary to resolve such objections as promptly as practicable (and in any event, at least five business days prior to the End Date). If there are any such objections or proceedings, Rocket Lab will, and will cause its subsidiaries and affiliates to, use reasonable best efforts to take all actions as may be necessary to obtain any authorization, consent or approval of a governmental authority or to avoid or eliminate any impediments under the HSR Act, any other Competition Law, any Foreign Investment Law, any Satellite and Communications Law, the NISPOM or any other applicable law or in connection with any Required Regulatory Approval so as to enable the consummation of the transactions contemplated by the Merger Agreement to occur as promptly as practicable and in any event no later than five business days prior to the End Date. Such actions include:

 

·agreeing to hold separate, sell, license, divest or otherwise dispose of any of the businesses or properties or assets of Rocket Lab, Iridium or any of their respective affiliates;

 

·terminating, amending or assigning any investments or other existing relationships, or any other contractual rights or obligations;

 

·terminating any joint venture or other legal partnership,

 

·granting any right or commercial or other accommodation to, or entering into any contractual or other commercial relationship with, any third party,

 

125

 

 

·imposing limitations on Rocket Lab or any of its affiliates or Iridium or any of its subsidiaries with respect to how they own, retain, conduct or operate all or any portion of their respective businesses or assets,

 

·effectuating any other change or restructuring of Rocket Lab or any of its affiliates, or Iridium or any of its subsidiaries (clauses (i) through (vi), a “Divestiture Action”); and

 

·opposing (A) any administrative or judicial Proceeding that is initiated or threatened to be initiated challenging the Merger Agreement or the consummation of the transactions contemplated by the Merger Agreement (including seeking to have any stay or temporary restraining order entered by any court or other governmental authority vacated or reversed) and (B) any request for, or the entry of, and seek to have vacated or terminated, any order that restrains, prevents or prohibits the consummation of the transactions contemplated by the Merger Agreement, by defending through litigation any Proceeding brought by any governmental authority, and pursuing all available avenues of administrative and judicial appeal.

 

Additionally, Rocket Lab will not, and will cause its subsidiaries and affiliates not to, acquire or agree to acquire any assets or securities or lease any assets (including spectrum rights) if such action would reasonably be expected to make it materially more likely that the expiration of any waiting period or any approval from any governmental authority necessary to consummate the transactions contemplated by the Merger Agreement does not occur, is not obtained or is materially delayed. Notwithstanding anything in this section “—Regulatory Undertakings” or the Merger Agreement to the contrary, Rocket Lab will not be required to effect, agree to effect or propose to effect any Divestiture Action that (x) would reasonably be expected to be material to either Iridium and its subsidiaries, taken as a whole, to Rocket Lab and its subsidiaries, taken as a whole, or to the Combined Company, and (y) is not conditioned upon the consummation of the Mergers. Iridium shall not effect, agree to effect or propose to effect any Divestiture Action without the prior written consent of Rocket Lab. However, at the request of Rocket Lab, Iridium will agree to any Divestiture Action relating to Iridium and its subsidiaries, provided that any such action is conditioned upon the consummation of the Mergers.

 

In connection with the items in this section titled “—Regulatory Undertakings,” Iridium and Rocket Lab will, subject to any information that is designated as competitively sensitive material or redacted as necessary to comply with applicable law or contractual obligations or is legally privileged:

 

·promptly notify the other parties of any substantive communication to that party from the FTC, the Antitrust Division, the FCC, the DCSA, any State Attorney General or any other governmental authority regarding the Merger Agreement or the transactions contemplated by the Merger Agreement and, subject to applicable law, permit the other parties to review, reasonably in advance, any written communication or presentation proposed to be submitted to any governmental authority with respect to the foregoing and consider in good faith any comments such other party may provide thereto;

 

·not agree to participate in any substantive meeting or discussion with any governmental authority in respect of any filings, investigation or inquiry under any Competition Law, any Foreign Investment Law, any Satellite and Communications Law, the NISPOM or any other applicable law in connection with the Merger Agreement or the Mergers and the other transactions contemplated by the Merger Agreement unless in each case it consults with the other parties in advance and, to the extent reasonably practicable and permitted by such governmental authority, gives the other parties the opportunity to attend and participate thereat;

 

·furnish the other parties with copies of all filings (other than Item 4(c) and Item 4(d) documents as defined in the HSR Act) and material correspondences and communications (and memoranda setting forth the substance thereof) between them and their affiliates and their respective representatives, on the one hand, and any governmental authority or members or their respective staffs, on the other hand, with respect to any Competition Law, any Foreign Investment Law, any Satellite and Communications Law, the NISPOM or any other applicable law in connection with the Merger Agreement; and

 

·Iridium and Rocket Lab will consult and cooperate with one another in connection with any analyses, appearances, presentations, memoranda, briefs, arguments, opinions and proposals made or submitted by

 

126

 

 

or on behalf of either party relating to proceedings under any Competition Law, any Foreign Investment Law, any Satellite and Communications Law, the NISPOM or any other applicable law.

 

Additionally, during the period between the date of the Merger Agreement and the Closing, Iridium and its subsidiaries will use reasonable best efforts to keep, maintain and preserve the Telecommunications Permits that are material, individually or in the aggregate, to Iridium and its subsidiaries in full force and effect and in good standing, including by using reasonable best efforts to (i) perform all of material obligations of Iridium or any of its subsidiaries required to be performed under such Telecommunications Permits, (ii) take such steps as are reasonably necessary to renew any such expiring Telecommunications Permits, including preparing and timely filing with the appropriate governmental authority all necessary applications in connection therewith and (iii) refrain from taking any action that would reasonably be expected to result in the suspension, revocation or adverse modification of any such Telecommunications Permit.

 

Conditions to the Mergers

 

The respective obligations of each party to the Merger Agreement to effect the Mergers at the Closing as contemplated by the Merger Agreement will be subject to the fulfillment (or, to the extent permitted by law, written waiver by Rocket Lab or Iridium, as applicable) at or prior to the Closing of the following conditions:

 

·adoption of the Merger Agreement by the stockholders of Iridium in accordance with the DGCL;

 

·the absence of any order or applicable law issued by a governmental authority of competent jurisdiction in specified jurisdictions that has the effect of preventing, impairing, prohibiting, rendering illegal or enjoining the consummation of the Mergers and that remains in effect (a “Legal Restraint”);

 

·the expiration or termination of any applicable waiting period (and any extensions thereof, and the expiration, lapse or waiver of any time period under any timing agreement with a governmental authority) under the HSR Act, and the making, obtaining or receipt of each other required regulatory approval specified in the Merger Agreement (including the required FCC and other satellite and communications approvals), which approvals must remain in full force and effect (or, as applicable, the related waiting periods must have expired or been terminated);

 

·the declaration by the SEC of the effectiveness of the Form S-4 registration statement, and no stop order suspending the effectiveness of the Form S-4 being in effect and no proceedings for such purpose being pending before or threatened by the SEC; and

 

·the approval for listing on Nasdaq of the shares of Rocket Lab Common Stock to be issued in the Mergers.

 

The obligations of Rocket Lab, Merger Sub I and Merger Sub II to effect the Mergers at the Closing as contemplated by the Merger Agreement are further subject to the fulfillment (or, to the extent permitted by law, written waiver by Rocket Lab) of the following conditions:

 

·Iridium shall not have materially breached the covenants required to be performed or complied with by it prior to the Closing;

 

·the representations and warranties of Iridium relating to corporate existence and power, corporate authorization, non-contravention, specified capitalization matters, its subsidiaries, finders’ fees, the opinion of its financial advisor and antitakeover statutes shall be true in all material respects (or, to the extent qualified by materiality or Company Material Adverse Effect, in all respects) as of the date of the Merger Agreement and as of the Closing (except for representations that by their terms address matters only as of another specified time);

 

·the representations and warranties of Iridium relating to its outstanding capitalization shall be true in all respects as of the date of the Merger Agreement and as of the Closing (except for representations that by their terms address matters only as of another specified time), except for any failure to be true and correct that is de minimis;

 

·all other representations and warranties of Iridium set forth in the Merger Agreement (disregarding all materiality and Company Material Adverse Effect qualifications) shall be true in all respects as of the

 

127

 

 

date of the Merger Agreement and as of the Closing (except to the extent such representations expressly relate to an earlier date), except for any failure to be true and correct as has not had, individually or in the aggregate, a Company Material Adverse Effect;

 

·since the date of the Merger Agreement, no Company Material Adverse Effect shall have occurred and be continuing; and

 

·receipt of a certificate, dated as of the Closing Date and signed by a duly authorized officer of Iridium, certifying that the foregoing conditions relating to the accuracy of Iridium’s representations and warranties and the performance of its covenants (and the absence of a Company Material Adverse Effect) have been satisfied.

 

The obligation of Iridium to effect the Mergers at the Closing as contemplated by the Merger Agreement is further subject to the fulfillment (or, to the extent permitted by law, written waiver by Iridium) of the following conditions:

 

·each of Rocket Lab, Merger Sub I and Merger Sub II shall not have materially breached the covenants required to be performed or complied with by it at or prior to the Closing;

 

·the representations and warranties of Rocket Lab, Merger Sub I and Merger Sub II relating to corporate existence and power, corporate authorization, non-contravention, tax treatment, finders’ fees, financing, solvency and ownership of Iridium Common Stock shall be true in all material respects (or, to the extent qualified by materiality or Parent Material Adverse Effect, in all respects) as of the date of the Merger Agreement and as of the Closing (except for representations that by their terms address matters only as of another specified time);

 

·the representations and warranties relating to the capitalization of Rocket Lab shall be true in all respects as of the date of the Merger Agreement and as of the Closing (except for representations that by their terms address matters only as of another specified time), except for any failure to be true and correct that is de minimis;

 

·all other representations and warranties of Rocket Lab, Merger Sub I and Merger Sub II set forth in the Merger Agreement (disregarding all materiality and Parent Material Adverse Effect qualifications) shall be true in all respects as of the date of the Merger Agreement and as of the Closing (except to the extent such representations expressly relate to an earlier date), except for any failure to be true and correct as has not had, individually or in the aggregate, a Parent Material Adverse Effect;

 

·since the date of the Merger Agreement, no Parent Material Adverse Effect shall have occurred and be continuing; and

 

·receipt of a certificate, dated as of the Closing Date and signed by a duly authorized officer of Rocket Lab, certifying that the foregoing conditions relating to the accuracy of the representations and warranties of Rocket Lab, Merger Sub I and Merger Sub II and the performance of their covenants (and the absence of a Parent Material Adverse Effect) have been satisfied.

 

Termination

 

Termination Rights of Iridium and Rocket Lab

 

The Merger Agreement may be terminated and the Mergers may be abandoned at any time prior to the First Effective Time (notwithstanding any approval of the Merger Agreement by Iridium’s stockholders):

 

·by mutual written agreement of Iridium and Rocket Lab;

 

·by either Iridium or Rocket Lab, if:

 

–the Mergers have not been consummated on or before the End Date (June 28, 2027, unless extended, as described in this paragraph); provided that if as of the End Date, specified regulatory conditions (relating to certain Legal Restraints arising under, or the receipt of Required Regulatory Approvals within the scope of, the Competition Laws, Foreign Investment Laws, Satellite and Communications Laws or the NISPOM) have not been satisfied or waived, but

 

128

 

 

all other conditions to Closing have been (or would be capable of being) satisfied or waived, the End Date will be automatically extended to September 28, 2027, and, in the same circumstances, will be further automatically extended to December 28, 2027; provided, further, that this termination right is not available to any party whose breach of the Merger Agreement has caused or resulted in the failure of the Closing to occur on or before the End Date;

 

–any Legal Restraint permanently preventing, prohibiting, rendering illegal or enjoining the consummation of the Mergers has become final and non-appealable; or

 

–The Iridium Stockholder Approval has not been obtained at the special meeting (including any adjournment or postponement thereof) duly convened and at which a vote on the adoption of the Merger Agreement has been taken;

 

·by Rocket Lab, if:

 

–prior to receipt of the Iridium Stockholder Approval, (A) an Adverse Recommendation Change has occurred or (B) Iridium has committed an Intentional Breach of its no-shop and related obligations under Section 6.05 of the Merger Agreement in any material respect; or

 

–Iridium has breached or failed to perform any of its representations, warranties, covenants or agreements in the Merger Agreement, such that the related closing condition would not be satisfied, and such breach or failure is incapable of being cured or, if curable, has not been cured by the date that is 30 business days after Iridium’s receipt of written notice thereof (or, if earlier, one business day prior to the End Date); provided that this termination right is not available if Rocket Lab, Merger Sub I or Merger Sub II is then in breach of the Merger Agreement in a manner that would cause the corresponding Rocket Lab-side closing condition to fail; and

 

·by Iridium, if:

 

–prior to receipt of the Iridium Stockholder Approval, the Iridium Board authorizes Iridium to enter into a definitive written agreement providing for a Superior Proposal in accordance with, and subject to the conditions set forth in, Section 6.05 of the Merger Agreement (with such agreement being entered into substantially concurrently with the termination), provided that concurrently with such termination Iridium pays the Termination Fee; or

 

–Rocket Lab, Merger Sub I or Merger Sub II has breached or failed to perform any of its representations, warranties, covenants or agreements in the Merger Agreement, such that the related closing condition would not be satisfied, and such breach or failure is incapable of being cured or, if curable, has not been cured by the date that is 30 business days after Rocket Lab’s receipt of written notice thereof (or, if earlier, one business day prior to the End Date); provided that this termination right is not available if Iridium is then in breach of the Merger Agreement in a manner that would cause the corresponding Iridium-side closing condition to fail.

 

The party desiring to terminate the Merger Agreement (other than by mutual written agreement) must give notice of such termination to the other parties, specifying the provision pursuant to which the Merger Agreement is being terminated. In specified circumstances, a terminating party may be required to pay the Termination Fee, as described under “—Termination Fees and Other Fees” beginning on page 130.

 

Effect of Termination

 

If the Merger Agreement is terminated in accordance with its terms, it will become void and of no effect, without liability of any party (or any stockholder, director, officer, employee, agent, consultant or representative of any party) to the other parties, except that no such termination will relieve any party of liability or damages resulting from fraud or from an intentional and material breach of the Merger Agreement (an “Intentional Breach”). The Confidentiality Agreement and specified provisions of the Merger Agreement—including those relating to the effect of termination, the Termination Fee, and the miscellaneous provisions in Article 11 thereof—will survive any termination of the Merger Agreement.

 

129

 

 

Termination Fees and Other Fees

 

The Merger Agreement requires Iridium to pay Rocket Lab the Termination Fee if the Merger Agreement is terminated in specified circumstances. The Termination Fee is payable if:

 

·Iridium terminates the Merger Agreement to enter into a definitive agreement providing for a Superior Proposal in accordance with the terms of the Merger Agreement (in which case the Termination Fee is payable immediately before, and as a condition to, such termination); or

 

·Rocket Lab terminates the Merger Agreement because, prior to receipt of the Iridium Stockholder Approval, an Adverse Recommendation Change has occurred or Iridium has committed an Intentional Breach of its non-solicitation (no-shop) and related obligations under the Merger Agreement in any material respect (in which case the Termination Fee is payable within two business days after termination).

 

In addition, Iridium must pay Rocket Lab the Termination Fee if an Acquisition Proposal Termination Scenario occurs:

 

·the Merger Agreement is terminated: (i) by either party pursuant to Section 10.01(b)(i) of the Merger Agreement because the Mergers have not been completed by the End Date, (ii) by either party pursuant to Section 10.01(b)(iii) of the Merger Agreement because the Iridium Stockholder Approval was not obtained at the special meeting, or (iii) by Rocket Lab pursuant to Section 10.01(c)(i) of the Merger Agreement as a result of an Intentional Breach by Iridium giving rise to a failure of the related closing condition;

 

·after the date of the Merger Agreement and prior to the applicable termination (or, in the case of a termination for failure to obtain the Iridium Stockholder Approval, prior to the special meeting), a bona fide Acquisition Proposal was made to Iridium or publicly disclosed; and

 

·within 12 months after such termination, Iridium consummates, or enters into a definitive agreement providing for, any Acquisition Proposal.

 

In an Acquisition Proposal Termination Scenario, the Termination Fee is payable concurrently with the consummation of such Acquisition Proposal or the earlier execution of such definitive agreement. For purposes of this “tail” provision, each reference to “25%” in the definition of Acquisition Proposal is instead treated as a reference to “50%.”

 

The Termination Fee of $223,620,000 represents approximately 3.75% of the equity value of Iridium implied by the transaction (based on the value of the Merger Consideration and the fully diluted number of shares of Iridium Common Stock outstanding, each calculated by the parties as of June 26, 2026, the last full trading day prior to the execution of the Merger Agreement). In no event will Iridium be required to pay the Termination Fee on more than one occasion.

 

The Merger Agreement characterizes the Termination Fee as liquidated damages, and not a penalty, representing a reasonable estimate of the losses that would be suffered by reason of the applicable termination. Except in the case of fraud or an Intentional Breach of the Merger Agreement by Iridium, if the Termination Fee becomes payable and is paid in full, the receipt of the Termination Fee will be Rocket Lab’s, Merger Sub I’s and Merger Sub II’s sole and exclusive remedy against Iridium, its subsidiaries and their respective directors, officers, employees, stockholders, affiliates and representatives in connection with the Merger Agreement and the transactions contemplated by it. However, nothing in the foregoing will limit a party’s rights as described below in “—Specific Performance”.

 

The Merger Agreement does not provide for any reverse termination fee payable by Rocket Lab to Iridium under any circumstances, and does not provide for the reimbursement of either party’s expenses upon termination. For a description of the allocation of fees and expenses generally, see “—Expenses” below.

 

Expenses

 

Except as otherwise expressly provided in the Merger Agreement (including with respect to the Termination Fee), all costs and expenses incurred in connection with the Merger Agreement and the transactions contemplated by it will be paid by the party incurring such cost or expense, whether or not the Mergers are completed.

 

130

 

 

Amendment or Supplement; Extension of Time; Waiver

 

Any provision of the Merger Agreement may be amended or waived prior to the First Effective Time if, and only if, such amendment or waiver is in writing and signed, in the case of an amendment, by each party to the Merger Agreement, and, in the case of a waiver, by each party against whom the waiver is to be effective. However, after the Iridium Stockholder Approval has been obtained, there may be no amendment or waiver that would, under the DGCL, require the further approval of Iridium’s stockholders without such approval first having been obtained. No failure or delay by any party in exercising any right or privilege under the Merger Agreement will operate as a waiver of that right or privilege. Additionally, no single or partial exercise of a right or privilege will preclude any other or further exercise of any other right or privilege. Such rights and remedies provided in the Merger Agreement shall be cumulative and not exclusive of any rights or remedies provided by applicable law.

 

No Third-Party Beneficiary

 

The Merger Agreement is binding upon and inures to the benefit of the parties and their respective successors and permitted assigns, and no provision of the Merger Agreement is intended to confer any rights, benefits, remedies, obligations or liabilities on any person other than the parties and their respective successors and permitted assigns, except for: (i) the indemnification, exculpation and insurance rights of Iridium’s current and former directors and officers as described under “The Mergers—Interests of Iridium Directors and Executive Officers in the Mergers”; (ii) the right of holders of Iridium Common Stock and Iridium Equity Awards to receive the Merger Consideration following the First Effective Time in accordance with the Merger Agreement; and (iii) the right of Iridium, on behalf of the holders of Iridium Common Stock and Iridium Equity Awards, to seek specific performance or, if specific performance is not granted, to recover damages (including damages based on the loss of the economic benefits of the transactions, such as any lost premium) in the event of fraud or an Intentional Breach by Rocket Lab, in each case as and to the extent provided in the Merger Agreement.

 

Applicable Law; Jurisdiction

 

The Merger Agreement, and any proceeding arising out of or relating to it, are governed by and to be construed in accordance with the laws of the State of Delaware, without regard to the conflicts of law rules of that state or other rules that would result in the application of the laws of a different jurisdiction.

 

The parties have agreed that any proceeding seeking to enforce any provision of, or based on any matter arising out of or in connection with, the Merger Agreement or the transactions contemplated by it will be brought exclusively in the Delaware Court of Chancery or, if that court does not have or declines jurisdiction, any federal court or other Delaware state court located in New Castle County, Delaware (and the appropriate appellate courts therefrom). Each party has irrevocably consented and submitted to the exclusive jurisdiction of those courts and has irrevocably waived, to the fullest extent permitted by applicable law, any objection to venue or any claim that a proceeding has been brought in an inconvenient forum. Special provisions govern proceedings involving certain Debt Financing sources. Process in any such proceeding may be served on any party anywhere in the world, whether within or without the jurisdiction of such court.

 

Each party to the Merger Agreement has irrevocably waived any and all right to a trial by jury in any proceeding arising out of or relating to the Merger Agreement or the transactions contemplated thereby.

 

Specific Performance

 

The parties have agreed that irreparable damage would occur if any provision of the Merger Agreement were not performed in accordance with its terms and that monetary damages, even if available, would not be an adequate remedy. Accordingly, the parties are entitled to an injunction, or any other appropriate form of equitable relief, to prevent or restrain breaches or threatened breaches of the Merger Agreement and to enforce specifically the performance of its terms and provisions, without any requirement to prove that irreparable damage would occur or that monetary damages would be inadequate, and without any requirement to secure or post a bond, in addition to any other remedy to which they are entitled at law or in equity.
